`AGENTS.md`:

```md
# Project direction

- This is a decompilation and reconstruction of Farming Simulator 15 / GIANTS Engine 6.
- Prioritize recovered scripts, original resources, native analysis and reuse of existing engine components where practical. Keep this direction when extending the project.
- Preserve original map geometry, transforms, scale and materials; identify temporary rendering approximations explicitly.
- Distinguish original native components, reconstructed behavior, third-party decoders and authored host code. Do not describe the full GIANTS engine as rebuilt before it is validated.
- Keep original executables, code snapshots, recovered game sources, mesh caches, textures and local packages out of Git. Requested rendered screenshots may be published.
- Keep GitHub documentation and the checkbox checklist in English. Explain progress to the user in French.
- See `docs/RECONSTRUCTION_STRATEGY.md`, `docs/ENGINE_BOOTSTRAP.md` and `PROJECT_CHECKLIST.md` for current scope and evidence.

```

`CONTRIBUTING.md`:

```md
# Contributing

Start with the [project checklist](PROJECT_CHECKLIST.md),
[reconstruction strategy](docs/RECONSTRUCTION_STRATEGY.md) and
[native recovery scope](docs/NATIVE_RECOVERY.md).

## What belongs in a contribution

- Authored reconstruction code, analysis tools and reproducible synthetic tests.
- Aggregate evidence: version/hash, function address, comparison count, result
  and the limits of what was exercised.
- Documentation that separates recovered scripts/resources, original native
  components, reconstructed behavior, external decoders and authored adapters.
- Rendered screenshots under `docs/screenshots/`, with the map, test scenario
  and temporary approximations identified.

Keep original map geometry, transforms, scale and materials as the reference.
Use recovered behavior and validated native interfaces when extending gameplay.
Do not describe pseudocode coverage or a passing fixture as full engine parity.

## Files that stay local

Do not attach or commit game executables, archives, code snapshots, raw native
exports, recovered game Lua, original models/textures/configurations, mesh
caches, user saves or playable packages containing those files. `inputs/`,
`recovered/`, `build/` and `logs/` are local-only. Downloaded dependency
checkouts also stay local. Share the tool invocation and aggregate results.

Public issue logs should contain only the relevant error and generic resource
names. Remove credentials and personal workstation/profile paths. User saves
and full memory dumps are not needed for a public bug report.

## Checks

Checks that use only repository code and synthetic fixtures:

```powershell
py -3 scripts/check_public_repo.py
py -3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py"
```

Use a full Git checkout for the publication check: it scans tracked files and
all reachable history, not just the latest commit. It checks known asset paths,
binary formats and common credential patterns; review provenance separately.

On Windows, install the documented LuaJIT toolchain before building:

```powershell
.\scripts\setup_lua_tools.ps1
.\scripts\build.ps1 -PythonExe 'C:\path\to\python.exe'
```

The complete local validation suite additionally needs prepared original
resources and pinned native references. Record which suites actually ran;
asset-free CI does not validate game recovery, original-engine parity or a
playable session. Do not upload local packages or inputs as CI artifacts.

## Pull requests

Explain the concrete behavior change, provenance, validation and remaining
limits. Keep GitHub documentation and checklist entries in English. Use small
changes that can be reviewed against their evidence. Preserve dependency
notices; do not add a blanket license over original or third-party material.
The current licensing status is documented in [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md).

```

`Launch FS15.cmd`:

```cmd
@echo off
if not exist "%~dp0build\FS15Launcher\FS15Reconstruction.exe" (
  echo Build the launcher first: scripts\build-launcher.ps1
  pause
  exit /b 1
)
start "" "%~dp0build\FS15Launcher\FS15Reconstruction.exe" --root "%~dp0."

```

```cmd
@echo off
setlocal
cd /d "%~dp0"
if not exist "build\ge6-objects-build\src\ge6_objects\Release\FS15GE6Objects.exe" (
    echo Build first with powershell -File scripts\build-ge6-objects.ps1
    pause
    exit /b 1
)
"build\ge6-objects-build\src\ge6_objects\Release\FS15GE6Objects.exe" --scene "build\ge6-objects\map01\scene.ge6scene" %*
if errorlevel 1 pause

```

`NOTICE.md`:

```md
# Project and dependency notices

This is an independent, unofficial research and reconstruction project.
Farming Simulator and GIANTS Engine names and original game content identify
the reference product; they do not imply endorsement by GIANTS Software.

## Repository scope

The public repository contains authored tools/host code, reconstructed
components, documentation, aggregate validation and selected rendered captures.
Original executables, archives, game scripts/resources, memory/code snapshots,
raw native pseudocode and local playable packages are not distributed here.
Screenshots illustrate local results using original reference resources and
are not a license to reuse the game's assets.

No project-wide license has been selected for the authored repository code.
Public visibility does not place the code, original game content or dependency
code under MIT or another blanket license. Existing third-party notices apply
to their respective material and are preserved separately.

## Dependencies

| Dependency | Use | License / notice location |
|---|---|---|
| [LuaJIT](https://github.com/LuaJIT/LuaJIT) | Locally built static Lua runtime | Upstream `COPYRIGHT` (MIT); copied into local runtime packages |
| [LJD fork](https://github.com/Dr-MTN/luajit-decompiler) | Local script recovery tool, invoked by the project adapter | Upstream `LICENSE` (GPL-3.0) and `LICENSE-upstream` (MIT), retained in its local checkout |
| [I3DShapesTool](https://github.com/Donkie/I3DShapesTool) | Local mesh decoder build with an authored stream adapter | MIT; notice retained in [licenses/I3DShapesTool-LICENSE.txt](licenses/I3DShapesTool-LICENSE.txt) |
| [Ghidra](https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra) | Local native analysis/export tool | Upstream Apache-2.0 license and bundled third-party notices |
| [SDL2](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/tree/release-2.30.0) | Window/context/input transport for the GE6 object preview; Linux frontend transport | zlib; official VC archive `COPYING.txt` is copied beside the locally built Windows object executable |
| [Pillow](https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow) / [NumPy](https://github.com/numpy/numpy) | Local DDS/DEM object-preview staging tools | Upstream HPND/Pillow notices and BSD-3-Clause, respectively; installed separately, not vendored |
| [OpenSSL](https://openssl-library.org/) | SHA-256 verification of the private original image in the Linux native-code boot diagnostic | OpenSSL 3 Apache-2.0; the Linux workflow archive includes the distribution copyright notices |
| [OpenAL Soft 1.24.3](https://openal-soft.org/) | Linux audio middleware called by original GE6 instructions through authored ABI adapters | LGPL-2.0-or-later with upstream exceptions/per-file notices; complete unmodified source, license, static library and relink object/script accompany the boot artifact; see [audio dependency details](src/ge6_linux/AUDIO_DEPENDENCY.md) |
| [libpng](http://www.libpng.org/pub/png/libpng.html) / [zlib](https://zlib.net/) | Decode embedded original PNG icon frames in Linux PE resource transport | libpng and zlib licenses; distribution copyright notices accompany the Linux boot and host artifacts |

The setup scripts pin dependency revisions; see
[analysis/lua-toolchain.json](analysis/lua-toolchain.json) and
[scripts/setup_shapes_tools.ps1](scripts/setup_shapes_tools.ps1).
Downloaded dependency checkouts and builds are excluded from this repository.
The repository's `src/shape_bridge/` directory contains the authored adapter;
upstream decoder sources are resolved from the separate local checkout.

# Project progress checklist

or execution evidence. They do not represent a percentage of the full game.

**Exclusive active focus:** original GE6 startup on Linux. The

comparisons in an isolated profile. The hybrid mode activates three recovered
wheel helpers and records all three being called by GE6 on Westbridge Hills.
Most original global gameplay remains in use;

at their original hierarchical transforms, with a free camera.

`README.md`:

```md
# FS15 Reconstruction

Early-stage reverse engineering and component reconstruction of **Farming
Simulator 15 for Windows**, based on a locally installed copy of version
**1.4.2.0**.

**Source and tooling repository:** original game files, recovered game sources,
raw decompiler exports and playable asset packages are kept local. Reproducing
the game-resource results requires your own FS15 1.4.2.0 installation. The
repository does not provide a ready-to-download copy of the game.

[Progress checklist](PROJECT_CHECKLIST.md) · [Build instructions](#build) ·
[Linux tester guide](docs/LINUX_TESTER.md) ·
[Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [Project and dependency notices](NOTICE.md)

**Exclusive active focus: original GE6 startup on Linux.** The new
[native-instruction launch path](docs/GE6_LINUX_NATIVE_BOOT.md) preserves original
x64 engine code and works on missing OS dependencies. ReFarm and the object
preview remain fixtures. Complete original-engine Linux boot is not yet validated.

The private reference image executes its CRT/global initialization and reaches
its original application entry inside a local Linux VM without Wine/Proton or
instruction patches; it stops at the unbound Steam restart API. The separately
pinned, existing **Local GE6** image now proceeds through original profile/XML
loading into central engine initialization. It writes its own startup journal,
reads actual Linux CPU/memory information and reserves/commits memory for its
original embedded Lua allocator. Original workers now execute on Linux
threads with separate stacks and TLS/FLS state. With unchanged integrity inputs
and GAR archives staged privately, startup reaches the original physics/input
log sections and initializes OpenAL audio through Linux OpenAL Soft (512 sources
in the isolated VM). The VM uses an explicit silent backend; audible gameplay
is unverified. Original SDL/CRT console-handler registration, optional icon
lookup, class registration and dynamic USER32 export probes now continue.

**The original FS15 loading screen now renders at 1280 x 720 on Linux.**
GE6 opens its original shader archive, builds shader programs, uploads textures
and buffers, issues draw calls and swaps its main-window buffers through typed
Microsoft-ABI bindings to GLX/Mesa llvmpipe. Its own journal reports successful
OpenGL initialization and loading of the game vehicle types. This is actual
original-code execution, separate from ReFarm and the recovered frontend host.
The image retains its previous Windows platform-bootstrap modification; the
Linux loader adds no instruction patches. Menu interaction, a loaded 3D world,
complete renderer parity and playable simulation remain unverified.
An original FOCUS introduction frame is also visible; the 90-second VM test
then ends with a presentation wait before the menu.
See [the loading-screen milestone and remaining boundary](docs/GE6_LINUX_NATIVE_BOOT.md#first-original-loading-screen-2026-10-21)
and its [source-pinned evidence](analysis/ge6-linux-x11-validation.json).

![Original GE6 loading screen rendered in the Linux VM](docs/screenshots/ge6-linux-native-loading-2026-10-21.png)

**This is not a complete game rebuild. The recovered frontend and original
map scenes and an experimental gameplay subset run in a compiled native host;
the full engine and farming simulation remain incomplete.**

The project follows decompilation and reconstruction of the installed GIANTS
Engine 6 game. Original scripts, geometry, textures, scene transforms and native
routines are reused or examined where practical. See the
[reconstruction strategy](docs/RECONSTRUCTION_STRATEGY.md) for component provenance.

**Linux direction:** port the actual GE6/game code to run natively without
Proton, using the original Windows version as the behavior and resource
compatibility reference. Matching that version is the target, not a result
already achieved. The active Linux transport executes original GE6 instructions
through its first loading frames. The separate recovered frontend host remains
available; complete native startup, graphics/physics/audio parity, playable
worlds and persistent simulation saves remain open. Original-resource
menu/input validation on a Linux desktop is also pending.

**Runtime target: the actual GIANTS Engine 6.** The Direct3D alpha is an
experimental viewer/test host. On Windows, the native entry point has reached the
original menu and Bjornholm, with 104 recovered-source helper comparisons
passing inside GE6. See the [native runtime instructions](docs/NATIVE_ENGINE_RUNTIME.md).

**Launch:** build with `scripts/build-launcher.ps1`, then double-click
`Launch FS15.cmd`. The graphical launcher offers GE6 with recovered wheel
helpers, **ReFarm** (the experimental reconstructed engine), and an original-GE6 baseline. It remembers local
settings and keeps native saves under `build/native-engine/profile`.
The **Resources** page detects the local installation and prepares/repairs map,
texture, mesh, recovered-script and starting-fleet caches with progress and
cancellation. See [resource preparation and fresh-workspace requirements](docs/LAUNCHER.md).
See [launcher modes and requirements](docs/UNIFIED_LAUNCHER.md).
The existing `FS15MenuRebuilt.exe` / `FS15EngineRebuilt.exe` packages are the
separate experimental host; they are not the actual-engine entry point.

The launcher has a visual library layout: original-map scene previews, clickable
engine cards, a persistent launch-profile bar and a prominent PLAY button.
**ReFarm** names the authored experimental host; the original GE6 runtime remains
a separate option. Existing executable filenames and the `--mode home` alias are
kept compatible; `--mode refarm` is also supported.

**Experimental local GE6 startup:** choose **Local GE6 (experimental)** under
Settings & activity > Native startup. An isolated modified original runtime now
reaches the original menu and Bjornholm without loading a Steam library. Steam
was already open during the test; a fully closed-client launch and complete
save/reload sessions remain unvalidated. Steam services and licensed DLC are
unavailable. See [preparation, evidence and scope](docs/LOCAL_ENGINE_RUNTIME.md).

## Current results

- **Original objects through recovered GE6 drawing:** a separate SDL/OpenGL
  integration target now displays original buildings, trees, roads and props
  using recovered GE6 transforms, projection/frustum, buffers and indexed draw.
  Bjornholm was captured on Windows/NVIDIA with original textures and DEM geometry.
  Materials, lighting, terrain color and LOD policy are temporary; gameplay is
  not connected. Double-click `Launch GE6 Objects.cmd` after building.
  See [capture, build/run instructions and limits](docs/GE6_OBJECT_RENDERING.md).

- **Connected physics results and scene/view preparation:** worker completion
  now runs recovered contact collection, native post-step order, wheel readback
  and enter/leave/stay events. The CPU probe connects 16 finalized steps to
  scene TRS, Camera/frustum/visibility and 17 shader-block uploads. Six more
  native entries have differential evidence. Backend samples and scene binding
  are authored fixtures; actual scene creation, solver and GPU rendering remain
  open. See [integration and limits](docs/PHYSICS_POST_STEP_RECOVERY.md).

- **Native physics scheduling:** the recovered dispatcher, synchronous step and
  worker loop now run over an authored real thread/auto-reset event transport.
  Comparisons cover 3,072 dispatch states, 1,024 synchronous states and 512
  worker lifetimes / 2,044 completed steps. The portable startup probe performs
  16 worker-thread force queries and joins cleanly. Full physics scene creation,
  solver, controller finalizers and GPU startup remain open. See
  [physics dispatch scope](docs/PHYSICS_DISPATCH_RECOVERY.md).

- **Native startup, 3D and physics:** recovered render-view creation/destruction
  now initializes state and requests/releases two buffers through explicit
  driver services. A recovered wheel-force adapter connects the native wheel
  registry, tangent and tire math to script results. Comparisons cover 1,024
  view lifetimes and 4,096 force frames. Both paths run in the portable CPU
  probe; real GPU and physics-world startup remain open. See
  [implementation and evidence](docs/STARTUP_3D_PHYSICS.md).

- **Native recompilation:** 30 uncovered binding targets
  were identified as functions and decompiled. The enlarged catalogue has
  **11,667 eligible exports**, after five scene-vtable targets and six
  memory-stream targets and 25 additional eligible physics-table targets were
  found through explicit table audits. A separate
  portable C++ core now builds the RLE
  decoders, tire math, wheel lookup/read adapters, seven bit operations and the
  native affine point transform. Together with subsequent scene, animation,
  Camera and file-stream recovery, the ledger now records
  **260 native entries on bounded tested paths**. The affine component passes
  36,000 math comparisons, 5,999 complete node-arena comparisons and 4,799
  complete script-frame comparisons against original code, bit for bit.
  ReFarm uses the recovered local/world adapters through an authored matrix bridge.
  Full GE6 linking remains pending; the future
  Switch homebrew target is deferred. See [recompilation scope](docs/NATIVE_RECOMPILATION.md).
- **Scene state recovery:** five native paths now reproduce dirty/visibility,
  clip-distance/mask propagation, observer-presence tracking and base/TRS matrix

  This is a portable component; native allocators, complete object destruction and arbitrary

- **Scene hierarchy recovery:** ordered attachment, reparenting and removal now

- **GE6 physics backend:** native RTTI and factory analysis identify Bullet.
  A pinned 2014 upstream revision now supports recovered GIANTS world, dispatcher
  and solver hooks. **15,360 simulated frames** match original GE6 trajectories
  and contacts; **26,984 nonempty vehicle callback events** and 1,024 native
  sort fixtures match. This is actual rigid-body simulation, separate from
  ReFarm. Five wheel frame/filter/raycast/finish paths additionally match
  **6,656 native fixtures** with no observed arithmetic difference; actual
  middleware rays test owner/trigger exclusion and suspension limits. GIANTS
  terrain collision, the complete raycast vehicle constraint solver and full

- **GE6 suspension constraints:** three further paths recover the wheel Jacobian,
  spring setup and split-penetration phase. **2,048 Jacobian states, 2,048 spring
  states and 6,640 repeated correction iterations** match unchanged original
  code. An isolated integration fixture connects real world rays, recovered
  setup, solver iterations and actual chassis transform writeback. This
  isolates suspension correction; the assembled vehicle milestone follows below.
- **GE6 wheel velocity/friction:** the native `0x1401540b0` phase now applies
  suspension velocity impulses, tire-force limits and coupled wheel braking.
  **1,024 states / 6,640 successive iterations**, including 18,448 gravity
  queries, match unchanged original code with an empty differential network.
  A one-wheel integration fixture supports a chassis under gravity, transfers
  initial wheel spin into chassis motion, then brakes it to rest. Its fixed
  slip inputs and orchestration are authored test data. Original-vehicle loading
  remains open; motor/differential recovery follows below.
- **GE6 motor and vehicle assembly:** differential weight preparation and the
  complete motor/clutch/network update match **1,536 networks / 13,056 successive
  updates**. An experimental typed raycast-vehicle class connects all wheel
  phases and this drivetrain; four wheels accelerate from rest, reverse, steer
  and brake in component scenarios. The whole-class native comparison records
  unresolved motion/readback differences and is **not a parity pass**. Original
  vehicle XML/joints/script control, terrain/rendering and a playable Linux
  game remain open. See [measured limits](docs/GE6_PHYSICS_BACKEND.md).
- **OpenGL buffer recovery:** nine native paths now provide portable vertex/index
  storage, staging, direct mapping, discard, subdata upload and deletion.
  **1,024 paired lifetimes** match unchanged GE6 code through recording GL seams.
  The SDL/OpenGL check passes actual driver byte readback on Mesa in Linux CI;
  shaders, materials and scene drawing remain open. See
  [scope and build commands](docs/GL_BUFFER_RECOVERY.md).
- **GE6 OpenGL draw dispatch:** native array/index/range dispatch and point-size
  caching match **4,096 states / 3,853 ordered GL calls**, including original
  32-bit index-byte/range wrapping. The actual-driver check now adds primitive
  framebuffer readback; scene shaders, materials and complete draw submission
  remain open. See [scope](docs/GL_DRAW_RECOVERY.md).
- **Portability audit:** the current static catalogue has 31,396 known call
  edges. Its scripting roots reach 2,878 eligible functions, including 939 with
  computed calls. Those targets and concrete types still need recovery before
  full linking. All thirty-eight asset-free component/transport tests pass on
  Windows x64, Linux x64 and ARM64 Linux under QEMU, separately from the future
  Switch target. See
  [current connected-chain platform evidence](analysis/physics-post-validation.json),
  [current OpenGL/platform evidence](analysis/gl-buffers-validation.json),
  [Linux CI run](https://github.com/nat649/fs15-reconstruction/actions/runs/39226238887) and
  [porting blockers](docs/PORTABILITY_STATUS.md).
- **Actual GE6 execution:** the installed original engine initializes its OpenGL
  renderer and physics 5.9.4, opens its frontend and loads Bjornholm in a separate
  profile. The recovered WheelsUtil source executes through the native mod
  loader and passes all 104 helper comparisons. The hybrid mode now activates
  three recovered wheel helpers, with all three called by actual GE6 vehicles
  on Westbridge Hills. Most gameplay remains original; full recovered-game
  replacement is pending. Direct startup of this Steam copy still fails; the
  launcher retains normal Steam startup and an explicit direct mode.
  See the [bounded log evidence](analysis/native-engine-validation.json).
- **Native decompilation coverage:** a full pass through the existing Ghidra
  catalogue exported **11,667 / 11,667 eligible functions** as local pseudocode,
  with no remaining export failures. The last two exports were unblocked with
  larger response capacity and C-only output; 565 thunks or external entries
  are excluded. **498 explicit native scripting API
  descriptors** now guide wheel/physics interface recovery. This is analysis
  coverage, not a recompilable full engine. See [native recovery](docs/NATIVE_RECOVERY.md).
- **Recovered vehicle animations:** original `AnimatedVehicle` and `Trailer`
  loading/update logic now animate doors, trailer bodies and pipes. Tipping waits
  for original discharge timing and automatically closes when empty. Recovered
  source and original bytecode produce identical traces in **777 fixture samples**.
- **Reconstructed tire-force math:** native routine `0x1400c24c0` is now compiled
  from reconstructed C++, with **3,300 native comparisons / 13,200 float outputs**.
  It remains a standalone validated component; contacts, suspension and its
  integration into playable physics are still pending.
- **Experimental gameplay:** original starting fleets, selectable/drivable
  tractors and combine, animated wheels, compatible implement attachment,
  original field/crop data, cutting/cultivation/sowing, silo filling, tipping
  stations, combine-to-trailer transfer and seed refilling now have a running
  native/Lua bridge. Physics, density services and client rendering remain
  partial. No persistent session saves yet. See [gameplay scope and controls](docs/GAMEPLAY_RUNTIME.md).
- **Original density recovery:** the reconstructed 16-bit RLE leaf matches
  original GE6 in **107 comparisons / 35,133,356 values**, including both
  4096-square fruit maps. Crop block meshes and density states are reused.

- **Rebuilt frontend executable:** opens the recovered `MainScreen` in a
  Windows window without starting the original game executable or Steam.
  Runs 36 recovered Lua sources with authored XML, rendering, input and
  read-only save services. Career displays twenty slots and existing save
  metadata; empty slots lead to three difficulty choices and two base-map
  previews. Credits/Back and Quit work. Start launches the new terrain engine
  for an empty-slot selection; existing saved simulations cannot be loaded yet.
- **Original map scene reconstruction:** the Direct3D 11 host renders both
  original terrains, buildings, trees, roads and props. Local `.i3d.shapes`
  decoding recovers **1,155 / 833 meshes**, instanced through the original scene
  hierarchy. Original diffuse textures and **8 / 6 terrain weight layers** are
  loaded at their I3D repeat sizes. The camera starts at the original saved I3D
  viewpoint. Shaders are simplified; mission simulation and physics remain
  incomplete. See [engine notes](docs/ENGINE_BOOTSTRAP.md).
- **Native GE6 mesh-cipher validation:** **128 comparisons / 74,848 bytes**
  against the isolated original routine, including partial blocks and counter carry.
- **Recovered environment/shaders:** the original sky dome/textures, sampled
  Lua environment curves and five original shader injection bodies now run in
  the host. Flags and bushes animate, the hour changes sky/light/fog, and a local
  shadow map casts building/vegetation shadows. Dedicated CTest suites cover this,
  including fixed-image motion/night/shadow comparisons. Full GIANTS cascades
  and mission weather remain incomplete. See [environment notes](docs/ENVIRONMENT_RUNTIME.md).
- **Reconstructed C++ launcher:** reads the game's startup XML, chooses the
  x86 or x64 executable, and forwards command-line arguments. It still runs
  the original installed game engine.
- **Reconstructed engine routine:** an RLE8 decoder that writes packed bit
  values. Compiled and compared with the original native routine in
  **266 cases covering 853,086 decoded values**, including 64 KiB memory
  segment boundaries.
- **Analysis tools:** installation inventory, PE metadata and strings,
  a code-section snapshot tool, and reproducible Ghidra exports.
- **Native catalogue:** 12,207 functions catalogued after binding-target, scene-vtable and memory-stream discovery. The full export supersedes
  the earlier overlapping targeted selections, which remain local references.
- **Lua interface mapping:** 112 observed name/implementation/wrapper
  associations from one registration routine.
- **GAR extraction:** 1,121 local files recovered from `dataS.gar` and
  `dataS2.gar`, including all 470 LuaJIT chunks found in these archives.
- **Lua recovery and rebuild:** all 470 recovered Lua sources compile.
  **308** reproduce the original deterministic stripped bytecode exactly; **162** pass
  syntax checks but still need behavioral validation. A local rebuilt
  script package is generated without replacing installed game files.

Function counts include runtime and third-party library code. They are not
a measure of game reconstruction completeness. See [the project status](analysis/STATUS.md)
for evidence, limitations, and the next targets.

Track completed work and remaining milestones in the
[project checklist](PROJECT_CHECKLIST.md).

| `scripts/stage_environment.lua` | Execute recovered environment curve initialization and AnimCurve locally |

| `tools/bootstrap_ghidra.py` | Download and verify a pinned official Ghidra release |

Original game executables, archives, assets, SDK files, memory snapshots,
raw decompiler exports, and downloaded tools are **not included**. Generate
them locally from your own installation. This repository contains authored
source, analysis tools, documentation, and selected validation metadata.

## Build

Requirements: 64-bit Windows, CMake, and Visual Studio with the C++ desktop
workload and a Windows SDK. Development was validated with MSVC 19.51 and
Windows SDK 10.0.26100. The C++ runtime is linked statically. The engine and
frontend require the pinned LuaJIT static library; prepare it before building.

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/nat649/fs15-reconstruction.git
cd fs15-reconstruction
.\scripts\setup_lua_tools.ps1
.\scripts\build.ps1
.\FS15LauncherRebuilt.exe --self-test
.\FS15LauncherRebuilt.exe --dry-run --game-dir 'D:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Farming Simulator 15'
```

CMake uses its default Visual Studio generator. Select another explicitly:

```powershell
.\scripts\build.ps1 -Generator 'Visual Studio 17 2022'
```

The build produces `FS15LauncherRebuilt.exe`, `FS15Core.dll`,
`FS15EngineRebuilt.exe` and the frontend, and runs the locally available CTest suites.
The launcher has nine behavioral checks. If the local native RLE reference
exists, the build also requires Python 3.11+ and runs the differential tests.
Pass `-PythonExe 'C:\path\to\python.exe'` to select the interpreter.

GitHub's **Repository checks** workflow uses only authored synthetic fixtures
and publication guards, with no game assets or native reference image. Its
result is separate from the eighteen-suite local game/native validation.
See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for asset-free checks and submission rules.

To start the installed game through this launcher, remove `--dry-run`.
Keep Steam available. This uses the **original game executable**. Set the
installation path with `--game-dir` or `FS15_GAME_DIR`; otherwise it defaults
to Steam's usual installation directory on C:.

### Launch the reconstructed frontend

After script/asset recovery below, run:

```powershell
.\scripts\setup_lua_tools.ps1
.\scripts\package-menu.ps1 -GameDir $env:FS15_GAME_DIR -PrepareOnly
.\scripts\setup_shapes_tools.ps1
& 'C:\path\to\python.exe' scripts\prepare_scene.py --game-dir $env:FS15_GAME_DIR
& 'C:\path\to\python.exe' scripts\prepare_mission.py --game-dir $env:FS15_GAME_DIR
.\scripts\build.ps1 -PythonExe 'C:\path\to\python.exe'
.\scripts\package-menu.ps1 -GameDir $env:FS15_GAME_DIR
.\build\FS15GameplayAlpha4\FS15MenuRebuilt.exe
```

The mesh preparation tools require Git and the .NET 10 SDK with the ASP.NET
reference pack; the packaged native runtime does not require .NET.
Preparation copies original files and stages geometry locally before the
build's menu/gameplay tests run. The engine's recovered gameplay bridge and the
frontend require the pinned local LuaJIT static library.

The local folder contains both executables, bootstrap, recovered Lua sources,
assets and LuaJIT copyright notice. A ZIP is generated at
`build/FS15MenuRebuilt-local.zip`. Both stay excluded from GitHub. Keep the
folder together; the executable finds resources beside itself regardless of
the working directory. No original game executable, runtime code snapshot,
archive cipher oracle or Steam process is required **to run this frontend and terrain engine**.

Mouse, wheel and arrow/Enter input use the recovered GUI's hit testing, focus
and callbacks. Career shows twenty slots, existing money/duration/map/date
metadata, and explicit unavailable labels for unsupported metadata. Save
files are read only; Delete is disabled. An empty slot opens the recovered
Difficulty and Map Selection screens. Start opens a new experimental session
with original map/fleet/crop data and partial native gameplay services. It creates
no persistent save.
Credits/Back and Quit also work.
Use WASD/ZQSD or arrows to drive, Space to brake, Tab to change vehicle, E to
attach, B to work, R to fill, I to tip and O for the combine pipe. Mouse drag/wheel
orbit/zoom the camera. P pauses/resumes; losing focus or minimizing also pauses
and clears pending input. F8 opens the earlier free camera. See the
[gameplay notes](docs/GAMEPLAY_RUNTIME.md) for limitations and test scenarios.
F5/F6 step the preview hour; F7 toggles local shadows.

Gameplay uses fixed 60 Hz host updates independently of rendering. Both maps
pass original-bytecode/recovered-source comparisons and timing/pause checks
in 24 native runs. See [reliability scope and evidence](docs/GAMEPLAY_RUNTIME.md#timing-pause-and-original-script-comparisons).

Interactive runs read the local Windows Documents/My Games/FarmingSimulator2015
profile. Override it with `--save-dir PATH`, or use `--empty-saves` for empty
slots. Smoke tests default to empty slots and inject authored metadata only
for deterministic input checks. Preview a screen explicitly:

```powershell
.\build\FS15GameplayAlpha4\FS15MenuRebuilt.exe --empty-saves --screen MapSelectionScreen
```

Other screens report their requested destination. The full `main.lua` startup, complete game worlds,
native physics parity, networking, audio and multiplayer remain unfinished.
See [menu reconstruction notes](docs/MENU_RUNTIME.md).

## Reproduce the local analysis

Requirements: Python 3.11+, JDK 21, and a local FS15 1.4.2.0 installation.
The Python tools use the standard library. Configure your own paths:

```powershell
$env:FS15_GAME_DIR = 'D:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Farming Simulator 15'
$env:JAVA_HOME = 'C:\path\to\jdk-21'

py -3 scripts\inventory.py
py -3 tools\bootstrap_ghidra.py
.\scripts\analyze.ps1 -Target launcher -Limit -1

# Start the installed game normally through Steam and capture its code section.
py -3 scripts\runtime_snapshot.py --launch-game --via-steam
.\scripts\analyze.ps1 -Target game-runtime -Limit 250 -TimeoutSeconds 300

# Export from the existing project without re-running analysis.
.\scripts\analyze.ps1 -Target game-runtime -Existing -ExportName game-focus -Limit 80 -Addresses '140011a30','1400149d0','14001ea90','14002b8c0','140096580','140098630','14028f430','14028f770'
.\scripts\analyze.ps1 -Target game-runtime -Existing -ExportName native-leaf -LeafReference '14028f430'
Copy-Item inputs\reference\rle8-reference.json analysis\rle8-reference.json
Copy-Item inputs\reference\rle8-reference.asm analysis\rle8-reference.asm
py -3 scripts\map_bindings.py
py -3 scripts\verify_workspace.py
```

Pass `--game PATH` to the inventory or snapshot tool to override the game
directory, `--steam PATH` for a different Steam executable, and `-JavaHome PATH`
to the analysis runner to override `JAVA_HOME`.

The bootstrap downloads [Ghidra 11.4.2 from the official release](https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra/releases/tag/Ghidra_11.4.2_build)
and checks the published SHA-256 before extraction:

```text
795a02076af16257bd6f3f4736c4fc152ce9ff1f95df35cd47e2adc086e037a6
```

The scripts do not overwrite installed game binaries. Starting the game
normally can update its usual user profile. The snapshot copies only `.text`
into a local analysis image, not the heap, writable state, or other modules.
That image is an analysis input, **not a rebuilt executable**.

Ghidra `.c` files are pseudocode with inferred types and generated names;
they are not original source files and do not compile directly. Preserve
binary hashes, addresses, and raw exports separately from each reconstructed
implementation. Local inputs and generated reports are excluded by `.gitignore`.

## Recover and rebuild the script layer

After creating the verified native image above, place local copies of
`dataS.gar` and `dataS2.gar` in `inputs/archives/`. Then run:

```powershell
py -3 scripts\extract_gar.py inputs\archives\dataS.gar --decode-luajit --validate-xml
py -3 scripts\extract_gar.py inputs\archives\dataS2.gar --decode-luajit --validate-xml
py -3 scripts\verify_recovered_files.py
.\scripts\setup_lua_tools.ps1
py -3 scripts\recover_lua.py
py -3 scripts\compile_recovered_lua.py
```

The tool setup uses pinned revisions of [LuaJIT](https://github.com/LuaJIT/LuaJIT)
and [LJD](https://github.com/Dr-MTN/luajit-decompiler), retained locally with
their upstream licenses. LuaJIT is built for Windows x64 with `nogc64 static`
to match the observed chunk architecture. See `analysis/lua-toolchain.json`.
The authored adapter `scripts/ljd_driver.py` fixes repeated literal AST nodes
and preserves empty-table allocation before subsequent field assignments,
without modifying the third-party checkout. Authored regression fixtures
check evaluation order and round trip to identical bytecode. The table fix
adds 54 exact matches with no loss of the previous 254.

Outputs remain local:

- `recovered/gar/`: extracted assets and original compiled scripts.
- `recovered/luajit/`: normalized chunks; all 470 observed chunks already
  used the standard version-2 header and required no transformation.
- `recovered/lua/dataS/`: recovered, compilable Lua source.
- `build/recompiled/dataS/`: recompiled chunks with portable source names.
- `build/FS15ScriptsRebuilt.zip`: 470 rebuilt chunks and validation metadata.

**The GAR cipher has not been independently reconstructed.** Extraction
currently calls two routines from the exact hash-pinned original code image
inside the extraction process. Header/index parsing, bounds/path checks, and
the extraction pipeline are reconstructed code. See [GAR notes](docs/GAR.md).

Lua validation loads/compiles chunks without executing their top-level game
code. `exact_match` compares deterministic `string.dump(chunk, "sd")` from the
original and rebuilt chunks. This sorts template-table hash entries while
retaining all instructions, constants, prototype order and upvalue metadata.
`syntax_only` proves compilation, not equivalence.
The package is a rebuilt script layer, not a rebuilt native engine or a
playable standalone game. See [Lua recovery notes](docs/LUA_RECOVERY.md).

## Next work

Investigate the 162 Lua round-trip differences, reconstruct the GAR cipher
without original-code execution, and continue documenting the Lua/native
interfaces, original physics/component joints, complete farming behavior and
persistent sessions. The current native gameplay bridge is documented above.

The RLE routine does not implement the complete GRLE file format, physics,
rendering, or game simulation. Recovered game assets and Lua sources are
excluded from Git; the repository publishes tools and selected metadata.

startup of the tested Steam copy exits with code 53; normal Steam startup works.
This combines launch configuration and bounded recovered logic, with separate
native renderer/physics processes. See [native evidence](native-engine-validation.json)
and [launcher evidence](unified-launcher-validation.json).

The launcher now has Play, Resources and Diagnostics pages. It detects local
Steam libraries and prepares/repairs original terrain, mesh, texture, script and
starting-fleet resources through the existing tools, with progress/cancellation.
The real GUI worker completed local preparation and recorded 1,609 file hashes;
fresh archive extraction still requires the pinned original native GAR oracle.
See [preparation instructions](../docs/LAUNCHER.md). Latest validation passes all
the earlier 24 Windows CTest checks. Latest component and Python checks are
listed above; directory-symlink checks require extra local Windows privileges.

The new [gameplay alpha](../docs/GAMEPLAY_RUNTIME.md) loads original starting
fleets and field/crop data, executes recovered motor/wheel and farm-transfer
rules, and supports basic cutting/cultivation/sowing through a partial native
bridge. Both maps pass 43 gameplay assertions. Recovered AnimatedVehicle and
Trailer loading/update now control original XML animations, discharge delay and
automatic closing. The source matches original bytecode in 777 fixture samples.
Both maps also render animated farm discharge with inventory conservation.
The host now uses fixed 60 Hz simulation updates, bounded stall recovery and
P/focus-loss pause with input clearing. In 24 native runs, both maps match
vehicle/crop/inventory state and captured images across 15/30/60/144 Hz frame
partitions and pause/resume. The same exercised paths match 28 original whole
Lua chunks loaded in a separate reference mode; source slices and authored
native services remain shared. See [reliability evidence](mission-reliability.json).
The RLE16 leaf matches original
code in 107 cases / 35,133,356 values, including both full fruit maps. Full
GE6/PhysX behavior, complete specialization startup and persistent saves remain
unfinished. Explicit harvest/silo scenarios relocate original equipment only
for reproducible trials; normal new-game placement uses original templates.

The native catalogue now has **11,635 verified local pseudocode exports** from
11,635 eligible functions, with zero remaining export failures in this catalogue.
Thirty uncovered entries were discovered from 32 explicit scripting code-label
references and then decompiled; four additional explicit scene-vtable targets
bring the catalogue to 12,200 functions.
Another 565 catalogue entries are thunks or external functions. There are also
498 explicit native scripting descriptors indexed separately from earlier Lua mappings.
The tire-force calculation at `0x1400c24c0` is reconstructed in C++ and matches
the original in **3,300 cases / 13,200 float outputs**. It is not yet integrated
with playable contacts/slip/rigid-body physics. See [native recovery](../docs/NATIVE_RECOVERY.md),
[export summary](native-export-summary.json) and [force validation](tire-forces-validation.json).

A newly compiled **FS15MenuRebuilt.exe** now launches a visible main menu
without starting the original game engine or Steam. It executes **36
recovered Lua sources** with authored XML/rendering/input/read-only save services,
including profiles, layouts, localization, textures
and the game's bitmap font. The native window was visually observed.

The frontend includes recovered Career, Difficulty and Map Selection screens.
Career displays twenty slots and reads existing metadata; mutations are
disabled. Empty slots lead through three difficulties and two base maps,
with Start launching the reconstructed original map scene for a new selection. Existing
saved simulations cannot load yet. Read failures,
unsupported maps and invalid numeric metadata cannot become new-game slots.

The smoke check renders 120 main-menu frames plus input-path screen captures,
exercises wheel scrolling to slot twenty, metadata display, new-game choices,
Back navigation, Credits and Quit. The package passes from a different working
directory with matching frontend PNGs. Source hashes are checked against the
recovery manifest. The build now has twenty-one CTest
suites when all local inputs/tools are present.

This is an independently implemented GUI host with a subset bootstrap.
Original `main.lua` and complete engine startup do not execute. The remaining
game screens, complete worlds, physics, audio and networking are unimplemented.
Career/Difficulty/Map selection, Credits/Back and Quit work; other destinations produce explicit progress
dialogs. See [menu notes](../docs/MENU_RUNTIME.md),
[validation](menu-validation.json) and the [checklist](../PROJECT_CHECKLIST.md).

| Component | Source | Validation | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| Launcher | `src/launcher/main.cpp` | Nine behavioral checks; dry run against the installed startup configuration | Starts the original game binary; not binary-identical source recovery |
| Frontend runtime | `src/menu/` | Native launch, recovered input paths, read-only metadata fixtures and portable package checks | Main/Career/Difficulty/Map Selection/Credits; new selections launch terrain exploration |
| Original map scene | `src/engine/`, `src/shape_bridge/` | Both original maps on hardware, authored WARP transformed-mesh fixture, separate terrain/object GPU samples and package parity | Original terrain, meshes, transforms and diffuse/weight textures; simplified shaders, no simulation |
| GE6 mesh cipher | `scripts/check_shapes_native.py` | 128 comparisons / 74,848 bytes with original native routine | Local isolated native oracle, not full engine integration |
| RLE8-to-bit-vector decoder | `src/core/rle8.cpp` | 266 comparisons with the original native function, covering 853,086 values | One engine routine with a documented valid-input domain |

The rendering host is authored code around recovered GIANTS resources and verified
format behavior, not recovered full GIANTS renderer source.
Both 1025-square original DEMs produce 2048-square-metre terrain meshes with
263,169 vertices and 524,288 triangles each. Strict version-3 `.shapes` decoding
recovers 1,155 / 833 triangle meshes. Original I3D transforms place 338,165 /
107,698 rendered shape instances, including individual leaf attachments.
Original diffuse textures and eight / six terrain layers are loaded. A 272-point
Bjornholm road/DEM check has 0.05 m median height difference (21.64 m for reversed Z).
See [engine scope](../docs/ENGINE_BOOTSTRAP.md)
and [engine validation](engine-validation.json).

The original sky dome/textures, Environment curve setup and AnimCurve evaluator
are now reused. Five original XML shader injections compile inside the native
host: sky depth/blending, wind, flags and two-sided foliage lighting. A local
2,048-square shadow map uses original sun settings and object shadow flags.
Fixed Map02 comparisons verify animation (17,978 changed pixels), night
brightness and visible shadows (212,089 changed pixels). Full GIANTS cascades,
skeletal trees, weather scheduling and mission simulation remain incomplete.
See [environment notes](../docs/ENVIRONMENT_RUNTIME.md) and
[validation](environment-validation.json).

The RLE reconstruction comes from **0x14028f430**, reached through references
to `src/base/util/RLEUtil.cpp`. Its descriptive name is inferred from code
and those references, not recovered from a debug symbol.

Differential tests execute the original function's **823 bytes** in the test
process and compare its outputs with recompiled C++. The Ghidra export checks
that the leaf has no external calls or memory references. The harness accepts
only the pinned SHA-256 reference; workspace verification also matches it to
the captured game code. No test code is injected into the running game.

Coverage includes 1–8-bit values, selected strides up to 16 bits, literals,
repeat-count extensions, prefilled outputs, and 64 KiB segment boundaries.
The reconstruction adds a checked output-capacity failure. Complete GRLE
files, the 16-bit input variant, arbitrary malformed engine inputs, and
gameplay are not validated yet.

Validation metadata: [reference](rle8-reference.json),
[differential results](rle8-validation.json). Instruction listings and native
reference bytes are generated locally and excluded from Git.

## Decompilation results

### Script layer recovery

The native `source` call chain and archive provider have now been traced.
Both local GAR archives have been extracted:

| Archive | Files | Relevant validation |
|---|---:|---|
| `dataS.gar` | 619 | 470 LuaJIT v2 chunks; 114 strict XML/I3D checks passed; seven original description XML files have missing attribute whitespace |
| `dataS2.gar` | 502 | 20 strict XML/I3D checks passed; asset headers and PNG CRCs checked |

All **1,121** extracted file sizes and hashes were rechecked against their
manifests. Independent checks passed for **374 DDS headers, 81 PNG CRC sets,
21 WAV headers, and 470 LuaJIT headers**. Seven strict XML diagnostics remain
recorded without changing the original extracted bytes.

The original native cipher is still used as a version-pinned oracle.
It is not a reconstructed, independent cipher implementation. The GAR
header/index parser and extraction checks are new code. The installed
game files were not replaced and no DLC path was used for this extraction.

All **470 Lua sources recompile** after authored adapters fix repeated literals
and prevent empty-table initialization from absorbing later stores. Comparison
against the original compiled chunks uses deterministic stripped dumps:

- **308 exact deterministic stripped-bytecode round trips**, 54 more than before.
- **162 syntax-only results**, with behavioral equivalence still unverified.
- **Zero remaining syntax failures** in this recovery pass.

All 254 earlier matches are retained under the deterministic check. The authored
table regression also verifies that a global table exists before a later field's
callback executes. Deterministic mode sorts template-table hash entries only;
it does not remove instructions, change constants or ignore control flow.

The rebuilt script package contains 470 recompiled chunks and a per-file
manifest. Chunks use portable game-relative names. The package was not
installed into the game, and game scripts were not executed by validation.
It is available locally at `build/FS15ScriptsRebuilt.zip`.

Public summaries: [recovery](lua-recovery-summary.json),
[script build](lua-build-summary.json), [file verification](recovered-files-verification.json).

The game selections overlap. Counts include C/C++ runtime and third-party

Automatic engine analysis completed within 300 seconds. The formerly failing
**0x1400f8420** and **0x1401f59a0** now export after increasing response capacity,
omitting unused syntax-tree output and using a 300-second function limit.
The full-export script preserves successful files and retries short Windows

diagnostics remain at `0x140457006` and `0x140457047`; exports and project
saving succeeded. The original PDB is unavailable. Raw pseudocode still
requires type recovery, naming, and reconstruction before compilation.

## Runtime code snapshot

On disk, the game's `.text` section has entropy close to 8 and cannot be
analysed directly as normal machine code. The installed game was started
normally through Steam, and only its loaded code section was copied into
a local PE analysis image.

- Captured code: **4,657,066 bytes**.
- Loaded code entropy: **6.5405**.
- Original x64 binary SHA-256:
  `21ce6fa0f776ad69f5a707a8c391cba6d2b80bdb612ffdf47f109372478b5488`.
- Analysis image SHA-256:
  `6d1beaf9d7e3c57dd51cec03385a53bda82b4ac946e622d8d2fa592a56d71f9f`.

Bytes outside the documented code range were verified unchanged. This partial
snapshot is an analysis input, not a runnable reconstruction or a complete
saved process state.

## Initial native function map

Virtual addresses use the x64 image's preferred base `0x140000000`.

| Address | Observation |
|---|---|
| `0x140011a30` | Lua registration routine; 112 observed name/implementation/wrapper associations indexed locally |
| `0x14000e200` | Native implementation registered as Lua `source`; traced into resource loading |
| `0x1400149d0` | Lua adapter associated with `source` |
| `0x14001ea90` | Reference to `dataS.gar` and initialization checks; full role undetermined |
| `0x14002b8c0` | Resource opening through a provider list under a critical section |
| `0x140096580`, `0x140098630` | Archive-related routines with an MD5 collision diagnostic; format unconfirmed |
| `0x14028e3d0` | Selects decoding variants for one- or two-byte input elements |
| `0x14028f430` | RLE8 decoder reconstructed and compared with the original |
| `0x14028f770` | Reconstructed RLE16; 107 differential comparisons, both original fruit maps included |
| `0x14027d5f0` | Archive factory; GAR is attempted before other formats |
| `0x1402a6d70` | GAR header/index loading and original cipher setup |
| `0x1402e6e60`, `0x1402e7500` | Original cipher initializer and buffer decoder used by the local oracle |
| `0x140280060` | Lua resource load; prefers `.luc` and handles the custom version-3 chunk transform |

Lua adapter signatures are partly inferred. Ghidra `undefined8` parameters
must not be treated as established source types.

## Remaining work

1. Investigate the 162 non-identical Lua round trips and validate behavior.
2. Reconstruct the GAR cipher independently and document native Lua interfaces.
3. Reconstruct RLE/GRLE variants and other isolated modules using differential
   comparisons with the original code.
4. Reconstruct engine startup, rendering, resources, audio, input, physics,
   and game behavior.
5. Validate a complete rebuilt executable through actual launches and play.

The recovered game scripts and assets remain local and excluded from Git.
Current validation establishes the analysis pipeline, launcher behavior,
one native routine, archive recovery, a recompiled Lua layer, a visible
recovered-menu launch and an authored native terrain-engine startup. It does
not establish full original engine or gameplay equivalence.

Known [CharacterSet/data/clip ownership](../docs/SHARED_SCENE_RECOVERY.md) now covers shared pose references, node rebinding,
update-list removal and nested clip destruction.
[Bounded animation evaluation](../docs/ANIMATION_RECOVERY.md) is now recovered
separately. Other resource classes, loading, scheduling, skinning, active
triggers and complete startup remain open.

# Recovered GE6 animation playback

Ten additional native entries are reconstructed as portable C++17. They extend
the recovered [CharacterSet ownership and binding](SHARED_SCENE_RECOVERY.md)
with key selection, compressed quaternion decoding, four-track playback and
pose application through known scene services. They do not establish a complete
animation loader, skeletal renderer or recovered GE6 executable.

| Native entry | Recovered behavior |
|---|---|
| `0x1400524b0` | Generate 512 reciprocal-square-root seeds and the special middle entry |
| `0x140174af0` | Four-component normalization using the generated seed and two double-precision refinement steps |
| `0x1402806f0` | Shortest-path normalized linear quaternion interpolation |
| `0x1401766d0` | Decode signed 16-bit XYZW keys, convert to WXYZ and interpolate the selected pair |
| `0x140176950` | Clamp/wrap clip time, use 64 lookup buckets, select adjacent/seam keys and apply per-component easing |
| `0x1401762a0` | Store a track time and detect pose changes using clamped old/new values |
| `0x140176330` | Store a blend weight and update the dirty byte |
| `0x140176370` | Assign a clip index, retain other track flags and mark changes |
| `0x1401763b0` | Case-sensitive name lookup with native inline/heap strings, returning the first match |
| `0x140175820` | Advance four tracks, sample active clips, blend translation/rotation/scale/visibility and apply node updates |

## Layout and retained behavior

CharacterSet contains four parallel arrays: flags at `+0x54`, clip indices at
`+0x64`, speeds at `+0x74`, times at `+0x84` and weights at `+0x94`. The update
entry receives the embedded `+0x38` observer in the original executable; the
portable API receives the containing record explicitly. Its enabled and dirty
bytes occupy `+0x50` and `+0x51`.

Clips have duration at `+0`, a native string at `+8` and channel pointers at
`+0x30`. A channel retains its flags, key vector, 64 unsigned-short lookup
entries, cached timing, three interpolation weights and two selected pointers.
Keys begin with time, flags and byte offsets for packed rotation and scale.
Translation is stored directly after the eight-byte key header. Packed rotation
stores signed XYZW components divided by 32767, then normalized as WXYZ.

The sampler retains the original exact-duration endpoint, negative-time wrap,
single-key behavior, repeated timestamps and the last-to-first looping seam.
Each component can use its own incoming/outgoing smooth interpolation flags.
Instruction inspection corrected the decompiler's floating-point grouping:
easing is `(3 - 2*w) * (w*w)`. Normalization also retains the observed float sum
order and double refinement grouping. The seed table is computed from the
recovered algorithm; original table bytes are not embedded.

Pose evaluation starts translation, scale and visibility from shared defaults.
Tracks add weighted translation/scale differences; quaternions accumulate with
hemisphere correction and are normalized before building their matrix basis.
Scale-only updates use the existing TRS scale cache, refreshing it when dirty.
A visibility channel chooses its first selected key only when track weight is
greater than 0.5. Matrix and visibility propagation use original origin zero.
If tracks share one clip, later sampling overwrites that clip's selections:
evaluation deliberately retains this native last-sample-wins behavior.

## Evidence

The [source-pinned original-code comparison](../analysis/animation-validation.json)
checks:

- All 512 generated seeds, 8,000 normalized quaternions and 8,000 nlerp outputs.
- 4,320 complete clip samples, comprising 42,444 complete channel records and
  compressed quaternion outputs.
- 1,680 clip-name lookups and 3,360 track-control records.
- 2,240 successive complete animation/scene arenas, including four active
  tracks, shared clip indices, reverse playback, negative/zero weights,
  disabled sets, visibility and scale-only cache refresh.
- 28,545 ordered observer notifications. Flags, opaque record bytes, selected
  keys and event origin/order are checked in addition to numeric results.

All compared float regions are bit-identical in the recorded Windows fixture.
The explicit numeric gate remains `8e-6` scaled error; this does not promise
universal bit identity across compilers or platforms. `sqrt` and `fmod` use the
platform library, while the original CRT implementations remain unrecovered.
Original routines execute only in an isolated pinned-image reference process.
No live game code is modified by these comparisons.

The asset-free `portable_animation` CTest independently checks loop endpoints,
easing flags, antipodal/zero quaternions, clamped dirty detection, pose/visibility
application, shared clips and invalid-input output preservation. Platform
results and their tested revision are recorded in the
[portable-core evidence](../analysis/portable-core-platform-validation.json).
All twenty-three asset-free core tests pass on Windows x64, Linux x64 and ARM64 Linux
under QEMU. Original-code differential execution remains Windows-only; these
checks do not validate a complete engine or Switch executable.

## Integration boundary and remaining work

`animation.h` exposes observed layouts and authored C interfaces. Callers own
valid decoded key storage, vectors and pointees; these APIs are not parsers for
untrusted animation files. Finite-value, capacity, index and track-count guards
are authored. Sampling stages its results before committing channel outputs.
Playback updates retain preceding mutations if a later host callback fails.

The host provides serialized TRS refresh, matrix setter and propagation
callbacks. The differential fixture delegates those to already recovered scene
arena services and uses side-effect-free observers. Arbitrary derived vtables,
callback reentrancy, concurrent scheduling and original exception/unwind paths
are outside this validation. Portable vtable values remain identity tokens.

The [binary animation resource path](ANIMATION_RESOURCE_RECOVERY.md) now builds
native-layout keys/clips/sets and reaches these playback services.
[XML callbacks](ANIMATION_XML_RECOVERY.md) also construct these resources.
Recover the original XML tokenizer/complete dispatch, file/archive/scene integration, scheduling, other resource
classes, skeleton/skin binding and renderer consumption next.
ReFarm still has its existing authored animation integration; this milestone
does not silently replace it or claim a complete GE6 or Switch build.

| Native entry | Recovered behavior |
|---|---|
| `0x1402805b0` | Build a WXYZ quaternion from radians using original Z/Y/X matrix rotations |
| `0x1401cb5c0` | Allocate and pack variable-size translation/quaternion/scale/visibility keys |
| `0x1401bd190` | Append strictly increasing, consistently controlled keys; retain rejected-key ownership |
| `0x1401bd2f0` | Generate the 64-entry acceleration lookup and time scale |
| `0x1401768b0` | Append a channel with native vector growth behavior |
| `0x1401751e0` | Combine channel control flags and register a clip in shared data |
| `0x1401ca840` | Parse the binary animation payload, build resources, resolve node IDs and bind CharacterSets |

The version/file wrapper is authored around the payload entry. It accepts the
observed big-endian version 2/3 headers; original file-opening routine
`0x1401995a0` is not counted as recovered. Node-ID resolution, allocation,
object registry/IDs, synchronization and result callbacks are authored transport
around the recovered algorithms. Portable vtable values are identity tokens.

## Format and construction behavior

The payload starts with a big-endian group count. Each group contains a counted
name padded to four bytes and its clips. Each clip contains a padded name,
float duration and channel count. Channels contain node ID, key count, then
time/control flags and optional three-float translation, rotation and scale.
Binary rotations are radians; the native inline XML path separately converts
degrees and remains unrecovered. The visibility state is carried in bit 15.
Counted temporary names pass through a C-string constructor, retaining the
original first-NUL behavior rather than silently storing embedded NUL tails.

Keys retain their native eight-byte header and variable-size payload. Packed
rotation stores signed 16-bit XYZW components with sign-dependent rounding of
`component * 32767`; it does not add a new clamp. Channel insertion rejects
equal/decreasing times and changes to the low four control bits. Those native
rejections leave the supplied key owned by the caller and report diagnostics.
The portable interface reports the same conditions without invoking a logger.

Lookup construction uses the key span, `span / 64` bucket spacing and
`64 / span` index scale. Empty/single-time channels only reset the first lookup
slot and scale; the remaining opaque slots are preserved. Empty serialized
channels are discarded by the payload reader. Each nonempty channel records
its first-encounter node ordinal in the newly named `node_index` field. Repeated
node IDs retain their ordinal; serialized channel ordering is preserved.

Clips and keys enter the recovered shared ownership chain. A later group that
binds the same nodes releases their old CharacterSet references and can delete
the earlier set/data/clip/key graph. This lifetime behavior is tested alongside
the final loaded records. Zero-node groups have no node references; their
explicit cleanup belongs to the host. Missing-node groups are skipped and
destroyed through the known lifetime paths.

## Original-code evidence

The [source-pinned report](../analysis/animation-resources-validation.json)
records:

- 4,000 Euler/quaternion comparisons and 4,000 complete packed-key allocations.
- 5,440 successive complete channel insertion/finalization records, including
  allocation capacity and preserved opaque lookup fields.
- 440 non-monotonic/mismatched-control diagnostics, with rejected-key cleanup
  performed separately by each fixture owner.
- 90 synthetic binary files plus one installed original resource, comparing
  final registries, complete surviving records, vector capacity, key payloads,
  default poses, bound node order and nested destruction.
- 637 resource-to-pose updates after loading, including negative/out-of-range
  looping seeks. All 10,437 compared node float regions match bit for bit in
  the recorded Windows run.

The real resource is `poettingerTop1252.i3d.anim`, SHA-256
`08aaf88f93f49775083624b141ca53e8c56464d6595dcf8adef13de120aa1b75`:
7,028 bytes, one group, one clip, 56 channels and 326 keys. All bytes are
consumed by both the independent fixture inventory and recovered reader. The
original payload reader and evaluator run in an isolated pinned-image process;
the installed game is not patched or launched. The original resource remains
local. Only aggregate evidence and reconstruction/tooling source are published.

Native temporary lookup trees and platform allocation internals are not claimed
as reconstructed by this reader. Their final graph effects are checked through
authored resolver/registry interfaces. Original-code fixtures use successfully
resolved TRS nodes; missing-node handling and allocation-failure guards are
checked separately by the asset-free test. Original CRT math remains a platform
library boundary; the numeric gate is `8e-6`, with recorded maximum error zero.

## Portable integration and guards

The `portable_animation_resources` test loads an authored binary fixture,
resolves its clip, seeks it, evaluates it and applies translation/visibility

All twenty-three asset-free core tests pass on Windows x64, Linux x64 and ARM64 Linux

Preflight count, string, finite-value, monotonicity and node-ordinal guards are
authored additions. Invalid/truncated inputs fail before engine allocation.
Allocation or host-service failures can retain earlier completed groups or a
partially bound group; the callback reports that boundary for caller cleanup.
Callbacks must be serialized, non-reentrant and must not throw. A borrowed
result can be invalidated by later rebinding unless the host retains a reference.

# Recovered XML animation callbacks

Nine additional native entries recover the GE6 decimal/vector readers and the
seven callbacks that construct animation sets, clips, channels and keys from
decoded I3D XML attributes. They feed the existing recovered ownership and
playback services. The original XML tokenizer, complete scene/file integration,
update scheduling, skinning and renderer startup remain open.

| Native entry | Recovered behavior |
|---|---|
| `0x140026e60` | Parse a scalar float and return the consumed input cursor |
| `0x140026850` | Split ASCII-space-delimited float vectors, retaining native token behavior |
| `0x140199890` | Start/replace a pending CharacterSet and reset its node-ordinal bookkeeping |
| `0x140199970` | Resolve accumulated node IDs, bind the set and transfer ownership |
| `0x140199d70` | Construct a named clip with its converted duration |
| `0x140199e90` | Register a completed clip in shared set data |
| `0x140199ec0` | Start a channel and update its source node ID when supplied |
| `0x140199fa0` | Finalize a nonempty channel, assign its first-encounter node ordinal and register it; destroy empty channels |
| `0x14019a100` | Decode key time/TRS/visibility/interpolation attributes, pack the key and attempt ordered insertion |

## Native parsing rules retained

The custom float reader rounds to binary32 after each digit. Integer and
fractional accumulation use their observed double intermediates; exponent
scaling repeatedly rounds a binary32 power-of-ten factor. It skips ASCII
spaces, accepts a leading minus and recognizes lowercase `e`, including an
exponent sign. Leading plus, tabs and uppercase `E` are not silently accepted
as conventional numeric syntax. The scalar API returns the original prefix
cursor and preserves signed zero and native nonfinite results.

Vector parsing splits at every ASCII space rather than collapsing whitespace.
For example, a three-value read of `1  2 3` yields `1, 2, 2`. The recovered
callback retains this behavior. Excessive exponent work, missing terminators,
short vectors and nonfinite animation payloads are rejected by authored guards.
Short vectors otherwise reach uninitialized native stack fields; that undefined
behavior is not fabricated or called in the original-code fixture.
Missing clip duration is rejected and absent names use an empty host string;
those guards do not validate native null-string/invalid-parameter paths.

Attributes use exact case-sensitive names and their first matching occurrence.
A key without a nonnull time is a native no-op. XML rotations convert degrees
using `(degrees / 180.0f) * pi_float` before the recovered Euler/quaternion and
packed-key routines; binary `.i3d.anim` rotations are already radians.

The six interpolation attributes retain independent incoming/outgoing flags:
`iptin/iptout`, `iprin/iprout`, `ipsin/ipsout`. Only exact lowercase `linear`
suppresses the corresponding smooth flag; absent or different values keep it.
Visibility defaults to true, even when the key does not control visibility.
When present, only a case-insensitive `false` makes visibility false; `0` remains
true. All of these choices are checked against original callback output bytes.

## Ownership and host transport

`animation_xml.h` supplies an authored opaque event context and bounded decoded
attribute views. XML tokenization and the scene node-ID map are host services.
The native callbacks' static CRT `atof`/`strtol` seams remain explicit duration
and node-ID conversion callbacks; their CRT implementations are not counted as
recovered. Channel/clip storage is shared with the binary resource component.
Final native-layout records, key buffers, capacities, flags, node order and
object-registry effects are compared; the opaque event context is not presented
as the original complete I3D loader object.

Completed sets are owned by node references. Zero-node results require explicit
host ownership/cleanup. Native rejection of a non-increasing key time or changed
control bits leaves the newly allocated key orphaned. The reconstructed XML
context retains those allocations until explicit context destruction; the
reference fixture reclaims its original orphans separately. This preserves
the observed boundary without describing native rejected-key retention as
ordinary channel-owned cleanup.

Failed allocation or binding can retain preceding mutations. Pending resources
are cleaned by context destruction; a partially bound set is handed back through
the result callback for node/host cleanup. Calls must be serialized and correctly
nested, and host callbacks must not throw or reenter. Arbitrary callback effects,
concurrent scheduling and original exception/unwind behavior remain separate.

## Evidence

The [source-pinned native comparison](../analysis/animation-xml-validation.json)
records:

- 12,015 scalar results/cursors and 6,000 complete vector output frames match
  the original machine code bit for bit, including native parsing quirks.
- 7,189 successive XML callback states and 93 completed groups across 60
  synthetic event streams and three original I3D files.
- Complete channel/key records are checked after each relevant callback, not
  only sampled positions or accepted-key counts.
- 179 rejected XML key allocations retain the observed orphan boundary and
  are explicitly reclaimed by their respective fixture owners.
- All 63 complete lifetimes finish with empty object registries and no owned
  resource/orphan allocations beyond the explicitly retained registry sentinel.

The original local files remain excluded from Git:

| Resource | Groups / clips | Channels | Keys |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `kroneSwadro2000.i3d` | 1 / 1 | 96 | 582 |
| `kuhnGA8521.i3d` | 1 / 1 | 28 | 170 |
| `poettingerTop1252.i3d` | 1 / 1 | 56 | 326 |

Their hashes and aggregate counts are in the evidence. This establishes
callback construction/binding on decoded original XML, not a recovered XML
tokenizer, a live rendered animation or a complete engine session.

Original callbacks run in a private process mapping with unchanged code bytes.
The oracle initializes a private CRT FLS slot/thread record and the pinned
C-locale views. Four additional inspected kernel imports are bound alongside
the existing five private-heap/critical-section seams. This avoids borrowing
captured per-thread pointers and does not claim recovered CRT initialization.
The installed game and its thread state are not modified.

`docs/BUFFERED_FILE_RECOVERY.md`:

```md
# GE6 buffered default-disk reader

Three more native callbacks are reconstructed in portable C++:

| Entry | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `0x1402e86b0` | Read through a 32 KiB buffer; refill through the default disk read method and stop after a short refill |
| `0x1402e8830` | Seek in the cached window or invalidate it and dispatch a disk seek |
| `0x1402e8930` | Report open/default-disk validity and the sticky refill-error state |

The original callback table initializer `0x1402e8960` references these routines.
The recovered code uses the earlier [disk-stream operations](FILE_STREAM_RECOVERY.md)
through explicit OS seams; arbitrary derived stream implementations are outside
this component. Original open/close allocation and write callbacks remain open.

## Preserved behavior

The native layout retains the disk-stream prefix, an inline 32 KiB buffer at
`+0x48`, cursor at `+0x8048`, fill count at `+0x804c`, logical position at
`+0x8050` and sticky error byte at `+0x8054`. The reconstructed API preserves
other bytes. Authored capacity/cursor guards reject malformed envelopes.

A cached seek window includes its first byte and excludes its end. An in-window
seek changes only cursor/logical position and performs no OS operation. A seek
to its end clears both cursor and fill before calling the disk seek method.
Offsets wrap as unsigned 32-bit values. Origin 1 computes current + offset;
origin 2 computes size **minus** offset. It is not POSIX's end + offset rule.

The original seek callback ignores the disk method's failure return, updates
its logical position on that path, and returns zero for recognized origins.
That result does not prove a successful disk movement. Invalid origin returns
`0xffffffff`. An unknown logical position (`0xffffffff`) follows the original
disk-tell branch instead of inventing a cached position.

A short refill stops the current read request after available bytes are copied.
Ordinary EOF does not set the sticky error. A refill error sets that error and
returns the already copied prefix. Seeking does not clear the sticky error;
later reads can still return bytes while status remains an error. These details
are retained for comparison with Windows, rather than normalized to a different
stream API.

## Integration and evidence

`FS15FileTransport::BufferedReadOnlyFile` supplies authored read-only OS ownership
and initializes the native-layout record. The bounded whole-file helper now
uses the recovered buffered reader. This connects it to frontend script,
DDS/font-metrics and Linux XML reads. Third-party image/XML decoding remains
separately identified; this does not establish native GE6 startup or full VFS
compatibility.

The [source-pinned differential evidence](../analysis/buffered-file-validation.json)
covers **2,163 operations across 35 sequences**: 726 reads, 763 seeks and 674
status calls. Complete records (including all cached bytes), guarded output
buffers and **1,680 ordered OS events** match the unchanged original callbacks
and default disk methods. This includes real Windows file I/O, nine fixture file
sizes around empty/32 KiB boundaries, unknown positions, unsigned offset wraps,
null/invalid streams, three explicitly injected refill-error sequences and one
injected short-read sequence. Four original local Lua/XML/font/DDS resources
are read without modification. No original code, resources or detailed vectors
are distributed.

```powershell
python scripts/check_buffered_file.py --dll build/linux-native-file/Release/FS15Core.dll
```

The native oracle requires the pinned local analysis image. Linux core and
transport tests use authored fixtures and do not need original executable
bytes. Original-resource Linux desktop validation, the complete engine loader,
archive decoding, writing/saving and native graphics/physics remain separate.

All twenty-six asset-free component/transport tests pass on Windows x64,
Linux x64 and ARM64 Linux under QEMU. The installed Linux script-host and ten
frontend/tester checks also pass in
[CI run 39122697535](https://github.com/nat649/fs15-reconstruction/actions/runs/39122697535).
The original English frontend and localization parity pass separately on Windows
with the buffered path. ELF/archive hashes and this platform evidence are
recorded in the validation report.
