`docs/ENGINE_BOOTSTRAP.md`:

```md
# ReFarm: original map scene reconstruction

**ReFarm** (`FS15EngineRebuilt.exe`) is an independently authored Win32/Direct3D 11 runtime.
It opens a native window, creates a device, swap chain, depth buffer and shaders,
uploads original terrain/object geometry and textures, and runs a free-camera render loop.
It does not load the original GIANTS executable. Bounded native routines recovered
into C++ provide GRLE decoding, Lua coordinate conversions and original TRS/affine
composition for I3D hierarchy, animated nodes and vehicle poses; the rest of the
host is authored and does not constitute a rebuilt GE6 engine.
Its resource pipeline reuses original GIANTS Engine 6 data and a verified mesh
decoder. See [component provenance](RECONSTRUCTION_STRATEGY.md). Full engine
startup and mission simulation remain incomplete.
The new experimental gameplay path, controls, recovered rules and physics
limits are described in [GAMEPLAY_RUNTIME.md](GAMEPLAY_RUNTIME.md). The sections
below describe the retained scene-viewer rendering path.

## Resources and rendering

The streaming I3D reader composes original translation, scale and XYZ Euler
rotations through the hierarchy in the documented right-handed coordinate system.
It resolves one untransformed root terrain. Each original 1025 x 1025 height
image produces a 2048 x 2048 metre terrain, sampled every two pixels into
263,169 vertices and 524,288 triangles with computed normals.

The installed RGB8 height PNGs contain a varying red/green pair and a zero blue
channel. The loader interprets this as `R * 256 + G`, scaled by
`heightScale / 65535`. This interpretation is inferred from the local resources;
it has not been compared with the original engine's native height queries.
An additional geometric check compares 272 sampled original Bjornholm road
vertices with the full-resolution DEM: median absolute height difference is
0.05 metres, versus 21.64 metres with the Z axis reversed. This checks alignment
against original geometry; it does not prove every height-query behavior.
Horizontal extent uses `(dimension - 1) * unitsPerPixel`, consistent with the
[GIANTS developer explanation](https://gdn.giants-software.com/thread.php?categoryId=16&threadId=893).

The surface uses original terrain weight maps, diffuse DDS mip chains and I3D
`unitSize` values: eight layers for Bjornholm and six for Westbridge Hills.
Their normalized blend is authored; GIANTS priority, parallax, normal-map and
dynamic crop/detail shader behavior is incomplete. Overview images are only a
terrain-only fixture fallback when no layers are defined.

Original binary meshes are decoded with pinned MIT I3DShapesTool source and an
authored .NET stream adapter. Float positions, normals, UVs, indices, subset
ranges and IDs are retained in a versioned local cache. Original shape IDs and
subset materials resolve through the scene. GPU instances preserve hierarchical
transforms; inverse-transpose normal matrices handle scaling. Object diffuse
textures retain mip chains and use alpha clipping. Water currently uses its
original underwater-fog color with simplified shading.

| Map | Decoded meshes | Rendered shape instances | Submitted object triangles |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Bjornholm | 1,155 | 338,165 | 15,071,727 |
| Westbridge Hills | 833 | 107,698 | 6,501,536 |

Instances include individual leaf/branch attachments; these are not tree or
building counts. Nonrenderable/trigger nodes, inherited hidden nodes and named
lower-LOD variants are filtered. LOD0 selection uses a static name rule;
distance-based LOD, clip distances and frustum culling remain incomplete.
The grid has no terrain LOD or collision. Original sky resources and shader
injections now provide sky blending, flags/bush wind and foliage lighting;
the native host provides a local shadow map. See [environment scope](ENVIRONMENT_RUNTIME.md).
Full cascades, tree skeletons, crop density, simulation and audio remain incomplete.

## Build and launch

The graphical launcher's **Resources > Prepare / repair assets** action now
orchestrates the existing local recovery/staging tools. See the
[resource preparation guide](LAUNCHER.md), including the original GAR-oracle
requirement for a fresh workspace. Interrupted preparation blocks host startup
until repaired. The manual commands below remain available.

The engine target needs Windows, MSVC, CMake and a Windows SDK. The frontend
uses LuaJIT; environment preparation also uses the local LuaJIT CLI and recovered
Lua sources. Mesh staging additionally needs Git and the

```powershell

.\scripts\setup_shapes_tools.ps1
& 'C:\path\to\python.exe' scripts\prepare_scene.py --game-dir $env:FS15_GAME_DIR
.\scripts\build.ps1 -PythonExe 'C:\path\to\python.exe'
.\FS15EngineRebuilt.exe --map Map01
.\FS15EngineRebuilt.exe --map Map02
.\FS15EngineRebuilt.exe --map Map01 --view overview
```

The current local package is `build/FS15GameplayAlpha4`. Launch its

`docs/FILE_STREAM_RECOVERY.md`:

```md
# Native file-stream recovery and Linux transport

The Linux port now uses four bounded stream operations recovered from GE6:

| Native entry | Recovered behavior |
|---|---|
| `0x14004f310` | Read a DWORD-sized request; clear EOF before an attempted read, set it on a successful short read, return `0xffffffff` on failure |
| `0x14004f410` | Absolute seek through the signed 32-bit Windows distance; preserve EOF on failure, otherwise set it from returned position versus requested position |
| `0x14004f460` | Return the low 32-bit file size or `0xffffffff` |
| `0x14004f4b0` | Query position through a zero-distance relative seek without changing EOF |

The x64 record retains its handle/token at `+8` and EOF byte at `+0x10`.
Other record bytes remain untouched. Instruction inspection confirms that seek
returns a C++ boolean in **AL**; the pseudocode's apparent 32-bit return includes
undefined upper bits. The portable API exposes a defined integer boolean.
Values from `0x80000000` through `0xffffffff` remain signed negative absolute
seek distances and normally fail. Seeking past EOF does not itself set EOF.
A successful zero-byte read clears EOF. Size/position sentinel ambiguities are
retained rather than silently replaced by 64-bit semantics.

## OS boundary and integration

`src/core/file_stream.cpp` contains the recovered control flow. Its explicit
service callbacks are authored OS seams. `FS15FileTransport` supplies a read-only
regular-file adapter: the inspected Win32 APIs on Windows, POSIX `open`, `read`,
`lseek`, `fstat`, `close` on Linux. It owns and closes its OS file token.

The bounded whole-file helper is authored: it checks the full OS size before
allocation and rejects oversize/short reads. It does not change the recovered
DWORD interface or add a native 64-bit file-service claim. The menu uses it for
source scripts, DDS data and bitmap-font metrics; the script host uses it for
localization sources, and the Linux XML adapter uses it before Expat parsing.
Third-party PNG decoders and Windows XmlLite retain their separate transports.

This is not a general Windows compatibility layer, Proton replacement or a
complete native engine startup. Native stream constructors/destructors, string
ownership, archive providers, write/append services, remaining buffered operations, live file
mutation, Windows path/case/locking semantics and the complete VFS remain open.
The native disk-corruption notification branch is surfaced as a callback; its
original logger/global-queue effects have not been validated. POSIX error codes
are mapped to bounded ordinary errors, not claimed as full Win32 error parity.

## Validation

`scripts/check_native_file_stream.py` compares the rebuilt code against the
unchanged routines in the pinned local Windows analysis image. Four kernel IAT
slots are rebound to actual Windows APIs. Ordinary failure scenarios use
explicit injected API seams; they are counted separately from real file I/O.
No PE entry point, Steam initialization or game process is run.

The comparison covers **2,492 operations in 37 sequences**: 692 reads, 554 seeks,
620 size queries and 626 position queries. Complete records and guarded output
buffers match. Inputs include empty files, UTF-8 paths with spaces, embedded
zero bytes, short/exact/zero reads, seeks past EOF, signed-limit failures,
invalid-token branches and eleven injected failure sequences. Four original
local resources cover Lua, localization XML, font metrics and compressed DDS.
Original bytes and detailed instruction dumps remain local. Source hashes,
input hashes and aggregate counts are in [validation evidence](../analysis/file-stream-validation.json).

Two asset-free CTests exercise the recovered control flow and actual OS
transport independently. The full portable suite now has twenty-five tests.
The subsequent [buffered-reader recovery](BUFFERED_FILE_RECOVERY.md) adds a
component test and connects native cached reads to this transport.
Linux x64/ARM64 execution evidence is separate from the native Windows oracle;
neither establishes complete original-resource Linux gameplay equivalence.
All twenty-five tests and existing frontend checks pass in
[Linux CI run 39122034884](https://github.com/nat649/fs15-reconstruction/actions/runs/39122034884).
The original-resource English menu and localization comparison pass separately
on Windows with the new stream path. The downloaded Linux ELF/runtime archive
hashes are recorded in the same aggregate evidence.

```powershell
python scripts/check_native_file_stream.py --dll build/linux-native-file/Release/FS15Core.dll
```

The reference image and DLL must match the documented local recovery build.
The core tests and Linux runtime require neither original code bytes nor a
Windows runtime.

## Timing, pause and original-script comparisons

The authored host now advances gameplay in fixed 1/60-second ticks. Different
render frame durations accumulate into the same simulation updates, so motor
control, crop work, grain transfers and original animations receive a consistent
time step. Each frame accepts at most 0.25 seconds of catch-up time; additional

attachment, filling, pipe and unloading actions are ignored while paused.

rates describe test input timing, not a graphics performance benchmark.

`docs/GAR.md`:

```md
# GAR 5.3 recovery

This parser targets the two observed FS15 1.4.2.0 archives, with version
word `0x00050003`. It rejects other versions and unsupported record fields.
No original archive data is included in the repository.

## Observed layout

The file begins with a 512-byte header. At offset `0x60` are the four bytes
`GAR `, followed by a little-endian version word at `0x64`. The native reader
at `0x1402a6d70` adds the 32-bit values at `0x68` and `0x6c` to obtain the
index record count for this version. Their broader meaning is not assumed.
For the reference archives these values are `(5, 614)` and `(5, 497)`.

The encrypted index starts at offset 512 and occupies `count * 512` bytes.
Each observed decoded record uses:

| Record offset | Interpretation used by this parser |
|---|---|
| `0x00` | 32-bit record kind, observed value 1 |
| `0x04` | 32-bit flags, observed value 0 |
| `0x08` | Encrypted payload length, interpreted as a 64-bit value |
| `0x10` | Original payload length, interpreted as a 64-bit value |
| `0x18` | Absolute payload offset, interpreted as a 64-bit value |
| `0x20` | Reserved 64-bit value, observed value 0 |
| `0x28` | NUL-terminated UTF-8 path in the remaining 472 bytes |

The upper halves of the observed span values are zero. File payloads use
complete eight-byte encrypted blocks with one to eight padding bytes.
The parser checks index bounds, payload bounds and overlaps, padding length,
name termination, case collisions, path traversal, and Windows path aliases.

## Cipher dependency

`scripts/native_gar.py` requires the exact previously verified analysis image
with SHA-256
`6d1beaf9d7e3c57dd51cec03385a53bda82b4ac946e622d8d2fa592a56d71f9f`.
It reserves the reference image address range in the extraction process,
copies the code/data sections, and calls the cipher initializer
`0x1402e6e60` and buffer decoder `0x1402e7500`. The PE entry point and game
initialization are not called. Key arguments are read from the observed
GAR factory instructions in that local image.

This is an **original-code oracle**, not a standalone cipher reconstruction.
No reference code bytes are distributed. An independent cipher is remaining
work; the current pipeline is a way to recover and validate local inputs for
the reconstruction effort.

## Extraction evidence

The two archives yielded 619 and 502 files. Hash verification covers all
1,121 outputs. Additional checks cover 374 DDS headers, 81 complete PNG
chunk CRC sets, 21 WAV headers, and 470 LuaJIT v2 headers.

Strict XML parsing passed for 134 of 141 XML/I3D files. Seven description
files contain adjacent attributes without required whitespace in their
extracted bytes. Those diagnostics are recorded; extraction does not repair
or rewrite the original files.

Use `scripts/extract_gar.py` followed by `scripts/verify_recovered_files.py`.
The full manifests and original content remain local. Aggregate metadata
is stored in `analysis/*-extraction-summary.json`.

```

`docs/GE6_LINUX_NATIVE_BOOT.md`:

```md
# Original GE6 startup on Linux x64

The active task is to run the original GIANTS Engine 6 on Linux. ReFarm and the
separate original-object preview are fixtures, not this runtime or its startup.

`FS15GE6LinuxBoot` is an experimental Linux ELF launcher for the user's private,
version-pinned original x64 instruction image. It preserves native GE6 code and
data, maps PE sections at their original addresses and binds supported OS
imports to Linux services through the Microsoft x64 calling convention. Neither
Wine nor Proton is linked or invoked. No replacement renderer, physics world,
menu or game engine is linked to this executable.

The initial entry is the inspected original CRT at `0x1403fc96c`, followed by
`0x1403fc7f4` and its original initialization chain. The platform bootstrap
section `.bind` is not executed. The normalized private analysis image is the
same reference used by the Windows original-code checks, SHA-256
`6d1beaf9d7e3c57dd51cec03385a53bda82b4ac946e622d8d2fa592a56d71f9f`.
The loader also recognizes the separately pinned, already prepared **Local GE6**
image described below. Original instructions are not distributed.

## Build and execute

On Linux x86_64:

```sh
sudo apt-get install g++ cmake libssl-dev libasound2-dev libpulse-dev libpng-dev libx11-dev libxrandr-dev libgl-dev
cmake -S src/ge6_linux -B build/ge6-linux-boot -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build/ge6-linux-boot --parallel 2
build/ge6-linux-boot/FS15GE6LinuxBoot \
  --image inputs/runtime/FarmingSimulator2015Game.runtime.bin
```

The root portable CMake also exposes `FS15_BUILD_GE6_LINUX_BOOT=ON`. Linux
workflow artifacts include `bin/FS15GE6LinuxBoot`; this remains a diagnostic,
not a playable GE6 build. OpenSSL checks the original-image SHA-256. CMake
downloads a SHA-256-pinned OpenAL Soft source release for Linux audio; it does
not download original game files. See [dependency and relinking materials](../src/ge6_linux/AUDIO_DEPENDENCY.md).

The normal dynamic build enables `FS15_GE6_X11=ON`. It needs a real X11 server
and host OpenGL/GLX drivers. `FS15_GE6_BOOT_STATIC=ON` retains the separate
headless diagnostic with X11 disabled. Neither build includes original files.

## OS transport and remaining work

The loader privately copies the validated readable PE resource directory into
bounded host storage. `LoadImageW` resolves group-icon names or integer IDs,
then decodes the first original frame for the observed zero-size/default-color
request. PNG frames use Linux libpng/zlib; uncompressed 8/24/32-bit DIB frames
use an authored palette/BGRA/orientation/AND-mask adapter. This is Windows image
resource transport, not recovered engine image-loading code. Authored fixtures
verify pixels, alpha/masks, IDs/names, shared/nonshared lifetime, missing-resource
errors and malformed directory/data bounds. A separate PE fixture loads an
authored icon through the six-argument IAT call and supplies a native WNDCLASSW.

`RegisterClassW` stores a copied ASCII class name, the original Microsoft-ABI
procedure, style/extra-byte counts and a retained icon reference. It returns an
atom for that actual process-local record and rejects duplicate registrations.
Unregistering releases the record and checks window references. This is class
metadata for subsequent window creation; it does not create an OS window or
call the procedure. Menus, cursors, brushes, global/DLL class namespaces and
full Unicode class-name comparison remain open. Unsupported image types,
file/system images, resizing/other LoadImage flags and unsupported class
parameters stop explicitly; missing named resources return their actual error.
The [Windows image API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-loadimagew)
and [class registration API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-registerclassw)
define the transported boundary.

`LoadLibraryW` transcodes validated UTF-16 into the same bounded authored-module
lookup/reference tracking used by `LoadLibraryA`. Null, malformed and missing
names retain failure/error behavior. This does not load arbitrary Windows DLL
instructions or provide a full Windows search path/dependency loader. Optional
unavailable modules remain unavailable. The authored USER32 module view exposes
the same implemented Microsoft-ABI image/class functions through GetProcAddress;
unimplemented exports return unavailable, never a System V pointer.
SDL's optional export probes format their failures with `FormatMessageW` before
continuing. Its observed FROM_SYSTEM call now supplies bounded English text for
module/procedure-not-found errors (126/127), preserving UTF-16 counts, caller
buffers and LastError on success. A seven-argument authored PE fixture checks
the output and its untouched guard. This is not a complete localized Windows
message catalogue: unsupported standard message IDs/formatting flags stop;
absent high IDs and unsupported languages return failure.

All 32 statically imported OpenAL functions have typed Microsoft-x64 wrappers
which call the actual Linux OpenAL Soft 1.24.3 implementation. Device/context
creation, errors, buffers, source queues and mixing are provided by that
third-party library. Only the two Windows router default selectors map to the
Linux default device; explicit device names are preserved and unknown ones
fail. No System V extension function pointer is returned to original PE code.
ALSA and PulseAudio backends are compiled in; the VM/CI select silent output.
Authored tests verify actual PCM loopback energy, queue order, source state,
errors and cleanup. A separate authored PE fixture calls the wrappers through
its IAT and checks the Windows XMM1 argument for a listener gain value. The
workflow also relinks the supplied object/archive and repeats the mixer test.
Complete upstream source, notices and relinking materials accompany installed
boot artifacts. This reuses Linux audio middleware; it does not reconstruct
GE6's engine logic or the original Windows OpenAL DLL.

There is no Direct3D9 service in this Linux transport. Its factory reports
documented failure (`nullptr`), allowing the original optional adapter probe
to choose its own continuation. It does not create an adapter, synthesize a GPU
identity or implement Direct3D rendering. The original application supports a
separate default graphics path; connecting its window/context APIs remains work.

`SetConsoleCtrlHandler` registers/removes actual callbacks, following reverse
registration order and stopping at a handled event. Linux `SIGINT` maps to
`CTRL_C_EVENT`, and `SIGQUIT` to `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT`; the null-handler ignore flag
affects only Ctrl+C. The POSIX signal routine writes to a nonblocking pipe;
it never calls original PE code or takes C++ locks. A dispatcher starts a fresh
thread for each queued event, installs the GS stack prefix, calls the Microsoft
ABI handlers and performs FLS cleanup before restoring GS. Notifications are
serialized. Host shutdown joins this dispatcher before unmapping original code.
The two pipe descriptors remain owned until process exit so an in-flight signal
handler cannot write into a recycled descriptor. Initialization failures after
signal installation also retain those descriptors and restore host dispositions.
See the [Windows API contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/console/setconsolectrlhandler).

Authored fixtures send real SIGINT/SIGQUIT, check order, ignore/removal (including
self-removal), distinct callback TIDs, GS/TLS isolation and FLS cleanup. A small
authored PE receives a real SIGINT through the IAT-registered callback and checks
its GS metadata and distinct TID. An unhandled signal test exits with Linux
status 130. Close/logoff/shutdown console events, console attachment/reset,
debugger exceptions, child ignore-flag inheritance and complete Windows process
status semantics remain unsupported; pipe saturation/POSIX signals can coalesce
notifications. The original-game boot test observes **registration only**; it
does not inject a control event or establish original handler return/shutdown.
Aggregate evidence distinguishes registration from a completed callback.

OS bindings use Linux clocks/process/thread identifiers, allocations, recursive
mutexes and bounded main-thread CRT slot/module services. These are authored
platform transport, not recovered engine code. `GetVersion` supplies API
compatibility level 6, not the host OS version. A small GS-based NT_TIB prefix
provides actual Linux thread stack bounds for original MSVC stack probes;
Linux libc's FS-based TLS is unchanged. CP1252 classification/case tables are
numeric Windows OS observations generated by `capture_ge6_ansi_reference.py`;
only the captured characters/locales/flags are supported. Environment staging
is still ASCII-bounded. Valid UTF-8/UTF-16 strings support non-ASCII names and
surrogate pairs; malformed input is rejected, so Windows flags-zero replacement
behavior is not complete. Synchronous file creation/read/write/seek/size/search,
copy and timestamp queries use POSIX services. Copies preserve permissions and
access/modification timestamps; unavailable creation timestamps are zero rather
than a fabricated POSIX change time. Windows sharing, case-insensitivity,
overlapped I/O and full NTFS metadata semantics are not reproduced.
`GetVersion`/`GetVersionExA` expose compatibility API level 6.0, not a Windows
host; the VM reports its actual Linux kernel separately.
`CoInitializeEx` explicitly fails: no COM apartment, object activation or
DirectX/COM service is supplied. Its return value is checked in authored tests;
the observed original startup caller tolerates the failure.
The bounded network adapter negotiates Winsock versions in the x64 `WSADATA`
layout, probes actual IPv4 UDP support, tracks startup/cleanup references and
owns real POSIX sockets. Its direct UDP bind/name/send/receive calls translate
errors and report truncation. TCP, DNS, IPv6, overlapped socket APIs and full
Winsock provider behavior remain unimplemented. This does not validate FS15
multiplayer or an online session. The isolated original-code VM has no network
device; UDP loopback is tested separately on the Linux CI host.

Main-thread timer requests check Linux clock resolution, bound timer slack and
restore it when leases end. Affinity uses actual Linux CPU masks within the
supported low 64 CPUs; it rejects unsupported handles/masks. Full Windows
multimedia/process-wide scheduling behavior is not reproduced. Unnamed events
support auto/manual reset and finite/infinite waits through mutexes/condition
variables. Non-alertable `WaitForSingleObjectEx` calls use that same transport;
alertable/APC waits stop explicitly. Named events remain unavailable.

`CreateThread` uses a Linux pthread with the PE's default stack reserve or a
bounded requested size. Every worker installs its own inspected NT_TIB prefix
without changing Linux FS TLS, then invokes the original callback with the
Microsoft ABI. Initially suspended creation, `ResumeThread`, wait/status queries
and handle closure are connected. Closing a handle does not cancel the worker;
normal callback return performs FLS callbacks before restoring GS and signaling
completion. Separate TLS (1088) and FLS (128) index pools hold per-thread values,
clear values on index reuse and dispatch non-null FLS callbacks on free/exit.
This supplies the observed native CRT storage mechanism; fibers and general
Windows TLS/CRT/DLL thread lifecycle parity are not claimed.

Shared critical-section, file/socket/key/module handle registries are protected
against concurrent mutation. Process exit and missing-import stops terminate
directly instead of destructing/unmapping code beneath live native workers.
Authored fixtures verify two workers, isolated errors/slots, 1000 protected
counter updates, real stack bounds and FLS callbacks. The original VM workers
are alive when the startup dependency stop ends the process; complete original worker return,
shutdown and cleanup remain unverified. `ExitThread`, arbitrary thread suspension,
termination, priorities, exception dispatch and processor groups remain open.

Only the documented legacy debugger naming packet (`0x406d1388`, validated
24-byte structure) is consumed by `RaiseException`, and maps to actual Linux
thread names truncated to 15 bytes. Other exception codes/payloads stop; C++
exceptions, assertions and engine failures are not ignored. Environment queries
use the actual Linux process and remain ASCII-bounded/case-sensitive.

The read-only CPU registry view exposes only `ProcessorNameString` from Linux
`/proc/cpuinfo`; unknown keys/values fail. Memory totals/availability come from
`/proc/meminfo`, not an invented Windows machine. Commit accounting/cgroup
limits and processor groups are not Windows-compatible; virtual space uses a
conservative low-47-bit budget capped by `RLIMIT_AS`.

The original Lua allocator's dynamically resolved `NtAllocateVirtualMemory`
uses real anonymous Linux reservations and page commitments, with low-address
allocation for its observed request. Managed-region `VirtualQuery` and
decommit/release are connected; recommit preserves existing data or zeroes
decommitted pages as appropriate. Only owned mappings and non-executable
protections are supported. Arbitrary address-space queries, guard pages,
large-page/NUMA policies and general NT/JIT contracts remain open.

`LoadLibraryA`/`GetModuleHandle`/`GetProcAddress` expose only the known authored
kernel/NT/timer ABI modules. Explicit loads/releases track references; this does
not load Windows DLL code or unload the resident import transport. Missing
modules/procedures fail. General Windows DLL loading, SEH/unwind and exception
dispatch and full TEB/PEB/thread behavior remain incomplete. Window/OpenGL/audio
now have the bounded Linux bindings described above; full parity is unverified.
Steam services remain unavailable through the local adapter.

Exception-filter registration retains/replaces the native callback and returns
the previous value; native Windows exception dispatch is not connected. The
named mutex binding implements only GE6's singleton presence/lifetime check
with a per-user Linux file lock, not general Wait/ReleaseMutex behavior.

Each unimplemented import has a named stop trampoline. Calling one prints
`GE6_BLOCKED_IMPORT library!symbol caller=...` and exits with status 78; it never
returns fabricated engine/render initialization success. Native instruction
faults report their instruction address separately.

## Validation boundaries

`tests/check_ge6_linux_boot.py` uses authored PE instructions to check mapping,
writable zero-filled data, an actual Microsoft-ABI import call/writeback, a
named missing-import stop, hash rejection and overlapping-section rejection.
Those fixtures do not boot original GE6 code.

`scripts/check_ge6_linux_vm.py` runs the private original image in a local QEMU
Linux VM using an existing Alpine kernel/initramfs and a static launcher build
(`FS15_GE6_BOOT_STATIC=ON`). No network device is attached. Its generated
`private-ge6-initramfs.gz` embeds original code and must stay local. The serial
log distinguishes CRT execution, missing services, native faults and exits.

PE mapping follows the [Microsoft specification](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/debug/pe-format).
The ABI bridge uses GCC's [`ms_abi` attribute](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/x86-Function-Attributes.html).
API contracts use Microsoft's [Winsock startup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winsock2/nf-winsock2-wsastartup),
[timer requests](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/timeapi/nf-timeapi-timebeginperiod)
and [NT virtual allocation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/ntifs/nf-ntifs-ntallocatevirtualmemory)
documentation; satisfying a bounded observed contract does not establish complete Windows API parity.
Thread behavior follows the bounded contracts from
[CreateThread](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createthread),
[FLS cleanup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fibersapi/nf-fibersapi-flsfree)
and [legacy debugger naming](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/debugger/tips-for-debugging-threads?view=visualstudio).

Acceptance milestones are original CRT completion, original application startup,
renderer/window creation, resource loading and a native GE6 menu/map session.
Mapping or passing an authored ABI fixture does not establish these milestones.

`docs/GE6_PHYSICS_BACKEND.md`:

```md
# GE6 physics world and solver recovery

This work targets GE6. It does not port or depend on ReFarm.

The pinned GE6 image contains explicit RTTI for `btCollisionDispatcher`,
`btDefaultCollisionConfiguration`, `btDiscreteDynamicsWorld`,
`btSequentialImpulseConstraintSolver`, `Bt2World`, `Bt2Solver` and
`Bt2RaycastVehicle`. Its world factory at `0x14027fb30` constructs the Bullet
configuration, dispatcher, broadphase, solver and GE6 world subclasses.
Earlier documents' references to a hypothetical PhysX backend are superseded
by this direct identification of Bullet in the inspected runtime.

## Reused middleware and recovered GIANTS code

The optional `FS15_BUILD_GE6_PHYSICS` target fetches upstream Bullet at commit
[`0e1a77047cfaa9bf94f7318686ba4179f40c8c1b`](https://github.com/bulletphysics/bullet3/tree/0e1a77047cfaa9bf94f7318686ba4179f40c8c1b),
with an archive SHA-256 check. It builds only LinearMath, BulletCollision and
BulletDynamics. Upstream code stays in the ignored build dependency directory;
its original license is installed with the package. It is reused middleware,
not newly decompiled GIANTS source. No original game binary is linked into the
portable target.

Neither released Bullet 2.82 nor released 2.83 matches all inspected structures.
The selected 2014 revision retains the user-pointer/user-index union, adds the
ignored-collision-object array and contains the row-solver function pointers.
Nine Windows x64 layout sizes match the inspected native paths:

| Object | Bytes |
|---|---:|
| Base discrete world | 464 |
| Base sequential impulse solver | 336 |
| DBVT broadphase | 288 |
| Collision dispatcher | 10,496 |
| Base collision configuration | 184 |
| Rigid body | 736 |
| Persistent manifold | 896 |
| Manifold point | 192 |
| Broadphase proxy | 64 |

This identifies a compatible tested upstream candidate, **not the exact full
GIANTS middleware fork**. Linux and ARM64 code use typed middleware APIs;
Windows object offsets must not be assumed portable.

[`src/ge6/physics_world.cpp`](../src/ge6/physics_world.cpp) recovers GE6's
collision dispatcher and near-pair rules, island merging, ordered vehicle
collision/solver hooks and setup/velocity/penetration/finish phases. In
particular, ordinary sleeping pairs are removed; stock Bullet's callback would
retain their manifolds. Trigger pairs follow a separate retention rule.
The [recovered vehicle sort](../src/core/physics_vehicle_sort.cpp) preserves
native equal-key swap order, rather than replacing it with `std::sort`.
RAII ownership and factory orchestration are authored. The stock broadphase
is currently serialized by its caller; the original broadphase's lock methods
and custom heightfield creation functions are not yet supplied.

## Native comparison

The [local differential test](../scripts/check_ge6_physics_world.py) executes
unchanged original GE6 factory, sphere, body setup, world/solver stepping and
destruction bodies in an isolated process. It supplies a private CRT heap,
aligned allocator and timing imports without calling the executable entry
point, Steam or an installed game process. The original factory's externally
supplied pair-cache allocation is explicitly reclaimed by the fixture owner.

The optional native math mapping now includes the auxiliary `data` section as
well as `text`: the original `powf` needs those masks/constants. A startup
assertion checks `powf(1, 1/60) == 1` before comparing trajectories. Mapping code
without its constant section had incorrectly erased damping velocities in an
early investigation; those results are excluded from the validation report.

The [source-pinned results](../analysis/ge6-physics-world-validation.json) record:

- 64 sphere-drop lifetimes and **15,360 trajectory frames**, including
  **6,963 frames with generated contacts**;
- maximum scaled position/velocity error **0.0000014157** against original GE6;
- 96 nonempty vehicle-hook fixtures and **26,984 ordered callback events**;
- 1,024 native vehicle-sort fixtures, including duplicate island keys and
  complete key-query order;
- complete native aligned-allocation cleanup after the explicit fixture-owned
  pair-cache teardown.

Vehicle callback fixtures verify the engine's routing and ordering. Their
objects do not implement the actual `Bt2RaycastVehicle` contact/wheel solver.
The portable CTest additionally requires accumulated gravity, collision response,
stable resting height and connected vehicle hook phases.

## Recovered wheel ray and finish paths

[`vehicle_wheel.cpp`](../src/ge6/vehicle_wheel.cpp) ports five further bounded
bodies: `0x140150a10` suspension frame, `0x140151930` wheel ray filter,
`0x1400ba820` closest-hit callback, `0x140153330` suspension ray and
`0x140155140` solved-wheel finish/readback. The public typed structures are
authored transport, not Windows Bullet object layouts.

The GE6 filter uses an OR of corresponding group/mask bits, rejects the owning
body, triggers and objects without the rigid-body internal type, and honors
the owner's ignored pairs. Replacing this with stock Bullet's cross-field AND
changes observed behavior. Suspension distances retain native compression and
droop clamps. Wheel finish preserves the native single angle wrap (not modulo),
sleep/inactive guards, solved normal-impulse force and slip/motor readback.

The [local comparison](../scripts/check_ge6_vehicle_wheel.py) and
[source-pinned result](../analysis/ge6-vehicle-wheel-validation.json) cover
768 frames, 768 miss/world-normal/local-normal ray fixtures, 4,096 filters and
1,024 finish states: **6,656 fixtures with zero observed numeric difference**.
The ray fixtures supply controlled results through an authored world callback;
unchanged original GE6 ray/callback bodies execute. A separate portable CTest
uses actual Bullet world ray queries to validate ground hits, owner/trigger/
non-rigid rejection, ignored pairs, compression limits and missing contacts.
These functions are not registered as a complete vehicle solver. The bounded
constraint helpers, penetration and velocity phases below extend them; full
setup orchestration and the drivetrain network remain open.

The world/solver checkpoint passes all 34 CTests on Windows x64, Linux x64 and
ARM64 Linux under QEMU ([CI](https://github.com/nat649/fs15-reconstruction/actions/runs/39155932339)).
The ray/finish extensions also pass Linux/ARM CI in
[run 39156379940](https://github.com/nat649/fs15-reconstruction/actions/runs/39156379940).

## Suspension constraint setup and penetration correction

[`vehicle_constraint.cpp`](../src/ge6/vehicle_constraint.cpp) recovers three
further bodies: the Jacobian helper `0x1401511a0`, spring setup `0x140150f50`
and complete wheel split-penetration loop `0x140154d70`. Its typed structures
are authored transport, not raw casts of the native Windows records. Query
and application directions remain distinct. Body inertia/angular factors,
solver velocities/external force impulses, asymmetric damping, compression
limits and solver ERP/split thresholds follow the original paths.

Instruction inspection corrected an ambiguous decompiler expression: the
native setup sums both body terms before adding spring softness. Preserving
that association matters near cancelling terms. Native wheel setup also uses
the geometric suspension length before its separate readback clamp; passing
the clamped length would suppress bottom-out correction.

The [local differential harness](../scripts/check_ge6_vehicle_constraint.py)
and [source-pinned report](../analysis/ge6-vehicle-constraint-validation.json)
cover 2,048 Jacobians, 2,048 spring states and 1,024 multi-wheel penetration
states over **6,640 successive iterations**. They compare complete records and
solver bodies, including inactive/sleeping guards, static solver bodies,
misses, accumulated-impulse clamps, shared bodies and aliased A/B bodies.
Maximum scaled numeric error is **0.0000005114** in this domain.

The additional `ge6_suspension_penetration_integration` CTest connects actual
Bullet world rays, recovered spring setup and the recovered penetration phase
through GE6's solver hooks to middleware transform writeback. With explicit
fixture ERP2 `0.2` and split threshold `0`, a chassis starts at height `0.5`,
reaches `0.56` after one step and `0.799629` after 30 steps, approaching the
`0.8` compression limit without introducing kinetic velocity or chassis
collision contacts. This is an authored one-wheel **phase isolation fixture**:
its motor and velocity phases deliberately do nothing. It is not registered
as a production vehicle and does not demonstrate drivable gameplay. All 35
component tests pass on Windows x64, Linux x64 and ARM64 Linux under QEMU;
[CI run 39220107155](https://github.com/nat649/fs15-reconstruction/actions/runs/39220107155)
validates source commit `5a880aa`.

## Wheel velocity, friction and braking

[`vehicle_velocity.cpp`](../src/ge6/vehicle_velocity.cpp) recovers the bounded
`0x1401540b0` phase over the previously recovered tire-force leaf. It applies
normal and correction velocity impulses, computes wheel load using the native
gravity queries, limits longitudinal/lateral tire impulses and couples brake
impulses to wheel spin and chassis velocity. Native impulse clamp order, up to
ten brake/friction inner iterations, body sharing, static-body guards and
sleep/inactive/contact guards are retained.

The [local comparison](../scripts/check_ge6_vehicle_velocity.py) and
[source-pinned report](../analysis/ge6-vehicle-velocity-validation.json) cover
**1,024 vehicle states / 6,640 successive iterations**, including **18,448
original gravity queries** and 584 states configured with brakes. Complete
wheel, constraint and solver-body records are compared. Maximum scaled numeric
error is **0.0000003242** in the tested finite, positive tire-parameter domain.

The original drivetrain helper `0x140155d50` executes with zero differential
nodes in these native fixtures. Recompiled code supplies an explicit no-op
driver callback and typed gravity transport. This does **not** recover the
motor/differential network or demonstrate power from a recovered engine.

The additional `ge6_wheel_velocity_integration` CTest connects actual world
rays, recovered Jacobian/spring setup, penetration, velocity/friction/brake
and wheel readback through the GE6 solver hooks. A one-wheel fixture starts
with wheel spin `20 rad/s`: the chassis reaches `8 m/s` while suspension keeps
it near height `1.49` under gravity. Applying the wheel brake brings chassis
speed and wheel spin to zero. Chassis-ground collision contacts do not supply
support or traction. Fixed slip inputs, simple geometry and setup orchestration
are authored fixture data. This is component integration, not an original
tractor, a recovered motor or a playable game. All 36 component tests pass on
Windows x64, Linux x64 and ARM64 Linux under QEMU.
[CI run 39223398050](https://github.com/nat649/fs15-reconstruction/actions/runs/39223398050)
validates source commit `2c65697`.

`docs/GL_BUFFER_RECOVERY.md`:

```md
# Recovered GE6 OpenGL buffers

Nine additional native paths now compile as portable C++17 in
[`gl_buffers.cpp`](../src/core/gl_buffers.cpp). These are recovered algorithms,
with explicit authored services for the original process-global GL dispatch,
allocator, counters and shared staging storage. They are separate from ReFarm's
authored D3D11 renderer and from the CPU buffers in the portable headless host.

| Native entry | Bounded recovered path |
|---|---|
| `0x140065c60` | Vertex allocation, GL storage, usage selection and cached binding invalidation |
| `0x140074850` | Index construction and unsigned-short/unsigned-int format selection |
| `0x140074920` | Index deletion, byte counter and base-vtable transition |
| `0x140074990` | Index mapping, optional orphaning and byte offset |
| `0x140074a10` | Index unmapping |
| `0x140074a40` | Vertex deletion, byte counter and base-vtable transition |
| `0x140074ab0` | Shared staging or direct vertex mapping |
| `0x140074b70` | Vertex unmapping or staged upload |
| `0x140074bd0` | Vertex subdata transfer, optionally orphaning storage first |

The native layouts retain opaque bytes, numeric vtable identities and unsigned
32-bit byte-counter wrapping. Original pointers are never executed by the port.
The allocator's CRT exception machinery is excluded; a failed authored allocator
returns null. The public API guards missing services and undersized caller
storage. It does not validate arbitrary native pointer graphs or GL ranges.

## Transfer semantics

Vertex storage uses `GL_ARRAY_BUFFER`; index storage uses
`GL_ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER`. Descriptor flags select `GL_DYNAMIC_DRAW`,
`GL_STATIC_DRAW` or `GL_STREAM_DRAW` exactly as in the inspected instructions.
Mode `1` discards old storage, mode `2` maps for reading, other modes write.

For vertex writes of at most 16 MiB, an available global scratch buffer supplies
the returned address. This is its **start**, regardless of the destination
offset. Unmap clears its occupied flag, binds the original buffer, optionally
orphans storage and uploads scratch bytes at the recorded destination offset.
Another map while scratch is occupied instead maps GL storage directly. Read
maps always use GL. Direct mappings return the GL pointer plus the byte offset,
including the original null-pointer-plus-offset behavior on mapping failure.
Callers must inspect GL errors and obey object, context and mapping lifetimes.

## Evidence and Linux check

The [Windows differential test](../scripts/check_gl_buffers.py) runs all nine
unchanged original bodies against owned recording GL callbacks and an isolated
native CRT heap: **1,024 paired vertex/index lifetimes**, randomized flags,
read/write/discard modes, scratch contention, the 16 MiB boundary, failed GL
mapping and counter wrapping. Full map/unmap/destruction records and ordered GL
calls match. Constructor allocator spare bytes are excluded. The deleting free
flag and allocator exceptions are not native differential coverage.
See the [source-pinned report](../analysis/gl-buffers-validation.json).

`FS15GLBuffersCheck` is an asset-free transport test in the normal CTest suite.
`FS15GLDriverCheck` uses an authored SDL context and actual GL symbols, checking
initial data, staging/subdata, direct/discard maps, byte readback, resource
deletion, counters and GL errors. It does not draw a game scene. Linux CI runs
this executable on Mesa's software renderer under Xvfb, separately from the
asset-free core tests. This is real OpenGL API execution, not hardware GPU
performance or original-resource desktop validation.

[Linux run 39152321706](https://github.com/nat649/fs15-reconstruction/actions/runs/39152321706)
passes all **32** component/transport tests on Linux x64 and ARM64 Linux under
QEMU, plus the actual GL check on **llvmpipe (LLVM 20.1.2, 256 bits)**. The same
32 component tests pass locally on Windows x64. The source-pinned report records
the tested commit, runtime archive and four installed executable hashes.

```sh
cmake -S . -B build/linux-gl -DFS15_PORTABLE_CORE_ONLY=ON \
  -DFS15_BUILD_GL_CHECK=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build/linux-gl --parallel 2
ctest --test-dir build/linux-gl --output-on-failure
# On a Linux desktop:
./build/linux-gl/src/core/FS15GLDriverCheck
# For headless Mesa validation (requires Xvfb and xauth):
LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 xvfb-run -a ./build/linux-gl/src/core/FS15GLDriverCheck
```

Install SDL2 development headers, OpenGL headers and a working GL driver
(`libsdl2-dev libgl-dev libgl1-mesa-dri` on the CI distribution). The optional
driver-check executable is installed in `bin` and needs SDL2 and desktop GL.
The component-only checks have no SDL or GL dependency, including ARM64 QEMU.

## Remaining renderer and physics work

These buffer paths are not the complete graphics driver. Shader compilation,
material/texture state, vertex layouts, draw submission, render targets and
connection to the recovered scene loader still need recovery and integration.
The headless host continues to report `renderer_started=false` and
`playable=false`. Native physics factory/scene construction, collision shapes,
terrain contacts and the complete body/constraint solver are also unfinished.

`docs/GL_DRAW_RECOVERY.md`:

```md
# GE6 OpenGL draw dispatch

`src/core/gl_draw.cpp` recovers native `0x140065540`, including the bound-layout
gate, five primitive modes, cached point size, non-indexed arrays, indexed
draws and range-index draws. Native instruction inspection establishes that
the index byte offset is multiplied in a 32-bit register and then zero-extended;
negative/large first indices retain that wrapping. Range end calculation also
wraps at 32 bits. Vertex layout/program/context/index binding are caller services.
Null service and invalid primitive guards are authored transport boundaries.

The [local comparison](../scripts/check_gl_draw.py) and
[source-pinned report](../analysis/gl-draw-validation.json) compare complete
driver records and ordered GL calls for **4,096 states / 3,853 calls**. This
includes missing layouts, both index sizes, cache hits/misses/NaN point-size
state, and integer wrapping. Original GL imports are rebound only in the local
isolated reference image; no running game or executable entry point is invoked.

The optional `FS15GLDriverCheck` now creates a triangle through recovered buffer
allocation and sends array/index/range draws through this recovered dispatch.
It reads the center pixel from an actual OpenGL framebuffer and requires blue
for all three paths, then black when the native layout gate suppresses drawing.
The context, fixed-function matrices/attributes and constant color are authored
test transport. They do not implement or replace GE6's scene shaders/materials.
The CPU-only `portable_gl_draw` CTest checks dispatch and wrapping without a GPU.

[CI run 39226238887](https://github.com/nat649/fs15-reconstruction/actions/runs/39226238887)
passes all 38 component tests on Linux x64 and ARM64 Linux under QEMU for source
commit `1d92558`. Its actual-driver step also passes array/index/range primitive
pixel readback on Mesa llvmpipe (LLVM 20.1.2). This is software OpenGL validation;
hardware GPU and original scene rendering remain separate.

On Linux with SDL2/OpenGL installed:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build/gl-check -DFS15_PORTABLE_CORE_ONLY=ON \
  -DFS15_BUILD_GL_CHECK=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build/gl-check --parallel 2
LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 xvfb-run -a build/gl-check/src/core/FS15GLDriverCheck
```

The [object integration target](GE6_OBJECT_RENDERING.md) now connects this draw

`docs/LAUNCHER.md`:

```md
# Launcher and local resource preparation

Build with `scripts/build-launcher.ps1`, then open `Launch FS15.cmd`.
The launcher needs the .NET 10 Windows Desktop runtime and Python 3.11+.
The **Settings & activity** page allows selecting Python and an optional Steam client.
The sidebar links
to Farming Simulator 15, Game resources and Settings & activity. The main view
shows a project scene preview, engine cards and a persistent bottom launch bar.
Choose **ReFarm (experimental)** for the authored reconstructed engine, or a GE6
profile for the installed original engine. Map/difficulty are ReFarm settings;
GE6 careers and maps are still selected inside the native game.

For the experimental native path without a Steam SDK dependency, use **Prepare
local GE6**, then choose **Local GE6 (experimental)** under Native startup.
See [the separate local-runtime requirements and limitations](LOCAL_ENGINE_RUNTIME.md).

![ReFarm selected in the redesigned launcher](screenshots/launcher-refarm.png)

## Prepare resources

1. Open **Game resources** and choose **Detect installation**, or browse to your FS15
   installation. Detection reads Steam libraries and app 313160 manifests, the
   `FS15_GAME_DIR` environment variable and this workspace's saved settings.
2. Choose **Prepare / repair assets**. Progress, errors and cancellation appear
   in the launcher. Keep the installation available until preparation finishes.
3. Return to **Farming Simulator 15**, choose ReFarm, map and difficulty, check the launch
   plan and launch. Build the Windows host first if diagnostics report it missing.

Preparation reuses the existing recovery pipeline. It verifies local archive and
source hashes, prepares original DEM/layer resources, decodes original map and
sky meshes, stages textures, samples recovered environment curves and prepares
original starting fleets and field grids. Matching source files are retained;
generated scene/vehicle caches are regenerated. No game assets are downloaded.
The installed game is read without being modified. Missing pinned LuaJIT,
decompiler or mesh tools are prepared through the existing setup scripts; these
may download third-party sources and require Git, Visual Studio C++ and the .NET
SDK/reference packs described in the build instructions.

Original resources and recovered scripts stay under ignored local `recovered/`.
`build/launcher/assets.json` records status, content hashes and preparation steps.
Interrupted/failed preparation blocks ReFarm startup until repaired. An
operating-system lock prevents concurrent preparations. Source copying uses a
verified temporary file and atomic replacement; interrupted temporary copies can
be repaired on the next run. Redirected output paths are rejected before staging.
Cancellation terminates the preparation process tree; rerun preparation to repair
unfinished generated caches.

**Check resources** is a required-file preflight, not a full integrity scan or
evidence of a rendered game session. Preparation rechecks archive/recovered
source hashes and records staged resource hashes. Separate engine tests verify
loading and rendering.

## Fresh-workspace extraction requirement

Archive decryption still uses the pinned **original native GAR oracle**, not an
independent recovered cipher. If extraction/recovery is missing, preparation needs
the locally captured FS15 **1.4.2.0 x64** analysis image. An absent/unsupported
image produces an explicit error. The launcher does not substitute placeholder
scripts/assets or capture a process as a side effect.

For a fresh workspace, start the installed game normally, then use the existing
read-only analysis tool while that game is running:

```powershell
$env:FS15_GAME_DIR = 'D:\Games\Farming Simulator 15'
python scripts/runtime_snapshot.py --game $env:FS15_GAME_DIR
# Then return to Resources > Prepare / repair assets.
```

The image stays in ignored `inputs/runtime/`; never publish it. A successful
resource import does not mean GE6 has been fully decompiled or recompiled.

The same operations are available without the GUI:

```powershell
python scripts/launcher_assets.py detect
python scripts/launcher_assets.py status
python scripts/launcher_assets.py prepare --game-dir $env:FS15_GAME_DIR
```

## Runtime selection and validation

GE6 baseline/hybrid modes use the installed original engine and its normal
startup requirements. GE6 uses installed assets in place. ReFarm uses
local prepared caches; the renderers run in separate processes. Native career/map
selection happens inside GE6; home mode uses the launcher's map and difficulty.
See [native integration limits](UNIFIED_LAUNCHER.md).

`--smoke-capture PATH` renders all three WinForms pages, both engine selections
and the compact layout, checks the custom profile menu and keyboard/accessibility
selection, and runs detection/preflight without starting a game. Adding `--smoke-prepare` also runs the real
preparation worker against the selected installation. Its JSON report distinguishes
preparation, UI rendering and game startup. Captures stay local and may contain
installation paths.

The two embedded banner images are existing rendered project screenshots; they
are labeled as ReFarm experimental captures. They do not imply original-GE6
rendering fidelity. No Minecraft assets or game-resource payloads are bundled.

For command-line startup, use `python scripts/unified_launcher.py --mode refarm`.
The existing `--mode home` command and `FS15EngineRebuilt.exe` filename remain
compatible. ReFarm is the name of the experimental engine, not the whole project.

# Linux x64 intermediate target

**Active porting path:** [original GE6 instruction startup](GE6_LINUX_NATIVE_BOOT.md).
The private original image has reached its original application entry under
Linux after CRT/global initialization. This is separate from the authored
frontend/physics/render fixtures described below. The unmodified-instruction
reference stops at the original application's unbound Steam restart import.
The existing modified Local GE6 input passes this boundary, loads configuration,
enters central initialization and writes the original engine journal. Linux
socket/timer/system/event and virtual-memory services now carry startup into the
original embedded Lua allocator. Two original workers now run with distinct
Linux stacks and TLS/FLS state. Staging unchanged integrity inputs and GAR files
advances startup through original physics/input logging to the next stop,
`OpenAL32.dll!alcOpenDevice`. This is startup evidence, not gameplay/input parity.
No original menu or
engine renderer has initialized through that Linux path yet.

An experimental graphical frontend is now also buildable as `FS15MenuLinux`.
Use the [Linux tester guide](LINUX_TESTER.md) to prepare a local package and
collect a friend's results. Public artifacts include only authored host code
and adapters; original menu resources/recovered game scripts stay local.
Linux CI uses authored fixtures. Original-resource desktop validation is pending.
The recovered [file-stream operations](FILE_STREAM_RECOVERY.md) now provide the
control flow around read-only POSIX resource loading for scripts, DDS/font data
and Linux XML input. This is bounded native behavior behind authored OS seams,
not a complete Windows API compatibility layer or a linked GE6 startup.
The [32 KiB buffered callbacks](BUFFERED_FILE_RECOVERY.md) are also recovered
and now sit above those disk methods in the frontend resource-read helper.
Recovered [memory-stream operations](MEMORY_FILE_RECOVERY.md) now also provide
the final borrowed-buffer read into the Lua script loader, without rewriting
resource bytes or changing their encoding.

Linux x64 is the next platform target while the native GE6 recovery continues.
The later Switch homebrew target remains deferred. This stage keeps recovered
native behavior and original-resource compatibility as its direction; it does
not replace GE6 with a newly authored game engine.

## Available executable

`FS15PortableHost` is an authored **headless portability host**, linked to the
recovered C++17 core. Its `--probe` path runs recovered Camera construction,
world-cache refresh, render-view construction, view/projection/shader-block
preparation, spatial grid allocation/registration, Camera-volume visibility,
registry-to-tire-force evaluation, render-view teardown and Camera destruction.
Allocator/registry/world/buffer transport is authored. Two CPU buffers now
follow the recovered driver allocation/destruction requests. See
[startup, 3D and physics scope](STARTUP_3D_PHYSICS.md).
The [recovered physics dispatcher/worker](PHYSICS_DISPATCH_RECOVERY.md) also now
executes 16 force-query steps on a real worker thread through authored portable
auto-reset events. [Native post-step and contact processing](PHYSICS_POST_STEP_RECOVERY.md)
now connect those steps through wheel readback to recovered scene TRS,
Camera/view, visibility and shader packing. Backend coordinates/contact groups
are fixture inputs. Full scene/solver creation and actual GPU drawing remain open.
Nine [recovered OpenGL buffer paths](GL_BUFFER_RECOVERY.md) now also build in
the core. The optional `FS15GLDriverCheck` uses an SDL context and actual GL
upload/map/readback/delete operations; it is separate from this headless host
and does not yet submit the original scene's draw calls.
The optional [GE6 physics backend](GE6_PHYSICS_BACKEND.md) now also builds
recovered GIANTS world/dispatcher/solver hooks over pinned upstream Bullet.
Its actual rigid-body/contact checks are separate from the older CPU fixture
probe. This introduces no ReFarm dependency and does not yet start the game.

The process checks balanced map/unmap, one visible and one outside object,
and zero retained allocations/registry entries after cleanup. It emits JSON
and exits nonzero on failure. This is a runnable Linux executable, but it does
not initialize the complete original engine, open a window, draw the menu,
load a playable map or implement GPU/physics/audio backends.

Source: [host](https://github.com/nat649/fs15-reconstruction/blob/master/src/portable/main.cpp). The recovered algorithms stay in
`src/core`; no additional native entries are claimed for this authored host.

## Build and install on Linux x64

Use a C++17 compiler and CMake 3.20 or newer:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build/linux-host \
  -DFS15_PORTABLE_CORE_ONLY=ON \
  -DFS15_BUILD_PORTABLE_HOST=ON \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build/linux-host --parallel
ctest --test-dir build/linux-host --output-on-failure
cmake --install build/linux-host --prefix "$PWD/build/linux-install"
./build/linux-install/bin/FS15PortableHost --probe
```

To include the graphical frontend, install `libsdl2-dev`, `libsdl2-image-dev`,
`libluajit-5.1-dev`, `libexpat1-dev` and `pkg-config`, then enable both
`-DFS15_BUILD_PORTABLE_SCRIPTS=ON` and `-DFS15_BUILD_LINUX_MENU=ON` in the same
configure command. `FS15MenuLinux` reuses `src/menu/main.cpp`, `render.cpp`,
XML/save adapters and the authored bootstrap; caller-supplied recovered Lua
still provides GUI behavior. SDL2/SDL2_image provide the Linux drawing, image
decode and window/input transport. This does not recover a native GE6 renderer.

The host uses no Windows APIs, Direct3D, original executables, game archives,
LuaJIT or GPU driver. It also builds on Windows for local verification. The
existing Windows GUI launcher and ReFarm are separate targets.

GitHub Actions builds and runs the installed Linux x64 executable, tests its
command line from another working directory and publishes an authored-only
`fs15-linux-x64-portable-host` workflow artifact. Download it from a successful
**Repository checks** run and extract the `.tar.gz` inside it:

```sh
tar -xzf fs15-linux-x64-portable-host.tar.gz
./bin/FS15PortableHost --probe --report probe.json
```

This workflow artifact is a portability tool, not a playable game release.
No original code image, recovered Lua or game resource is included.
The archive is built on the GitHub Ubuntu runner and uses its standard C/C++
runtime libraries. It includes `share/fs15-reconstruction/runtime-dependencies.txt`.
For a distribution with older runtime libraries, build locally rather than
assuming the CI binary is compatible.

## Optional local resource inspection

```sh
./bin/FS15PortableHost --probe \
  --game-dir "/path/to/your/Farming Simulator 15" \
  --report probe.json
```

The supplied directory must exist. The host reports presence and byte sizes
for `dataS.gar`, `dataS2.gar` and the two map I3D files. Missing files remain
explicit in the report. This is filesystem discovery only: file presence does
not prove a supported version, complete installation or successful scene load.
The host never copies or modifies those resources, and rejects a report path
inside that game directory. Original-resource version/hash verification and
full archive/scene loading remain separate recovery work.

## Script/XML and localization stage

`FS15ScriptHost` is a second headless executable. It runs a text-only subset
bootstrap using caller-supplied `class.lua`, `Utils.lua`, `I18N.lua` and local
localization XML. The original menu window and full `main.lua` do not execute.
The shared read-only XML/property and save-metadata adapters now build on Linux.
Windows keeps XmlLite; Linux uses **Expat**, a third-party decoder. This is
platform transport, not recovery of the native GE6 XML tokenizer.

Install LuaJIT development headers, Expat development headers and pkg-config
through your distribution. On Ubuntu these packages are `libluajit-5.1-dev`,
`libexpat1-dev` and `pkg-config`.

The prebuilt script executable needs the corresponding runtime packages
(`libluajit-5.1-2` and `libexpat1` on the CI Ubuntu distribution); they are not
bundled into the archive. The original CPU-only host keeps its earlier
standard C/C++ runtime dependencies. Add the script option when building:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build/linux-host \
  -DFS15_PORTABLE_CORE_ONLY=ON -DFS15_BUILD_PORTABLE_HOST=ON \
  -DFS15_BUILD_PORTABLE_SCRIPTS=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build/linux-host --parallel
./build/linux-host/src/portable/FS15ScriptHost --i18n-probe \
  --root "/path/to/your/local/reconstruction/workspace" --language en
```

The root supplies `recovered/lua/dataS/scripts/...` and
`recovered/gar/dataS/...`, or the equivalent `lua/...` and `assets/...`
directories in a prepared local package. Required missing files fail explicitly;
bytecode is rejected by the runtime. Sources and assets are never modified.
The JSON report labels input as caller-supplied text; it does not certify its
provenance simply because it has the expected filename.

Local Windows parity checks compare all 1,425 English texts, 165 descriptions,
seven menu labels and three conversion factors with the original compiled Lua
chunks. The reference-bytecode entry is test-only and is never installed.
Recovered `I18N.lua` is classified `syntax_only` by the earlier recovery manifest;
this comparison establishes these exercised outputs, not universal equivalence.

Linux CI uses independently authored Lua/XML fixtures, never uploaded game
assets. Its installed-host checks are separate from that local original-code
comparison. XML tests cover repeated zero-based paths, Unicode/entities/CDATA,
typed values, DTD rejection, size/depth limits and VM document cleanup. The
same tests exercise existing read-only save snapshots; mutations still reject.

The local French `descriptions_fr.xml` is rejected by strict XML parsing at
line 217 (adjacent attributes without whitespace). It remains unchanged. No
French runtime/parity success is claimed; native-tokenizer compatibility needs
separate recovery. The current validated original-resource language is English.

## Remaining Linux milestones

- Recover and link complete native subsystem startup and the script bootstrap.
- Implement platform transport for window/input, filesystem, threading/timing,
  GPU resources and audio while recovering the original engine consumers.
- Recover complete scene/resource loading and native renderer/physics lifetime.
- Run the recovered menu, then original maps, vehicles and farming sessions.
- Validate persistent save/reload and package a playable Linux build.

The existing 23 asset-free core tests cover bounded recovered components.
Linux host integration checks exercise the installed executable and filesystem
contract separately. Neither establishes complete GE6 gameplay or Switch
hardware compatibility.

# Experimental local GE6 runtime

The launcher now offers **Local GE6 (experimental)** under **Settings & activity
> Native startup**. This runs an isolated, modified copy of the original FS15
1.4.2.0 x64 runtime with an authored local platform adapter. It is separate from
**ReFarm**, and it is not a fully recompiled GE6 engine.

## Prepare and launch

1. Select the installed FS15 directory in **Game resources**.
2. Choose **Prepare local GE6**. Preparation needs the pinned local native
   analysis image, the recovered WheelsUtil source, CMake and MSVC x64. Original
   resources are copied into ignored `build/ge6-local`; allow several GB of space.
3. In **Settings & activity**, select **Local GE6 (experimental)** as Native startup.
4. Select a GE6 launch profile and choose **PLAY**. Choose Career/map inside GE6.

The existing original/Steam/direct modes and ReFarm remain available. Preparation
refuses a running FS15 session. Original installation files and normal personal
saves are not rewritten; the local mode has its own profile. Licensed `.dlc`
containers are excluded. The profile and restart-safe alias remain local.

```powershell
python scripts/prepare_local_engine.py --game-dir $env:FS15_GAME_DIR --activate-recovered
python scripts/unified_launcher.py --mode hybrid --transport local --game-dir $env:FS15_GAME_DIR
# Once prepared, inspect the command without starting another game:
python scripts/unified_launcher.py --mode hybrid --transport local --game-dir $env:FS15_GAME_DIR --dry-run
python scripts/verify_native_engine.py --local
```

File copies are hash checked. A private source/target size/mtime index avoids
rereading unchanged resource contents on subsequent preparations; changed files
are rechecked and repaired. Interrupted preparations retain an incomplete marker.
Executable/image and adapter hashes are checked separately. This cache is not a
continuous integrity monitor of every installed asset.

## Native and authored boundaries

The original normalized code image remains version/hash pinned and private. The
local image selects the discovered native CRT entry point, retires the original
Steam-only bootstrap wrapper and resolves the observed Steam import names to
`fs15_local.dll`. Only the local copy is changed. The adapter supplies bounded
local/no-op services for the 13 observed imports and a minimal utility table.
Client, user, apps and statistics interfaces are unavailable; initialization does
not pretend that a Steam session exists. No user ID, login, ownership or licensed
DLC entitlement is synthesized. Steam callbacks and achievements are unavailable;
gamepad text input falls back to an unavailable result.

This is a runtime integration experiment around **original native code**, not
recovered engine source. Original executables, snapshots, scripts, resources and
generated binaries stay out of Git. Only authored tooling/adapter code, aggregate
evidence and rendered screenshots are published.

## Observed result and limits

The local session reached the **original menu**, initialized GE6 **6.0.2**,
physics **5.9.4** and OpenGL, then loaded **Bjornholm** with its original HUD and
vehicles visible. The recovered-source probe passed **104 comparisons**, and all
three activated wheel helpers were called by native gameplay. Module inspection
found `fs15_local.dll` and **no Steam-named library** in the game process.
The authored adapter has no Steam or network-library imports.

Steam was already running on the machine and was left untouched. A launch with
the client completely closed has **not** been tested. The module/import checks
and adapter trace establish the exercised local code path; they do not establish
every possible game path. The first Gold DLC attempt correctly failed its license
check; the base-game test excludes that container. Steam services, licensed DLC,
multiplayer and complete save/reload/graphics-restart sessions remain unsupported
or unvalidated in this mode.

See [runtime evidence](../analysis/local-engine-validation.json) and
[recovered-helper evidence](../analysis/local-engine-script-validation.json).

`docs/LUA_RECOVERY.md`:

```md
# Lua recovery and rebuilt script package

## What was recovered

The local `dataS.gar` contains 470 compiled `.luc` chunks, all with the
standard `ESC LJ 02` header. Their debug data includes source paths, line
information, and local names. The generic loader's custom version-3
transform was identified, but none of these 470 chunks needed it.

The strict recovery pipeline uses the pinned [LJD checkout](https://github.com/Dr-MTN/luajit-decompiler)
listed in `analysis/lua-toolchain.json`. It disables the unsafe extra pass
and does not enable `catch_asserts`. Each output is compiled/loaded with the
pinned official [LuaJIT toolchain](https://github.com/LuaJIT/LuaJIT), built
for x64 with GC64 disabled. No game chunk is executed by these checks.

## Repeated literal adapter

The first pass produced 70 syntax failures. LJD's substitution logic reused
literal AST objects in sibling expressions; its writer tracks object identity
and omitted later occurrences. A call such as `emit(nil, nil, nil)` could
be written as `emit(nil, , )`.

`scripts/ljd_driver.py` clones primitive and constant leaf nodes during slot
substitution. It leaves the third-party checkout unchanged. The authored
fixture `tests/fixtures/repeated_literals.lua` is compiled, decompiled through
the adapter, and recompiled; its stripped bytecode matches exactly.

## Empty-table initialization adapter

LJD also folded later field assignments into empty-table constructors. For
example, `Probe = {}; Probe.value = observe()` became
`Probe = {value = observe()}`. The callback then ran before the global table
existed. This is a behavioral error, not just different bytecode formatting.

The adapter marks original `TNEW` instructions with a zero allocation hint,
keeps their table references during slot substitution, and prevents the later
constructor-filling pass from merging subsequent stores. Sized constructors
and `TDUP` templates keep their existing handling. The authored table fixture
checks global initialization order, local/nested fields and genuine templates.
It failed with the previous adapter and now matches the original bytecode.

This adds **54 exact matches**, including WheelsUtil, SpecializationUtil,
Plough, Mower, MixerWagon and TreePlanter. All 254 previous matches are retained.
These are script recovery results, not proof of complete native vehicle or
farming simulation in the gameplay host.

## Deterministic comparison

The pinned LuaJIT writer supports `string.dump(chunk, "sd")`: `s` strips debug
data and `d` writes template-table hash entries in deterministic order. The old
`true` argument stripped debug data but could randomly change a comparison
result across processes with the same source hash. Deterministic mode still
compares all instructions, constants, prototype ordering and upvalue metadata.
It does not normalize register allocation or control flow. Negative controls
reject changed constants, calls and allocation instructions, and ensure that
comparison never executes a chunk's top-level code.

All 470 outputs compile:

| Result | Files | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `exact_match` | 308 | Original and rebuilt chunks produce identical deterministic `string.dump(chunk, "sd")` output under the verification runtime |
| `syntax_only` | 162 | Source compiles and its bytecode loads, but the deterministic stripped dump differs; behavior remains unverified |

An exact match is a strong check for that chunk. A syntax-only result must
not be presented as behavioral equivalence. Differences may involve code
generation or actual reconstruction errors and require investigation.

## Built artifact

`scripts/compile_recovered_lua.py` checks each recovered source hash against
the recovery manifest, compiles it without executing its code, assigns a
portable `@dataS/...` chunk name, writes deterministic bytecode and rechecks the
compiled chunk's comparison status. It creates:

- `build/recompiled/dataS/`: 470 rebuilt chunks.
- `build/FS15ScriptsRebuilt.zip`: those chunks, a per-file build manifest,
  and a scope/validation notice.

The package is not automatically installed. It is a script-layer artifact,
not an independent native engine or a complete playable reconstruction.
Recovered sources, compiled chunks, and original assets are excluded from
Git; only tools and aggregate results are published.

`docs/MEMORY_FILE_RECOVERY.md`:

```md
# Native memory streams and Linux resource staging

The portable core now reconstructs six default memory-stream operations:

| Native entry | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `0x14006bc00` | Valid when the stored data pointer is nonnull |
| `0x14006bcf0` | Copy the remaining requested bytes, clamp at size and advance position |
| `0x14006bd50` | Clamp an absolute seek to size and return a boolean success |
| `0x14005f670` | Return the stored DWORD size, including with a null data pointer |
| `0x14006bc10` | Return position, or `0xffffffff` for a null data pointer |
| `0x14006bd60` | Compute EOF from size <= position; no sticky EOF byte |

The x64 record stores the data pointer at `+8`, ownership byte at `+0x10`, size
at `+0x14` and position at `+0x18`. These operations preserve ownership and
other record bytes. Unlike the disk reader, a memory seek above size clamps to
the end, and seeking back clears computed EOF. The original seek returns a
boolean in AL; undefined upper return-register bits are not treated as data.
Null data remains an invalid stream even for a zero-byte read. Size and EOF
queries retain their original independent behavior.

## Discovery and native evidence

Two observed memory-stream tables, `0x1404bbb38` and `0x1404d9ff8`, were audited
over twelve slots each. Six uncovered functions were catalogued without splitting
existing bodies. Four of those new entries are used by this component; two
shared constant-return methods remain analysis-only. Validity and read already
existed in the catalogue. The full local pseudocode export now covers 11,642
eligible functions out of 12,207 catalogue entries, with zero export failures.
This is analysis coverage, not complete buildable GE6 source.

The prior five scene tables retain their separate forty-slot audit. Memory and
scene vtable dependency roots are now reported separately. The complete native
dependency export and source-pinned reconstruction ledger were refreshed.

[Differential evidence](../analysis/memory-file-validation.json) records
**13,366 operations across 238 sequences** against unchanged original routines:
2,658 reads, 2,238 seeks, 2,030 validity queries, 1,950 size queries, 2,263
position queries and 2,227 EOF queries. Complete records, guarded output buffers
and unchanged source buffers match. Cases include empty buffers, embedded NULs,
short/end reads, rewinds, extreme unsigned seeks, nine null-data sequences and
four original local Lua/XML/font/DDS resources. Instruction dumps, original
bytes and detailed vectors remain local.

## Integration and limits

`ReadOnlyMemoryFile` is an authored borrowed-storage owner adapter around the
recovered operations. It never frees or modifies caller storage. An empty view
uses a stable empty byte so its validity does not depend on the C++ container's
empty-data-pointer choice. This initialization is not a recovered native factory.

The bounded script-read helper now feeds Lua through the disk stream, recovered
32 KiB buffered callbacks, then this memory stream. Recovered menu sources and
the script host both use this path. The existing string copy is performed by
the recovered reader without changing bytes or encoding. Bytecode remains
restricted to the separately labelled local parity oracle.

Authored envelope/capacity guards reject malformed records, position beyond size,
invalid spans and the original uint32 addition-overflow read case. Those cases
are outside the differential contract; arbitrary memory is not made safe by
these checks. Native factories/destructors, ownership transfer/free, GAR cipher,
archive providers, writes and full engine startup remain open. Loading the
frontend through these streams does not establish native GE6 Linux startup.

```powershell
python scripts/check_memory_file.py --dll build/linux-native-file/Release/FS15Core.dll
```

The native oracle needs the pinned local Windows analysis image. Portable core
and Linux integration tests use authored fixtures; original-resource Linux
desktop and full gameplay validation remain separate.

All twenty-seven asset-free component/transport tests pass on Windows x64,
Linux x64 and ARM64 Linux under QEMU. The Linux script-host and ten frontend/
tester checks also pass in
[CI run 39123910117](https://github.com/nat649/fs15-reconstruction/actions/runs/39123910117).
The original English menu and localization comparison pass separately on Windows.
Platform results and downloaded ELF/archive hashes are in the validation report.

# Reconstructed frontend milestone

`FS15MenuRebuilt.exe` is a newly compiled Windows GUI host. It executes

- `main.cpp`: LuaJIT source compilation in text-only mode, resource resolution,
  window/message loop, mouse/keyboard forwarding, logs and exit.

Required missing/corrupt resources cause startup errors instead of placeholders.

The runtime uses LuaJIT's pinned static library and normal Windows libraries.

Preparation creates `build/native-engine/profile` and a local script probe under

GE6's graphics restart was observed to lose quotes around a profile path with

directory junction under the temporary directory with a path without spaces.

pointing elsewhere is rejected. Profile data stays in the workspace. This
alias and its launch command were checked locally; a complete graphics restart
round trip through it remains pending. If the temporary directory itself has
spaces, the launcher reports an error instead of using an unsafe profile path.

## Validated native baseline (2026-10-15)

A normal Steam startup produced a fresh isolated log identifying **GIANTS
Engine Runtime 6.0.2 64bit**, physics **5.9.4**, and successful OpenGL
initialization. The original menu, Bjornholm loading completion and the player
HUD inside the world were observed. The native script loader executed the
