found in the captured log. See [aggregate evidence](../analysis/native-engine-validation.json).

These observations establish native engine use and recovered-source execution.
They do not establish complete reconstructed gameplay: original global game
classes still provide most of the playable simulation. The later hybrid check
on Westbridge Hills additionally activated `getTireType`, `getTireFriction` and
`getGroundType`, and recorded all three being called by native vehicles.

Preparation starts with `native_boot_verified=false` and

```powershell
python scripts/verify_native_engine.py
```

The verifier requires the native startup, renderer initialization and ordered
probe markers, rejects captured Lua errors, and rejects a log older than the
current launch request. It updates the private manifest and writes an aggregate
report containing hashes rather than profile paths or original code. Visual
gameplay checks remain separate from this log verifier.

## Recovered-source probe

The observed FS15 mod loader accepts `descVersion=21` and loads
`extraSourceFiles` through native `source(filename, modName)`. The generated
single-player probe captures the original WheelsUtil table, loads the recovered
WheelsUtil source into the isolated mod environment, and compares 104 pure
tire-friction/ground-classification cases. Original global gameplay classes
are not replaced by the baseline probe. Hybrid mode adds an authored activation
adapter after verification, replacing only three helper methods in that table.
Other native rendering/physics/gameplay services stay original. See the
[hybrid integration limits](UNIFIED_LAUNCHER.md#recovered-helpers-in-native-gameplay).

Start a career in the isolated profile, then start the mission. In the observed
single-player flow the local probe loaded automatically without a separate
mod-selection screen. Descriptor discovery at the main menu is insufficient:
`extraSourceFiles` execute during `MPLoadingScreen.initializeLoading`, before
specialization initialization and mission loading. Require both a fresh native
log containing `GIANTS Engine Runtime 6.0.2` and this script execution marker:

```text
FS15_NATIVE_RECOVERED_LUA_OK comparisons=104
```

That establishes only the exercised recovered helpers inside the real engine.
Further game-code replacement and complete session validation remain pending.

The authored fixture `tests/fixtures/native_engine_probe.lua` verifies source
ordering, mod isolation and those 104 comparisons against original bytecode in
the standalone verification VM. It is explicitly **not a native engine boot**.

## Native analysis supporting the entry point

- `0x14000c9a0` parses `-profile`. `0x14002ce80`, `0x14002cf00`,
  `0x14002c610` and `0x14002c880` resolve the supplied full profile directory.
- Recovered `main.lua` supports a profile-local mods directory and optional
  `gameSettings.modsDirectoryOverride`.
- Native `0x140280060` prefers same-basename `.luc` over `.lua`. The probe stages
  plain source with no neighboring `.luc`, letting the original engine compile it.
- The original startup loads `dataS/scripts/main.lua`. `-script`/`-base` occur in
  generic help strings, but parsing/working startup overrides are unverified.
- Original `main.lua` disables `loadfile`, `load` and `string.dump`. The probe
  uses the supported engine source path instead.

Modern-verifier bytecode matches do not establish compatibility of freshly
compiled `.luc` files with the older FS15 VM. Local source loading is the first
integration route. Original native code, recovered scripts, profile contents
and generated mod packages remain excluded from Git.

Wheel lookup comparisons use valid synthetic native registries. Missing-record

## Portable build

```powershell
cmake -S . -B build/portable-core -DFS15_PORTABLE_CORE_ONLY=ON
cmake --build build/portable-core --config Release
ctest --test-dir build/portable-core -C Release --output-on-failure
```

The C API is in `src/core/api.h`. Windows export attributes are isolated in one
header and disappear for the static portable build. The wheel object views
currently require 64-bit pointers and IEEE binary32 floats. RLE16 writes its
little-endian output explicitly; bit shifts use unsigned wrapping and masked
counts instead of depending on x64 instruction behavior. Host compilation and
tests are distinct from cross-compilation and execution on the Switch.

The CI workflow builds/tests this target on Linux without original resources.
The Windows DLL remains available for original-code differential comparisons.
No Switch toolchain or packaging target is configured yet. Homebrew `.nro` is
the selected future route; no console SDK contents are included.

The workflow also defines an **ARM64 Linux cross-build with QEMU user-mode
execution**. See the tested source revision, test counts and platform scope in
[platform evidence](../analysis/portable-core-platform-validation.json).
On a Linux host with `g++-aarch64-linux-gnu` and `qemu-user` installed:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build/arm64-core -DFS15_PORTABLE_CORE_ONLY=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=cmake/aarch64-linux-gnu.cmake
cmake --build build/arm64-core --parallel 2
ctest --test-dir build/arm64-core --output-on-failure
```

This checks a different CPU architecture with authored asset-free invariants.
It is not a libnx build, `.nro`, console execution or a second architecture's
original-code differential comparison. See [portability status](PORTABILITY_STATUS.md).

## Recovered scene component boundaries

`scene_math.h` documents the original affine lane order and **WXYZ** quaternion
order. Quaternion-to-matrix preserves translation and padding; scale extraction
retains the native near-unit snapping interval. Matrix inversion retains its
`1e-36f` determinant threshold. Instruction inspection corrected a pseudocode
addition-order ambiguity in the quaternion trace before validation passed.

`scene_graph.h` exposes a caller-owned native-layout node arena: parent pointer
at `+0x28`, flags at `+0x50`, local matrix at `+0x98` and cached world at `+0xd8`.
Only traversed dirty nodes update, clearing bit `0x40`. Parent pointers must
resolve to records in that arena. Cycle, truncated buffer and nonfinite guards
are authored additions; no original object allocator, dirty propagation, scene
loader, vtable callbacks or ownership lifecycle is reconstructed by this API.

The four Lua adapters retain numeric tag/value locations and unrelated frame
bytes. The original inverse adapters ignore an inversion failure and can read
uninitialized stack data; one singular generated chain was excluded rather than
executing that undefined path. The bounded API rejects it and preserves the frame.

ReFarm supplies its existing world matrices through a cached synthetic-node
bridge. This exercises recovered coordinate conversions without claiming native
scene lifecycle integration. Both original-map gameplay fixtures still match
source/bytecode, frame partitions and pause/resume in 24 host runs. See
[component evidence](../analysis/scene-core-validation.json).

The additional `scene_state.h` component recovers the base/TRS state dispatcher,
observer-presence propagation and the two matrix-setter variants. It supplies a
partial `0x170`-byte node layout, bounded pointer views and ordered notification
output. It does not execute arbitrary original vtables/callbacks or allocate
engine objects. Its staged failure guards and maximum descendant depth are
authored. See [state recovery scope and remaining lifecycle work](SCENE_STATE_RECOVERY.md).

The [TRS update component](SCENE_TRS_RECOVERY.md) recovers lazy cache refresh,
matrix rebuilding, the original origin-zero propagation call, and six complete
Lua setter/getter frames. Its matrix/Euler flow is recovered; trig and square-root
functions use platform libm, with a recorded numeric gate. ReFarm now uses these
recovered composition/affine routines for I3D node transforms and vehicle poses.

The [hierarchy component](SCENE_HIERARCHY_RECOVERY.md) recovers ordered scene
membership changes and their state/observer updates. Child vectors are bounded
caller-owned storage; native allocation/growth, constructors/destructors and
registry/resource ownership remain unresolved.

The [object lifecycle component](SCENE_LIFECYCLE_RECOVERY.md) recovers known
constructor, rename and destructor chains, including recursive owned children.
Allocator, ID/registry and known dispatch callbacks are authored services.
Shared resources, triggers, arbitrary derived classes,
singleton startup and native exception/concurrency behavior remain unresolved.

The [attribute component](SCENE_ATTRIBUTES_RECOVERY.md) extends those destructor
chains to valid nonempty maps. It retains native tree/string layouts and
script-frame semantics, including observed String-to-scalar allocation retention.
It does not recover shared resources, arbitrary derived teardown or full loading.

## Reconstructed tire-force component

`src/core/tire_forces.h` reconstructs the calculation at `0x1400c24c0`:
load smoothing, stiffness sensitivity, combined slip response, longitudinal and
lateral force, wheel torque and the aligning quantity. Parameter names/units
are inferred from wheel-record fields. The callable authored API rejects invalid
or non-finite inputs/results instead of exposing unchecked native memory.

`scripts/check_tire_forces.py` compares compiled C++ with the original routine
in **3,300 cases / 13,200 float outputs**. Cases cover zero/tiny slip, both signs,
pure/combined slip, load-ramp boundaries, the cosine transition and deterministic
random parameter combinations. Each output must satisfy
`abs(error) <= 2e-5 * max(1, abs(original))`. See [validation](../analysis/tire-forces-validation.json).

Only the inspected calculation and finite-input math helpers execute in an
isolated test process with synthetic wheel records. The oracle optionally maps
the original auxiliary `text` section for its cosine helper; no PE entry point,

local and is not a runtime dependency of the playable package.

This calculation is compiled into FS15Core but is **not yet used by gameplay**.
Original contact/load/slip data and the force-to-rigid-body bridge must be
recovered before replacing the temporary planar integrator reliably. The joint
and wheel interfaces remain separate outstanding work.

# Recovered physics dispatch and worker loop

Three more bounded GE6 paths now compile as platform-independent C++17:

| Original entry | Recovered behavior |
|---|---|
| `0x1400c7a60` | Active/busy/positive-delta gate, elapsed and capped clocks, milliseconds-to-seconds conversion, synchronous call or worker wake |
| `0x1400c3c50` | Scene simulation call, backend/world lookup, observation collection boundary |
| `0x1400c3b90` | Request wait, stop check, simulation/collection, pending-time clear, completion signal and next wait |

Sources: [core implementation](../src/core/physics_dispatch.cpp),
[native record/service interface](../src/core/physics_dispatch.h),
[authored event/thread transport](../src/platform/physics_worker.cpp).
These are runtime scheduling paths, not a reconstructed physics solver.

## Native ordering and record fields

The manager's supported fields retain their original offsets: scene at `+0x38`,
active flag at `+0xa8`, fixed-step value at `+0xb0`, unsigned iteration count at
`+0xb4`, two clocks at `+0xc0/+0xc8`, busy flag at `+0x448`, request/completion
events at `+0x478/+0x480`, pending seconds at `+0x488` and asynchronous flag at
`+0x48c`. Opaque manager fields remain unchanged.

An eligible dispatch adds the full delta to the elapsed clock. It adds the
smaller of the delta and `float(iterations) * fixed_step * 1000` to the capped
clock, marks busy, and multiplies the delta by the original binary32 `0.001`
constant. Asynchronous dispatch stores the converted value before signaling
the request event. Synchronous dispatch invokes the backend immediately.
Nonzero busy, inactive state or nonpositive delta leaves the record unchanged.

The worker first waits, then checks the stop byte. Each accepted wake calls
the scene's simulation slot with seconds, unsigned iterations and fixed-step
value. It then resolves the backend world and runs the observation collection
boundary. Only after collection does it clear pending seconds and signal
completion. Stop wakes do not simulate or signal completion through the native
loop. Event waits use the observed infinite timeout and non-alertable mode.

## Real event/thread transport

The portable transport owns a `std::thread` and two mutex/condition-variable
events. Their retained signal bit supplies auto-reset semantics: a signal sent
before a wait is retained, one successful wait consumes it, and repeated signals
coalesce. Calls are serialized with one outstanding request. Stop is published
through the request event and the thread is joined before backend data dies.
The idle request wait remains unbounded. A submitting caller has an authored
10-second completion watchdog; no original watchdog behavior is claimed.

The transport accepts caller-provided simulation/world/collection callbacks.
It does not create a native physics scene. Completion now runs the recovered
[post-step/contact/wheel paths](PHYSICS_POST_STEP_RECOVERY.md), which replace
the earlier authored busy-flag acknowledgement. Full manager/scene creation,
controller movement, successful native deletion and the solver remain open.

`FS15PortableHost --probe` now runs **16 dispatched steps** on a distinct worker
thread. Its backend evaluates the recovered wheel-registry/tire-force adapter
using authored fixture records, verifies result tags, and collects completion.
The JSON reports this CPU path separately from `physics_world_started=false`,
`native_engine_started=false`, `renderer_started=false` and `playable=false`.
There is no gravity/contact/body simulation substituted behind those flags.

## Validation

[The native comparison](../scripts/check_physics_dispatch.py) executes the three
unchanged original bodies in the pinned local Windows image. Complete manager
and guard bytes plus ordered scene/world/event snapshots match:

- **3,072 dispatch states**: 2,660 ignored gate states, 287 asynchronous signals
  and 125 synchronous steps;
- **1,024 standalone synchronous states**, including unsigned iteration counts
  above `INT32_MAX` and the original floating-point conversion order;
- **512 complete worker lifetimes**, including stop before the first step and
  **2,044 completed steps** before stop.

The original observation collector runs only its empty-list path in these
fixtures. Its nonempty contact processing is covered separately by the
[post-step/contact comparison](PHYSICS_POST_STEP_RECOVERY.md). The backend solver and OS waits/signals are explicit seams;
original machine code, pseudocode and raw records stay local.

[Portable component fixtures](../tests/physics_dispatch.cpp) check native gate,
clock and callback order plus authored short-record, nonfinite-input and service
failure guards. Unlike the original code's ignored OS return values, authored
services stop on failure and retain preceding native mutations.
[Thread transport fixtures](../tests/physics_worker.cpp) check 24 real thread
lifetimes, completion counts, zero-step stops, repeated stops, rejected ticks
after shutdown, and backend failure without false completion success.
See the [source-pinned aggregate evidence](../analysis/physics-dispatch-validation.json).

Graphics-driver creation, full physics scene creation, collision detection,
constraint solving, rigid-body integration, controller/deletion services
and complete game startup remain unfinished.

All **30 component/transport CTests** pass on Windows x64, Linux x64 and
ARM64 Linux under QEMU. The installed Linux host passes six integration
checks including the 16-step worker probe, alongside six script-host and
ten frontend/tester checks. [CI evidence](https://github.com/nat649/fs15-reconstruction/actions/runs/39140990548).
These fixtures contain no original resources and do not validate a full

[native comparison](../scripts/check_physics_post.py),

## Ordering and ownership

Asynchronous finalization waits for worker completion before reading results.
It finalizes registered objects in native tree order, updates wheels, delivers
contact transitions, then removes inactive pending items using the last element
to fill each gap. It clears busy last. The native synchronous branch clears
busy before callbacks. The thread transport now calls this recovered routine
instead of clearing busy itself. Failed finalization cannot count as a
completed frame or be silently retried against partial state.

The pending callback's third argument is a **float in XMM2**, confirmed in the
original instructions. Owner IDs are reloaded after callbacks, and pending
count/storage are reloaded after cancellation because it can compact or replace
the queue. The decompiler's untyped 32-bit value does not establish that ABI.

Wheel updates preserve source fields and opaque bytes. Point/normal copies,
contact flag checks and the translated frame-basis product retain native order.
Position's fourth lane is zero. Actor-frame lookup is an explicit service;
`atan` uses an optional original math boundary or platform libm. This does not
generate wheel load, slip or contact response.

The contact collector consumes backend groups. Indexed contacts select the
proper endpoint column and wrap byte selectors through their low five bits.
Nonindexed contacts test whether groups contain contacts. The reusable group
count resets while its pointer/capacity remain. Contact finalization matches
ordered endpoint IDs through native hash chains, emits entered/departed/retained
bits in order, and preserves suppression, part IDs and listener short circuiting.
History growth uses native capacity and 16-byte alignment. The host tracks its
allocations and releases them after joining; caller-supplied buffers retain
their ownership contract.

Bounds, finite-input checks, cycle limits and service/allocation failure handling
are authored guards. Errors can retain preceding callbacks and mutations; no
transaction across services is promised. All traversed pointer graphs, part
arrays and group row spans must be valid caller-owned storage.

## Connected CPU probe

`FS15PortableHost --probe` performs 16 real worker-thread steps with recovered
force queries and contact collection through an authored backend fixture. It
then runs native post-step order on a nonempty wheel registry/contact history,
delivers 16 enter/stay/leave events, binds wheel positions to recovered scene TRS,
and prepares Camera matrices, frustum, shader block and visibility queries.
Including the initial state, it checks **17 scene/view/visibility/upload frames**
before joining and releasing resources.

The binding and backend coordinates/groups are authored test inputs, not a
recovered vehicle specialization or a substitute solver. Wheel, scene, Camera,
packed shader positions and visibility must agree. JSON retains
`native_engine_started=false`, `physics_world_started=false`,
`renderer_started=false` and `playable=false`.

- 512 contact collector states, including 455 nonempty pair lists and 3,577
  ordered backend lookup/group calls;
- 1,536 notification-policy states and 768 contact-history lifetimes;
- 256 full post-step manager states with contact history and pending callbacks,
  including cancellation against an empty native registry.

Native post-step fixtures use empty object/wheel registries; separate native
wheel-registry comparisons and connected portable fixtures cover the nonempty

## Work required before a complete port

1. Extend the recovered partial scene layout and base/TRS propagation with
   allocation/destruction, remaining derived vtables, callbacks and ownership.
   The [state component](SCENE_STATE_RECOVERY.md) supplies bounded caller-owned
   memory and notification events, not native scene construction.
   Ordered [link/reparent/unlink](SCENE_HIERARCHY_RECOVERY.md) is recovered for
   preallocated vectors; native allocation and object lifetime remain open.
   [Supported lifetime chains](SCENE_LIFECYCLE_RECOVERY.md) now run through
   authored allocator/registry/dispatch services. Native-layout
   [nonempty attributes](SCENE_ATTRIBUTES_RECOVERY.md) are supported; shared
   resources, triggers, complete scene ownership and native startup remain open.
2. Recover the resource lifecycle, archive decoding without an original-code
   oracle, complete I3D scene loading and original terrain/density services.
3. Recover and link subsystem startup and scripting, following the observed
   dependencies and resolving virtual/callback targets instead of fabricating
   replacement implementations for unknown services.
4. Recover rendering/material behavior and physics world, bodies, shapes,
   joints, suspension and drivetrain, keeping original middleware boundaries
   explicit. ReFarm's Direct3D renderer and temporary planar physics do not
   fulfill these items.
5. Supply the chosen platform's filesystem, threading, timing, input, graphics,
   audio and required networking interfaces. Windows/OpenGL/Direct3D/OpenAL
   imports identify only part of this work; dynamic symbols and statically
   linked services need separate recovery.
6. Configure libnx/devkitPro packaging, then validate hardware startup, menu,
   maps, vehicles, farming and persistent save/reload sessions. This stage
   remains deferred; no complete GE6 ARM64 or Switch executable is available.

The full engine is **not yet decompiled into buildable portable source**.
Pseudocode export completeness and bounded component counts are not completion
percentages. Original executable bytes, raw graph/pseudocode details, recovered
game sources and original resources remain local.

## Original engine components

The installed x64 runtime contains the game executable plus Steam and OpenAL
libraries. A standalone GIANTS Engine 6 renderer DLL was not found there.
The SDK includes GIANTS Editor 6.0.3 installers; they are additional local
references for editor/engine behavior, not a rebuilt game executable.

Native code analysis traced `externalShapesFile` loading through
`0x1401866c0`, the cipher-state constructor `0x14029f350`, the stream reader
`0x14029f490` and its buffer routine `0x1402b3fa0`. The native routine is
already reused directly as a local oracle. The comparison harness uses only
the pinned analysis image and does not inject into a running game.

The native entry point now uses the installed original engine with a separate
profile. The recovered WheelsUtil source runs through its supported script
loader and passes 104 helper comparisons. The original menu and Bjornholm were
observed in the actual engine. Hybrid mode now additionally replaces three
wheel helper methods after parity checks; native vehicle calls to all three
were recorded. Most original game code and all original native engine services
remain in use. Wider code replacement and full session validation remain
separate milestones. The experimental host remains useful for fixtures.

Original executable/code bytes, decoded geometry, textures and recovered Lua
stay local. GitHub contains authored code, dependency provenance/licenses,
aggregate validation and selected rendered screenshots.

## Next reconstruction targets

The [native recovery report](NATIVE_RECOVERY.md) records full-export scope,
catalogue limits and 498 observed native scripting descriptors. Wheel creation, property
updates, slip lookup, tire forces and differential dispatch are now traced to
native entry points; their full services are not integrated yet.

Recover the remaining native physics/density interfaces, original component
joints, complete specialization startup and persistent sessions. Restore full
terrain/crop material behavior, density placement, distance-based LOD, shadow
cascades and tree skeletons. The current [gameplay subset](GAMEPLAY_RUNTIME.md)
keeps authored physics/contact/trigger approximations explicit.
Validate placement, rendering and gameplay separately as those components land.

`docs/SCENE_ATTRIBUTES_RECOVERY.md`:

```md
# Recovered native scene attributes

Eight additional native paths now have portable reconstructed code. Attribute
storage retains the original `0x50`-byte red-black-tree nodes, `0x10`-byte tagged
values, sentinel links, colors and observed key-string layout. This component
does not replace the tree with an unrelated authored key/value dictionary.

| Native entry | Recovered path |
|---|---|
| `0x1400246f0` | Case-sensitive byte-key lookup and value-pointer result |
| `0x140136870` | Find an existing value or allocate/insert a zero-initialized value; existing kind is retained |
| `0x140136980` | Allocate a native-layout entry and copy its inline/heap key |
| `0x14027e1c0` | Attach, update extrema/count and rebalance the observed red-black tree |
| `0x1400e6900` | Lua getter frame, exact result tag and partial value writes |
| `0x1400e69b0` | Lua setter frame, type dispatch and integer conversion |
| `0x14016edc0` | Replace text storage and update value kind |
| `0x1401365f0` | Release attribute values, key strings, tree nodes and the map sentinel |

## Storage and script semantics

Keys compare unsigned bytes and preserve case. Up to 15 key bytes fit inline;
longer keys allocate the observed `(length | 15) + 1` buffer. String padding,
unused value bytes and node padding remain unchanged. Native allocator and
exception internals are not recovered by these routines; allocation uses the
existing authored platform service. Temporary lookup-string allocation is not
reproduced, since the original key comparison can read the supplied bounded
bytes directly. Normal lookup results and tree contents retain native behavior.

The setter recognizes exactly `Boolean`, `Integer`, `Float` and `String`.
Unknown type names leave the map unchanged. Boolean writes preserve the input
byte, not just zero/one. Integer input with the original integer tag copies its
32 bits; other tags follow observed `CVTTSS2SI`, including `INT_MIN` for NaN or
out-of-range input. Floats preserve their 32-bit representation. Getter tags and
write widths match the original: bool 1 byte, integer/float 4 bytes and text
pointer 8 bytes. Missing/null getters clear only the result tag.

The original setter can retain an allocation when changing a String to a scalar:
it overwrites only the scalar bytes and kind without freeing the previous text.
**1,177 such retained allocations were observed** in these fixtures. Upper
bytes can also retain part of the former pointer. This behavior is preserved
and reported; it is not hidden under a leak-free claim. The owning allocation
context must track/reclaim those blocks separately. Full-map cleanup frees text
for kind 3, while kind 4 is returned as text but is not freed by that cleanup.
Replacement through the text setter has its separately observed ownership rules.

## Lifetime integration and guards

The recovered object destructor chains now accept valid **nonempty** attribute
maps and call recovered cleanup before releasing observers/children/name state.
Cleanup first frees values in key order, then releases key strings and tree
nodes in the original right-subtree/left-chain order, followed by the sentinel.
The public clear operation can instead retain/reset the sentinel for reuse.

Bounds on input strings/frames, tree validation, depth checks, rejection of
self-aliasing text replacement and cleanup after failed staged allocation are
authored guards. They are not claims about native malformed-input handling or
C++ exception unwinding. These low-level APIs require valid owned member
pointers. They do not parse arbitrary untrusted addresses. Individual map-entry
erasure, remaining shared resources, active trigger cleanup,
remaining derived objects and full scene loading remain separate recovery work.

ReFarm's object ownership and resource loader remain authored. This component
is not evidence that the entire engine or a console executable is rebuilt.

## Evidence

- **12,600 setter frames** and **25,200 getter frames** match the original.
- **12,780 complete tree comparisons**, covering **218,914 entry observations**,
  include topology, colors, key capacity/buffers, values and opaque padding.
- **25,200 original getter calls directly consume reconstructed trees**. The
  original code reads the portable component's actual native-layout storage;
  there is no intermediate dictionary or marshalled lookup result.
- 360 additional ensure-existing/kind-4/unknown-kind frames and 180 null-owner
  getter/setter pairs validate the remaining observed frame branches.
- **180 nonempty-map destructor and complete member-free-order traces** match.
  Residual allocations are checked explicitly against the observed native
  String-to-scalar retention and kind-4 behavior, then reclaimed by the fixtures.
- A seventh asset-free CTest checks sorted insertion/balance, conversion and
  frame invariants, sentinel reuse, destructor integration, malformed-map
  rejection, allocation-failure cleanup and the retained-text behavior.
- All twenty-three portable-core tests pass on Windows x64, Linux x64 and ARM64 Linux
  under QEMU. The original-code comparisons remain Windows-only. These checks
  do not validate a complete engine or Switch executable.

Addresses are normalized between the two independent allocations. Scalar
pointer residues are first checked against their actual originating allocation,
then normalized; unrelated value bytes remain exact. The Windows oracle uses
the existing private-heap native reference without running the game entry point
or modifying a live process. Original code and raw allocations stay local.

See [native evidence](../analysis/scene-attributes-validation.json),
[lifetime scope](SCENE_LIFECYCLE_RECOVERY.md),
[platform results](../analysis/portable-core-platform-validation.json) and
[remaining porting work](PORTABILITY_STATUS.md).

```powershell
python scripts/check_scene_attributes.py --dll build/native-recovery/Release/FS15Core.dll
cmake --build build/portable-core --config Release
ctest --test-dir build/portable-core -C Release --output-on-failure
```

The later [scene-copy component](SCENE_CLONE_RECOVERY.md) recovers typed value
cloning and whole-map assignment, including self-copy and kind-4 retention.

`docs/SCENE_CAMERA_RECOVERY.md`:

```md
# Native Camera recovery

Nine additional bounded GE6 paths are compiled in the portable C++17 core.
The reference is the pinned local x64 analysis image, SHA-256
`6d1beaf9d7e3c57dd51cec03385a53bda82b4ac946e622d8d2fa592a56d71f9f`.
The native comparison process maps this image privately and calls original code
without starting its entry point or modifying the live game. Allocator, registry,
owned-forest and callback transport around the recovered algorithms is authored.

| Native entry | Recovered path |
|---|---|
| `0x140052540` | Three-vector normalization using the native reciprocal square-root table |
| `0x1400b5870` | Camera constructor |
| `0x1400b5910` | Deleting/nondeleting destructor wrapper |
| `0x1400b59f0` | World pose to parent-relative Euler rotation and translation |
| `0x1400b5be0` | Follow a target along the normalized camera world Z axis |
| `0x1400b5d00` | Smooth the target point before applying the follow offset |
| `0x1400e8840` | Script-frame camera creation |
| `0x1400e8940` | Script-frame smooth-follow adapter |
| `0x14018c430` | Decoded I3D Camera begin callback |

The existing constructor, TRS, common XML, hierarchy, state and non-shape end
paths are reused; they are not counted again. See
[source-pinned evidence](../analysis/scene-camera-validation.json).

## Object and inherited dispatch

The Camera occupies `0x190` bytes. Its first `0x170` bytes are the recovered TRS
node. The constructor calls the typed TRS constructor with class `0x16`, adds
type flag `0x8000` and installs identity token `0x1404c1078`. These identity
addresses are never invoked as C++ vtables in the portable core.

| Offset | Field / native initialization |
|---|---|
| `+0x170` | FOV, stored directly in degrees |
| `+0x174` / `+0x178` | Near/far clip parameters |
| `+0x17c` | Orthographic height |
| `+0x180` / `+0x184` | Unknown fields, initialized to `0.1` / `3.0` |
| `+0x188` | Orthographic byte, preserved without canonicalizing direct constructor inputs |
| `+0x189..18f` | Untouched opaque bytes |

The eight inspected Camera slots inherit the same link/unlink, base state,
observer, LOD-marker/token and TRS matrix-setter bodies already recovered.
The owned view therefore dispatches Camera as TRS kind `1`, preserving its
derived tail. Known-table guards now accept Camera when traversing a branch
or inherited LOD token. The fixture checks a Camera with an attached LOD child:
camera motion reaches the descendant's world position in the LOD manager.
Recursive destruction dispatches the Camera wrapper and releases its ordinary
TRS members; no additional camera-owned allocation was observed here.

At the Camera milestone, four constructor-observed tables exposed 32 slots
and 14 distinct targets. The later [Light audit](SCENE_LIGHT_RECOVERY.md)
extends the total to five tables, 40 slots and 17 targets. The five earlier discovery records remain retained; the
Camera audit created no new functions. This is not exhaustive class discovery.

## XML and script inputs

The I3D callback ignores missing/null first `name` matches. All attribute
searches start at attribute zero and retain the first exact-case match. This
was checked against instructions because decompiler loop restructuring
misleadingly suggested that `fov` might skip the first attribute.

XML defaults are FOV `60`, near `0.1`, far `1000`, orthographic false and height
`1`. Scalar parsing uses the recovered scene numeric grammar. Orthographic is
true only for case-insensitive `true`. Common attributes use physics `0`, source
ID registration `1` and joint `0`; `dynamic`/`joint` attributes do not create body
or joint metadata on these nodes. Construction precedes common attributes,
ordered append and current-parent update. Camera end uses the existing
non-shape callback.

The callback API shares the group ownership contract: after successful
construction the caller owns the returned node even when registration,
attribute processing or attachment later fails. A completed prefix is not
rolled back. Constructor allocation failures clean acquired members before the
raw record is released. Derived lifecycle dispatch must remain supported.

The creation script frame holds name at `+0`, FOV at `+0x10`, near at `+0x20`
and far at `+0x30`. It creates a perspective camera with orthographic height
`1`. The follow frame holds target XYZ at `+0/+0x10/+0x20`, distance at `+0x30`,
alpha at `+0x40` and factor at `+0x50`. A null camera is a successful no-op.
The APIs add explicit frame/string bounds and leave input frame bytes intact.

## Pose and follow ordering

With a parent, pose refreshes its world matrix, initializes an inverse to
identity and attempts the recovered affine inverse. GE6 ignores inverse
failure; a singular parent therefore retains identity. It multiplies this
inverse by the requested world pose and extracts Euler angles without a scale
argument. A parentless camera uses the requested pose directly.

The camera's existing scale is retained. After a lazy TRS refresh if needed,
the function stores rotation and rebuilds/propagates. It then refreshes again
if necessary, stores translation and performs a second rebuild/propagation.
Collapsing these two updates would change callback and descendant ordering.

Follow copies the current world matrix, normalizes lanes `8..10`, replaces its
translation with `target + axis * distance`, then calls pose. Normalization
reuses the recovered seed-table initialization and performs the same two double
precision refinement steps. Zero vectors retain native zero results.

Smoothing first evaluates the camera origin through the world matrix, preserving
the original multiply/add order. For squared distance `d2 > 0.001`, it computes
`alpha = ((d2 * factor + (1 / d2) * 0.00065) * (1 / d2)) * alpha`, subtracts the
scaled displacement from that origin, and calls follow. These constants are
checked directly against the pinned image. No replacement camera-control model
is substituted for this behavior.

## Validation and remaining boundaries

The Windows native differential suite passes:

- 2,000 bit-exact vector normalizations;
- 200 direct constructors, 200 script creations and 400 complete lifetimes;
- 127 Camera XML creations, two ignored begins and 129 complete forest lifetimes;
- 381 pose, 381 follow, 381 smoothing and 381 script-follow updates;
- 1,653 complete forest states / 6,608 node records, including 18 parentless
  cameras, singular parents, retained non-unit scale, gimbal cases and 127
  exact/below-threshold smoothing inputs;
- six original camera attribute sets from both original maps, Deutz Agrostar
  and New Holland T8 resources, exercised in isolated synthetic parent fixtures.

Original camera attributes are retained; these isolated fixtures are not
complete original scene loads. Pointer fields are normalized for comparison,
opaque bytes are checked and transform/libm tolerance is `2e-5`. The asset-free
portable test also covers Camera-to-LOD updates, script frames, nonfinite guards

```md
# Scene attribute, property and node copy recovery

Seven additional bounded native paths now compile in `FS15PortableCore`.
They recover the shared copying behavior used below the original scene clone
dispatcher, including Camera and LOD wrappers. This is not yet the complete
recursive scene clone/remapping pipeline or a complete vehicle loader.

| Entry | Recovered behavior |
|---|---|
| `0x14016eea0` | Allocate and clone one typed attribute value |
| `0x1401366d0` | Clear destination attributes and copy source entries in key order |
| `0x1401279d0` | Clone rigid-body property metadata into a new detached record |
| `0x140149a60` | Clone joint property metadata into a new detached record |
| `0x14010fd80` | Copy common TRS-node state, properties and attributes |
| `0x1400b5950` | Construct a fresh Camera and apply the common copy |
| `0x1400d7ca0` | Construct a fresh LOD group and apply the common copy |

The default-property clone, constructors, attribute RB insertion/cleanup,
TRS refresh/rebuild, state propagation and supported owned/LOD services were
already recovered and are reused without counting their entries again.
Plain TRS allocation plus common copy is exposed through authored known-type
dispatch; this does not mark the larger original `0x1401b9d70` dispatcher as
recovered. See [source-pinned native evidence](../analysis/scene-clone-validation.json).

## Preserved copy semantics

Attribute values start with a zero 64-bit payload and the source type.
Boolean copies one byte, integer/float copy four bytes, and string kinds `3`
and `4` allocate independent terminated text. Unknown kinds retain their type
and a zero payload. Opaque `+0xc` bytes remain untouched, rather than being
copied from the source.

Map assignment destroys existing destination values/keys and reinserts source
entries in sorted order using the native RB tree behavior. Tree topology,
colors, key capacities/spare bytes and value allocation contents match the
reference. It is not a dictionary conversion or a raw pointer copy. Native
self-assignment clears the map. Kind `4` text is duplicated, but the original
map cleanup still does not release it; the fixtures track those retained
allocations separately and reclaim them explicitly. Ownership quirks are not
silently replaced with different semantics.

Rigid-body cloning constructs default metadata with the new owner, merges
source flags, clears the native low state bits, copies collision/material and
damping fields, clamps density to the native minimum and clears its override
flag. Optional center-of-mass fields copy only when source flag `0x8000` is set.
Solver iterations copy, the final change mask is zero, and backend/attachment
fields remain freshly initialized. Unknown fields that the original clone
does not copy retain their constructor/default/opaque state.

Joint cloning copies projection/drive values, per-axis limits, break values
and the observed byte at `+0x80`. Source flags merge with constructor defaults,
then low state bits clear. Manager/constraint pointers and observer bindings
are not copied. Neither property path duplicates a live PhysX actor or joint.
Native trigger flags can remain in copied metadata; active-trigger teardown
still requires unrecovered services and remains a separate boundary.

The common node copy preserves this order:

1. Refresh the source's lazy TRS cache if dirty; copy nine cached floats.
2. Clear the target cache-dirty bit and rebuild/propagate its transform.
3. Copy flag `0x20`, clone the source property and destroy/replace the target property.
4. Apply each changed clip value separately with propagation mask `8`, then
   each changed local mask with `0x10` / `0x20`, all with origin zero.
5. Apply visibility and propagate mask `2` if changed; copy flag `4`.
6. Replace the attribute map.

Destination identity, class/table, name, child ownership and shared-animation
binding remain its existing state. A clone wrapper obtains a new registered
object/ID through its constructor and copies the source name. It does not
copy the source's child vector or its animation binding. Existing target
children remain attached when copying into an existing node.

The LOD wrapper infers its distance count by scanning from the second slot
with a previous value initialized to zero. A fully distinct four-slot array
therefore produces count `3`: `(0,10,20,30)` clones as `(0,10,20,20)`. A second
slot equal to zero produces count `1` and constructor defaults. This behavior
is retained from the instructions instead of replacing it with a four-float
memcpy. Camera cloning copies only the constructor's projection parameters
before the common TRS copy; opaque/default tail fields are freshly initialized.

## Ownership and validation

The C API uses authored allocator, registry, owned-forest and propagation
callbacks; stable native vtable addresses are identity tokens, never callable
tables in the portable binary. `constructed` registers a fresh record with
the caller's owned view before common copy callbacks run. After successful
construction, the result remains caller-owned even if a later step fails.
Completed prefix mutations and registry effects are not rolled back.

Known default, detached body and detached joint target properties can be
replaced. Trees/pointees must be valid owned storage; distinct owners must not
share member allocations. Bounds/finite/allocation guards and failure cleanup
are authored. Native exception unwinding and temporary CRT string allocations
are not reproduced. This component copies supported single records; original
top-level clone finalization, unsupported derived resources, backend observers,
shared-animation rebinding and complete loading remain open.

The private Windows native reference calls unchanged code from the pinned image
without starting its entry point or altering a running game. Comparisons cover:

- 1,800 complete attribute-value clones, including strings and unknown kinds;
- 900 complete default/body/joint property clones;
- 270 map assignments, 90 self-assignments and 90 complete map lifetimes;
- 1,344 observed retained kind-4 text allocations in the map fixtures;
- 270 copies into existing scene nodes, 90 self-copies, 30 Camera and 30 LOD clone wrappers;
- 600 complete forest states, 2,580 node records and 2,940 complete tree comparisons;
- 90 complete cloned LOD-manager allocations and 90 complete scene lifetimes.

Complete record/property/tree bytes are checked after pointer normalization;
transform/libm tolerance is `1e-5`. Child-vector contents/capacities and names
are compared separately. The portable test loads its source through recovered
I3D group/Camera callbacks, validates independent attribute storage and LOD
distance behavior, and exercises allocation failures with owned-prefix cleanup.
All twenty-three portable tests pass on Windows x64, Linux x64 and ARM64 Linux
under QEMU. All 28 native differential suites pass on Windows. Platform
validation is tracked in [the separate report](../analysis/portable-core-platform-validation.json).

```powershell
cmake --build build/native-recovery --config Release --target FS15Core
python scripts/check_scene_clone.py --dll build/native-recovery/Release/FS15Core.dll
cmake --build build/portable-core --config Release
ctest --test-dir build/portable-core -C Release --output-on-failure
```

Original executables, raw pseudocode and allocation snapshots stay local.
This milestone does not recover projection/rendering, full startup or a Switch
executable; the [remaining port work](PORTABILITY_STATUS.md) still applies.

The later [recursive clone component](SCENE_CLONE_TREE_RECOVERY.md) adds native
pointer remap storage, clone-list allocation and known TRS/Camera/LOD/Light subtree
assembly. Top-level shape/skin/resource finalization remains open.

```md
# Recursive scene cloning and pointer remapping

Seven further native entries now have bounded reconstructed paths in the
portable C++17 core. This milestone connects the recovered single-record copy
to native-order subtree traversal, owned attachment, pointer remapping and
clone-list storage. It does not recover the complete top-level scene-clone
finalizer, skin/animation rebinding or unsupported derived resource classes.

| Entry | Recovered behavior |
|---|---|
| `0x1401ba050` | Allocate a `0x30`-byte original-to-clone map candidate |
| `0x14016ea00` | Unique insertion, consuming duplicate candidates without replacing values |
| `0x14016eb20` | Pointer-keyed RB tree attachment, rotations and recoloring |
| `0x140096190` | Recursive map-node cleanup in descending unsigned-key order |
| `0x140088360` | Clone-list pointer-vector reservation |
| `0x140320740` | Clone-list 1.5x growth when an append needs space |
| `0x1401b9d70` | Recursive clone dispatcher on known TRS, Camera, LOD and Light branches |

Existing constructors, single-record copy, typed attribute/property cloning,
hierarchy dispatch and pointer-vector algorithms are reused. Distinct native
vector template instantiations are compared directly; they share portable
allocation logic with the already recovered vector implementation. No existing
entry is counted twice. See [source-pinned evidence](../analysis/scene-clone-tree-validation.json)
and [single-record copy](SCENE_CLONE_RECOVERY.md).

## Remap layout and ownership

The map header has an opaque word at `+0`, sentinel pointer at `+8` and count
at `+0x10`. Each node holds left/parent/right pointers, source at `+0x18`, target
at `+0x20`, color/nil bytes at `+0x28/+0x29` and untouched padding. Source keys
compare as unsigned 64-bit pointer values. Insertion preserves native topology,
extrema, colors and duplicate behavior. The candidate factory initializes only
observed fields; it does not zero opaque bytes or the sentinel payload.

Initialization and whole-map release are authored C entry points around the
observed setup/free sequence. Releasing the map frees map nodes and optionally
its sentinel, never the mapped scene objects. Clone-list storage also owns
only its pointer allocation. Scene allocations remain owned by the constructor
callback and recovered lifetime services.

The comparison suite checks standalone maps with identical numeric keys on
both sides, including zero, maximum unsigned and high-bit keys. Exact topology
comparison is meaningful there. Scene source addresses differ across the two
heaps, so their numeric ordering and resulting tree topology may differ. Those
scene remaps compare normalized original-to-clone associations. Original GE6
lookup code additionally consumes the reconstructed map storage directly.
Cleanup ordering is checked against descending unsigned keys in each heap.

## Native traversal and attachment

The recovered dispatcher first searches the original-to-clone map. An already
mapped source returns null and performs no clone or attachment; it does not
return the previous target. A fresh supported source is handled in this order:

1. Dispatch by native type flags and run the known constructor/copy wrapper.
2. Insert the original address and new clone into the remap map.
3. Append the new clone to the pointer vector, retaining native capacity/spares.
4. Traverse source child slots in order. Null children and children without
   type flag `0x40` are skipped, including their descendants.
5. Recursively clone eligible children and attach each nonnull result using
   the recovered ordered link path with position `UINT32_MAX`.

Camera flag `0x8000` takes precedence, followed by the original derived
dispatch order. Known LOD flag `0x80` precedes plain TRS flag `0x40`. A plain
root without `0x40` returns null. Light flag `0x2000` now selects the
[recovered Light wrapper](SCENE_LIGHT_RECOVERY.md), before reference/LOD/TRS
dispatch. The Shape and reference/resource clone branches remain unsupported and reject where encountered; they are not
reinterpreted as generic transforms. A completed prefix remains available.

The cloned hierarchy retains local transforms, source names, supported
properties, independent attributes and the Camera/LOD copy behavior already
recovered. The clone's root remains detached, while children attach beneath
the copied parents. The original source tree is not reparented. LOD requests
from copy and attachment reach the recovered registry/world-position update.

The `constructed` callback must retain every completed allocation and add it
to supported owned transport before copy services run. Failures can leave
registered objects, remap entries, list entries and partial links. `result`
retains a root allocation when one exists; `unfinished` identifies a record at
failure and may alias it or an existing map/list entry. These are references
to one allocation, not independent ownership. Callers release all retained
prefixes using known lifecycle dispatch, without double destruction.

## Evidence and limits

The private Windows oracle maps the pinned original image and executes its
unchanged code, with explicit platform/private-heap/locale seams. It does not
run the game entry point or modify a live game. Comparisons pass for:

- 5,490 complete candidate records and successive remap states, including
  5,250 insertions, 240 duplicate insertions and 120 complete lifetimes;
- 3,000 complete clone-vector states: 1,000 reserves and 2,000 grow/appends;
- 628 source XML begin callbacks followed by 564 recursively cloned nodes;
- 99 complete scene lifetimes, 297 successive forest states and 3,873 node records;
- 99 duplicate-root no-ops and 564 original lookups on reconstructed remaps;
- 72 post-copy LOD updates and 99 complete LOD-manager allocation comparisons;
- 63 complete original subtrees: 20 from Krone Swadro, 19 from Map01 and 24
  from Map02. Original attributes, transforms and hierarchy are retained.

No unsupported child is removed or reparented to fabricate an original map
fixture. Synthetic mixed TRS/Camera/LOD trees separately test the native
excluded-child filter. All compared node/property/attribute bytes, names,
child-vector allocations and clone-list allocations are checked. Pointer
identities are normalized; transform/platform-libm tolerance is `1e-5`.
Pending trigger metadata, if encountered, is deactivated only for bounded
teardown after copy comparisons; active trigger/backend teardown is not proven.

The asset-free portable test covers remap reuse/duplicates, copied hierarchy
and world positions, excluded subtrees, stopping at unsupported derived
dispatch and cleanup across 55 allocation-failure attempts. Bounds, validation,
failure cleanup and owned callback transport are authored. Current limits are
65,535 traversal calls, depth 256 and 1,048,576 remap/vector slots. Repeated
validation/staging is a bounded correctness transport, not a validated strategy
for loading the entire original maps in one allocation/view.

```

## Recovered entries

| Native entry | Bounded reconstructed behavior |
|---|---|
| `0x14018c1a0` | Named TransformGroup/LOD construction, common attributes, append attachment and current-node update |
| `0x14018c370` | Pop current to its parent and return for non-shape nodes |
| `0x1400266d0` | Append parsed scalar segments to the dynamic `lodDistance` float vector |
| `0x140028150` | Grow a four-byte-element vector by the native 1.5x capacity rule |
| `0x1400281d0` | Reserve four-byte-element storage, copy used elements and release old storage |

The original code retains the first attribute-name pointer in `RDX` while its
name search advances `RCX`. Instruction inspection confirms that the subsequent
lodDistance search restarts at attribute zero. A decompiled loop representation
was ambiguous here; a lodDistance attribute preceding name is explicitly tested.

## Callback and numeric behavior

The first exact matching name wins. An absent or null first name returns without
allocation or current-node change, even when a later duplicate has a value.
The first exact lodDistance also wins; null keeps a plain TRS node, while an empty
nonnull value still selects a LOD object with its constructor defaults.

Common attributes run before attachment with the original physics, source-ID
registration and joint switches enabled. The parent receives the child at
`UINT32_MAX` append position. Current changes only after that call completes.
End always pops the current node; it does not maintain an authored parallel stack
that silently repairs a preceding ignored begin callback.

The dynamic float parser appends a scalar for every ASCII-space delimiter and
one final scalar. Repeated/leading/trailing spaces retain native duplication and
empty-value behavior. For example, `0  10 100` yields `(0,10,10,100)`, which the LOD
constructor retains. A direct parser call with scan length zero appends its final
scalar; the group callback skips that call for an empty lodDistance string.
The scalar grammar is the previously recovered native numeric grammar.

The four-byte vector preserves native capacity, spare bytes and prefix appends.
The scalar/count/finite/work guards are authored and exclude undefined inputs.
Raw allocation exception and native stack-alias corner cases are not claimed.

## Ownership and authored services

`FS15SceneGroupServices` transports decoded attributes and uses known recovered
scene services. A constructed-node callback adds each completed allocation to the
host's owned view before common attributes need it. A link callback invokes the
recovered hierarchy path. These services and the exposed result structure are
authored interfaces, not a recovered complete loader object.

After construction succeeds, the result transfers ownership of that node even
if common attributes or a later callback fails. Source-ID registration and a
partially performed link are not rolled back. Callers must retain and release
that prefix with its known lifetime path. Failed constructors release their
acquired members before the raw record is freed. Callbacks cannot throw/reenter.

The non-shape end path is recovered. When type flag `0x800` identifies a shape,
the API performs the original parent pop and reports the remaining branch as
unsupported without reading derived `+0x190` renderer state. Native render-resource
finalization, scheduling and the rest of that branch are still open.

The new owned matrix adapter calls the recovered matrix/TRS setter; inspected
LOD tables inherit that same TRS setter. Together with recovered cache refresh
and state propagation it connects animation playback to callback-created nodes.

# Recovered scene attachment and removal

Three GE6 hierarchy entries now have bounded portable C++ paths:

|---|---|

threshold. It excludes affine padding. Reparenting retains local coordinates;
the child's world pose follows its new ancestor chain.

## Portable boundary and provenance

`fs15_scene_link` and `fs15_scene_unlink` extend `scene_state.h` using its partial
native node layout and known base/TRS dispatch. Caller-owned writable child
storage must match the arena's child view. Each node reserves a disjoint span
through its observed begin/end/capacity pointers.

The native control flow, masks, ordering and identity test are recovered.
Temporary storage, bounds/forest checks, atomic commit and notification
transport are authored. Standard C++ rotation/copy operations implement the
observed pointer-vector effects; the original CRT/container helpers are not
claimed as recovered functions.

**Native vector allocation/growth is not implemented.** Exhausted child or event
capacity rejects without changing nodes, child storage, events or the returned
insertion index. The event-count output may report the required capacity.
Malformed pointers, overlapping reserved vectors, inconsistent links, duplicate
children, cycles and hierarchies deeper than 256 nodes are rejected by authored
guards. Outputs must not overlap the supplied input views.

These APIs do not allocate or destroy objects. They recover scene membership
changes relevant to lifecycle, not constructors, destructors, reference counting,
global registries, object naming or resource ownership. Arbitrary derived
vtables and observer callbacks that mutate the scene remain unresolved.
ReFarm still uses authored scene ownership; the new hierarchy component is
validated independently and is not substituted for a complete GE6 lifecycle.

  removals. Cases include 7,335 reparentings, 2,602 root attachments and 1,217
  same-parent reorderings.

| `0x14010fa90`, `0x14010fb40` | Default-class and caller-typed TRS constructors |
| `0x1400b1710` | Matrix property release, empty attribute-map cleanup and observer storage release |
| `0x1401362a0` | Detach from parent, delete ordered children, free child storage, unregister and release name |
| `0x14010fbb0` | TRS destruction when no active-trigger teardown is required |
| `0x1400b5f90`, `0x1400b16e0`, `0x14010fb10` | Node/matrix/TRS deleting wrappers, including the low-bit delete flag |

## Recovered layout and ordering

`scene_state.h` now names the registration byte, name pointer, identifier, class
tag, attribute-map header/count and shared-resource pointer at their observed
offsets. Other bytes remain opaque. The default TRS constructor forces class tag
`0x1d`; the typed constructor retains its argument. Registration occurs before
the final class tag and derived type flags are written.

Matrix defaults include a local identity, dirty-world flag `0x40`, clip interval
`[1000000, 0]`, masks `0xffff`/`0xffffffff` and a separate property allocation.
The cached world matrix remains uninitialized until its lazy update; the
reconstruction preserves those bytes. TRS caches start at translation/rotation
zero and scale one. Empty construction names remain null; an empty rename
allocates one byte. Self-aliasing rename input is rejected before freeing.

Destruction changes dispatch identity as each base is reached. In particular,
after entering hierarchy-base destruction, child detach uses the raw hierarchy
operation rather than the live matrix-node propagation path. Children are
deleted from the front in original order, with descendants removed before their
parent. The parent detach requests suppression. The node's child-vector storage,
name and registration are released after its children.

## Recovered code versus authored services

`scene_lifecycle.cpp` contains recovered initialization/lifetime flow.
`FS15SceneLifecycleServices` supplies allocation/free, synchronized ID generation,
registry insertion/removal and known unlink/deleting-dispatch callbacks. Those
platform/container services are **authored integration boundaries**, not
recovered CRT heaps, Windows critical sections or native red-black-tree bodies.
The low-level API expects valid owned member pointers and correctly dispatched
known object kinds. It is not an untrusted-memory parser.

Observed vtable addresses are stored as stable identity tokens. They are never
called as original C++ function pointers by the portable library. The native
reference separately executes the actual observed vtables. ReFarm retains its
authored object ownership; these lifecycle paths are not yet integrated into a
fully recovered scene loader, physics world or complete engine startup.

Supported destruction now accepts valid nonempty maps through the
[recovered attribute component](SCENE_ATTRIBUTES_RECOVERY.md), while requiring
default property type, a supported shared-reference dispatcher and no active-trigger teardown. Per-object checks reject
those unsupported states before freeing that object's members. The owning host
must preflight descendants and supply correct callbacks. A callback failure
after teardown starts cannot undo external frees or registry changes.

Allocation-failure cleanup and bounded-input rejection are authored behavior.
The ID may already have advanced and a failed construction record may be
partially initialized; it must not be destructed. Original C++ exception/unwind
paths, arbitrary derived classes, shared-resource reference
counting, triggers, singleton startup and concurrent registry semantics remain
open. Full native allocation/ownership recovery is therefore still incomplete.

- **7,500 renames**, **3,500 auxiliary allocation comparisons** and **4,970

# Native Light recovery and derived scene dispatch

Nine additional bounded native paths now compile in the portable C++17 core.
They recover Light records, cone/dirty state, decoded I3D loading, pending-only
lifetime and clone dispatch. The scene walker now distinguishes Light virtual
behavior from ordinary TRS behavior. This does not implement spatial light
registration, render/GPU resources or the original deferred-update consumer.
The later [spatial component](SCENE_SPATIAL_RECOVERY.md) now recovers grid
registration/removal, active destruction and LOD/Light pending consumption;
the narrower fixture described here remains independently reproducible.

| Entry | Recovered path |
|---|---|
| `0x1400d9bc0` | Construct the `0x200`-byte Light record |
| `0x1400d9de0` | Deleting/nondeleting destructor wrapper |
| `0x1400d9e10` | Pending removal and inherited lifetime, without active spatial/GPU ownership |
| `0x1400d9f30` | Light clone wrapper followed by common node copy |
| `0x1400da110` | Base scene traversal followed by Light-specific dirty/queue effects |
| `0x1400da1b0` | Cached inherited LOD token and recursive marker override |
| `0x1400da210` | Cone factors, drop-off clamp, dirty flags and queue request |
| `0x140087cf0` | Append the Light to its manager's pending pointer vector |
| `0x14018c770` | Decoded I3D Light begin callback |

Constructors, common XML attributes, TRS/state propagation, supported property
copying, pointer-vector allocation, LOD services and recursive remap/clone
storage are reused. They are not counted twice. See
[source-pinned evidence](../analysis/scene-light-validation.json).

## Recovered record and metadata

The Light uses typed TRS class `0x17`, type flags `0x2072` and identity table
`0x1404c1d98`. The eight inspected slots inherit ordinary link/unlink, observer
rescan, inherited LOD lookup and TRS matrix assignment. State and marker slots
are Light-specific, as is the deleting wrapper. Across five observed scene
tables, 40 slots resolve to 17 distinct targets; the five earlier discovery
records remain retained and this audit creates no new functions.

| Offset | Observed field |
|---|---|
| `+0x170` | Spatial packed token, untouched by construction; identified by later grid recovery |
| `+0x174` | Type: directional `0`, point `1`, spot `2` |
| `+0x178/+0x184` | Diffuse/specular colors, three floats each |
| `+0x190/+0x194/+0x198` | Range, drop-off and cone angle in degrees |
| `+0x19c/+0x1a0` | Outer/inner cone cosine factors |
| `+0x1a4..1b0` | Depth-map bias, slope bias/clamp and resolution |
| `+0x1b4..1c4` | Shadow far/extrusion distances, perspective parameter, splits and split parameter |
| `+0x1c8/+0x1cc` | Decay and affected-light masks |
| `+0x1d0/+0x1d4` | Light option flags and cached LOD token |
| `+0x1d8..1f0` | Sphere subobject table, opaque word, center and float radius; named by later spatial recovery |
| `+0x1f4/+0x1f8` | Opaque word and render-resource pointer |

The constructor leaves opaque bytes untouched, initializes spatial links and
render resources to null, replaces decay zero with one and initializes masks
and LOD token to `0xffffffff`. Shadow splits clamp to `1..4` for directional
lights and become one for other types. Option bits preserve diffuse/specular,
shadow-map and perspective arguments in their native positions.

Cone calculation retains float operation order:
`angle = ((coneAngle * 0.5f) * piFloat) / 180.0f`.
It stores `cos(angle)`, clamps drop-off to `0..5`, then stores
`cos(angle - (angle / 5) * dropOff)`. Negative zero is retained by the clamp.
The math backend is the platform float cosine, not a recovery of the original
CRT trigonometric implementation. Finite-input guards are authored additions.

## Virtual updates, queues and ownership

After base traversal, the Light state override uses the **original input mask**,
including bits suppressed by base propagation. Mask `0xc` sets dirty bit
`0x400`; bit `4` also invalidates the cached LOD token. Mask `3` sets `0x500`.
A visible or already registered Light requests a pending update only when its
`0x800` queued bit is clear. The marker override updates a changed cached token,
sets `0x400` and requests the update before invoking the base recursive marker.

The new authored `scene_derived.h` transport supports matrix/TRS/LOD/Light
dispatch. It stages Light token fields separately from base records and emits
separate LOD and Light queue requests in each manager's original order. Queue
capacity and node/token changes are checked before commit. The previous APIs
retain their original supported-kind boundary; callers opt into derived
transport explicitly. World/matrix transport accepts the inherited Light paths.
Marker traversal for LOD registration and teardown does not inspect already
dying ancestors or property objects.

The Light context represents only the observed pending vector, not the complete
native manager. Original pending storage is at `manager + 0xe8`; the oracle maps
that subview explicitly. The constructor starts hidden and normally does not
append. Loading/attachment, inherited visibility and later transforms trigger
the recovered queue behavior.

Pending-only destruction removes the first matching pending entry using a
swap with the last entry. Native queued flag/spare-slot bytes are retained.
It changes the spatial subobject's table, then runs inherited TRS cleanup.
Active spatial registration or render resources reject before that path;
those resource lifetimes remain open. Callback/allocation failures can retain
native-order prefixes, and completed allocations remain caller-owned.

## XML and clone details

Attribute searches retain the first exact-name match from attribute zero.
Missing/null first `name` ignores the begin callback. Light type values and
boolean `true` checks are case-insensitive; a nonnull boolean value other than
`true` is false. Diffuse/specular default to `(1,1,1)`, with emission enabled.
Shadow-map casting defaults false. Range defaults one, decay two, cone angle
60 and drop-off four. Cone/drop attributes apply only to spot lights.

Shadow settings parse only when shadow-map casting is enabled. Defaults are
depth bias/slope bias `0.005`, slope clamp `0.02`, resolution `512`, far distance
`80`, extrusion distance `200`, perspective parameter `5`, one split and split
parameter `0.4`. Color triples use native scalar-cursor-plus-one parsing.
Decay/split counts use unsigned digit-prefix accumulation with wrapping.
Depth resolution uses the original signed-decimal CRT seam; affected masks use
the original unsigned CRT seam with base zero, including its overflow behavior.
These CRT services are not newly recovered parsers.

The callback constructs and retains the Light, reads affected masks, applies
common attributes with physics `0`, source IDs `1`, joint `0`, then appends it
to the current parent. Other physics/joint attributes therefore do not create
those property types on a Light. End uses the existing non-shape callback.

Light cloning copies constructor parameters, then copies the source option
flags and runs the recovered common node copy. Affected masks reset to the
constructor default rather than copying the source mask. Recursive clone
dispatch now accepts Light at its original priority between Shape and reference
resources. The copied subtree uses real Light state/queue behavior; it is not
reinterpreted as a TRS-only placeholder.

# LOD registration, distance selection and scene dispatch

The portable core now reconstructs the known GE6 LOD node's metadata,
registration and removal, camera-distance cache, child branch tokens, dirty
updates and supported destructor chain. These paths run in mixed owned LOD/TRS
hierarchies. They do not constitute the complete spatial culler or renderer.

## Native paths

| Entry | Reconstructed bounded behavior |
|---|---|
| `0x1400d7a70` | Construct the `0x188`-byte LOD node over the recovered TRS constructor |
| `0x1400d7be0`, `0x1400d7bb0` | Remove pending/registered state and execute the known destructor/deleting chain |
| `0x1400d7620` | Append a `0x28`-byte registry entry, with allocation blocks of 1024 entries |
| `0x1400d7840` | Swap-remove a registry entry and update the moved owner's index |
| `0x1400d78f0` | Update world position/distances and invalidate the cached selection |
| `0x1400d60b0` | Stamp-cached squared-distance level selection |
| `0x1400d7d50` | Base scene propagation followed by LOD dirty marking and pending scheduling |
| `0x1400d7e20` | Set the group index and dispatch packed branch tokens to children |
| `0x1400d7ea0` | Dirty world-position refresh, visible-group registration/move and hidden-group removal |
| `0x1400d7db0` | Direct-child LOD token lookup, or inherited lookup for a null child argument |
| `0x1400b6260` | Inherited lookup through known matrix/TRS/LOD parents |
| `0x140087e50` | Append the LOD pending-update request through recovered pointer-vector allocation |

The LOD constructor explicitly references table `0x1404c1c48`. Auditing its eight
slots found `0x1400d7db0` as executable code without a catalogue function.
Discovery created that function without splitting an existing body. Across the
five inspected scene tables including [Camera](SCENE_CAMERA_RECOVERY.md)
and [Light](SCENE_LIGHT_RECOVERY.md), 40 slots now resolve to 17 distinct targets; five
functions were discovered through those explicit slots. All have local
pseudocode exports. The catalogue now contains 12,201 entries and 11,636 eligible
exports. This bounded audit is not exhaustive engine class discovery.

The discovery script now retains earlier verified creation records when an
audit is extended, rather than losing their provenance when targets already
exist. See [aggregate vtable evidence](../analysis/scene-vtables-summary.json).

## Preserved details

- Fewer than two constructor distances produce `(0,100,100,100)`. Otherwise
  up to four supplied values are copied and the last value fills remaining lanes.
- The initial group index is `0x3fffffff`. A valid child token combines the group
  index with the child's ordinal in the upper two bits. An unregistered group or
  an absent direct child returns `0xffffffff`. Known inherited lookup stops at
  the first LOD parent, retaining that invalid-index behavior.
- Registry rows hold position, four squared distances, a level count, selected
  byte and 16-bit cache stamp. Unused distance lanes stay opaque. Growth copies
  used rows; removal retains the unused trailing row and updates the moved owner.
- The camera epoch is a 32-bit field, but row invalidation compares only its low
  16 bits. Changing a viewer position without changing those bits retains the
  cached selection. Exact distance equality selects the next level.
- The first distance lane is not a transition threshold. Selection starts with
  lane one and compares squared distance against the squared camera factor times
  the stored squared threshold. Floating-point addition order follows inspected
  instructions: `z*z + (x*x + y*y)`.
- LOD dirty scheduling uses the original input mask, even if base propagation
  suppresses every bit. Derived post-processing runs after base traversal, so
  descendant LOD requests precede their ancestor's request. A queued bit prevents
  duplicate scheduling until the update clears it.
- Hiding unregisters the group and directly restores its invalid index. Deleting
  a pending group removes its first pending occurrence by swapping the last
  pointer into that slot, matching the native lifetime path.

## Authored boundaries

The reconstructed C++ retains native record offsets and opaque bytes. Native
vtable addresses are identity tokens and are never executed by portable code.
The context combines observed manager/pending views; its aggregate layout and
initialization are authored rather than a recovered complete global singleton.

`scene_state_lod` and the corresponding TRS/link/unlink variants accept LOD kind
two. The existing APIs retain their matrix/TRS dispatch contract. Their staged
queue output and the owned scatter transport are authored interfaces that retain
native request order; callers append successful requests to the LOD context.
Observer notifications remain side-effect-free outputs. Reentrant observer or
allocator side effects are outside the comparison scope.

World position and inherited child marking use the recovered world-transform
and inherited-state paths through explicit services. A known-subtree marker can
also run while the rest of a forest is being destroyed, without inspecting freed
parent properties. Allocator, registry and supported destructor dispatch services
remain authored platform seams.

Finite/bounds/cycle checks exclude malformed storage and undefined numeric
inputs. The registry limit is 64,512 entries, before native uint16 block-capacity
overflow. Staged node/queue capacity failures preserve live nodes; callback or
allocation failures in the direct native-order functions can retain a mutation
prefix. Their guards do not claim native exception semantics.

```md
# Owned child vectors and allocated scene hierarchies

Recovered scene operations can now work on individually allocated objects and
their independently owned property, child and observer buffers. Previously the
portable hierarchy component required a contiguous synthetic arena and fixed
child-vector capacity. This removes that transport constraint before recovering
the I3D node-construction callbacks.

## Recovered code and authored transport

Three additional native entries are reconstructed in portable C++:

| Entry | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `0x1400d5f30` | Reserve a larger pointer vector, copy used elements, free old storage and preserve its length |
| `0x1400d34e0` | Ensure one spare pointer slot, growing by `max(count+1, capacity+capacity/2)` |
| `0x14005a1b0` | Append an external or in-vector aliased pointer value, rereading an aliased element after relocation |

The native growth sequence starts `1,2,3,4,6,9,13`. A reserve copies used elements;
new unused bytes remain supplied by the allocator. Removal retains capacity and
its trailing pointer residue. Same-parent reordering removes the old membership
first, so a full vector does not need to grow for that operation.

`FS15SceneOwnedView` and its scatter/gather staging are **authored transport**.
They do not count as additional recovered GE6 functions. They adapt separately
allocated native-layout records into the existing recovered state/TRS/hierarchy
operations and commit changes back to their original owners. Parent/child
identities and property views are remapped; observer identities, opaque fields,
unchanged unused slots and unrelated ownership pointers are preserved.

Ordered link/reparent/unlink uses the already recovered `0x1401363d0`,
`0x1400b17b0` and `0x1400b19c0` behavior. Those entries are not counted again.
Child-vector growth now uses the recovered capacity/allocation rules. A service
allocator supplies the platform heap; its implementation remains authored.

## API scope and failure behavior

The view must describe a complete valid forest of supported matrix/TRS records,
with every object listed once. Default properties and detached body/joint
metadata are valid first-16-byte property views. The original interfaces retain this matrix/TRS contract. New
[LOD-aware variants](SCENE_LOD_RECOVERY.md) accept known LOD records with ordered
pending-request output; other derived dispatch remains excluded.

Bounds currently allow 65,535 nodes, 1,048,576 total child/observer slots and
256 levels. Pointee storage and complete vector allocations must be valid.
Staging copies the supplied forest and allocated child slots for each call; it
is a bounded validation transport, not a proven full-map loading strategy. The
complete original maps exceed its current node bound.

Output buffers must be disjoint. Bounds, cycle checks and transactional staging
are authored guards: insufficient event capacity, invalid views and allocation
failure leave the live forest unchanged. Native exception/prefix-write behavior
is not claimed for those rejected cases. Callbacks cannot throw or reenter.

Notifications retain original node indices, observer identities, order and
origin. They are returned for caller delivery. Real observer side effects and
reentrancy are not simulated. Recursive destruction still uses the recovered
object lifetime chain and known dispatch services; it is distinct from staging
a hierarchy operation.

- 120 complete separately allocated forest lifetimes;
- 10,800 successive forest states and 179,100 complete node-record comparisons;

  1,800 removals, 1,800 state updates and 1,800 TRS rebuilds;
- 2,989 ordered side-effect-free observer notifications;
- common XML attributes applied through recovered services to actual allocated
  records, including detached body/joint properties;
- recursive destruction with every owned buffer and object registration released.

The original constructor, allocator/container, hierarchy, state and destructor
code executes unchanged in a private-heap reference process. XML decoding,
platform initialization and portable registry/dispatch services remain authored.
No game entry point or live game is touched. All supported record bytes and
complete child allocation contents are compared after address normalization;
TRS/libm regions use scaled tolerance `1e-5` across successive operations.
